recent_facts.fact: The most recent independent general-election polls had Democrat Rob Sand ahead of Republican Zach Lahn. NYT/Siena (Sep 22–Oct 1): Sand 52%, Lahn 41%. Fox News (Sep 24–28): Sand 53%, Lahn 44%.
A Marist poll of 1,050 Iowa registered voters taken Sep 17–20, 2026 had Sand at 54% and Lahn at 42%.

Other September polls also had Sand ahead. YouGov (Sep 3–8): 51–41. Emerson (Aug 31–Sep 1): 49–46. Cygnal (Sep 9–11, 500 likely voters): about 48–44.4. Rasmussen (Sep 8–10, 1,031 likely voters): 50–39. The Republican-aligned firm co/efficient (Sep 14–16, 831 likely voters): 46–42.

Zach Lahn, a businessman and farmer, won the June 2 Republican primary and U.S. Rep. Randy Feenstra conceded. Rob Sand was unopposed for the Democratic nomination. Gov. Kim Reynolds is not running again, so the seat is open.
Three candidates are on the November 3, 2026 general election ballot: Rob Sand (D), Zach Lahn (R) and Libertarian Nicholas Gluba.

The first gubernatorial debate was held Oct 6, 2026 at St. Ambrose University in Davenport. Sand raised Lahn's Kansas residency, saying Iowa needs a 'full-time Iowan' as governor. Lahn criticized data centers and focused on agriculture.
Four debates are scheduled before Election Day on November 3, 2026, and the first took place Oct 6.
Sand is campaigning for support beyond the Democratic base. The polling coverage cited above credits much of his lead to independent voters.

In 2024 the final Des Moines Register/Selzer Iowa Poll had Harris ahead by 3 points, but Trump won Iowa by about 13.2 points. That was a miss of more than 16 points in the Republican direction. The Register's Iowa Poll has since been discontinued.

In 2020, Sen. Joni Ernst trailed by just under 3 points on average across 19 tracked polls, then won by 6.6 points. Trump led Iowa's final five polls by about 2 points on average and won by 8.5. Polls also underestimated Ernst in 2014.
Trump has won Iowa three times, most recently by 13+ points in 2024. From memory and unverified here: Republicans have won the last four Iowa governor races (2010, 2014, 2018, 2022).

The question resolves when AP, Fox News and NBC all call the race for the same candidate. If they don't, it resolves on official certification. The Republican option is whoever is the GOP nominee, currently Zach Lahn.

recent_facts.fact: As of Oct 4, 2026, an average of six polling aggregators showed Republican Gov. Greg Abbott at 48.5% and Democrat Gina Hinojosa at 46.7%, so Abbott was ahead by 1.8 points.
YouGov (Sept 28–Oct 5, 3,625 likely voters, ±3.0) had Hinojosa 48% and Abbott 47%. NYT/Siena (Sept 22–Oct 1, 615 likely voters) had Hinojosa 49% and Abbott 46%.

recent_facts.source: Wikipedia (polls listed: Beacon Research/Shaw & Co., Stratus Intelligence)
recent_facts.fact: Beacon Research/Shaw & Co. (Sept 24–28, 1,005 likely voters) had Abbott 52% and Hinojosa 47%. Stratus Intelligence (Sept 22–24, 865 likely voters) had Abbott 50% and Hinojosa 45%. Texas Public Opinion Research (Aug 21–24) had Abbott 49% and Hinojosa 42%.

A ReconMR/Siena poll from Sept 18 had Hinojosa ahead 49–45. The same firm had Abbott up by 1 in July, so that is a 5-point swing. A late-September Marist poll had Hinojosa ahead 49–46. Abbott launched a $12M ad accusing Hinojosa of voting 40 times to raise taxes, and data centers have become a major issue in rural counties.

No debate between Abbott and Hinojosa is scheduled. Hinojosa says she has accepted four TV debate invitations, and Abbott has not responded. Abbott did debate in each of his previous governor races (2014, 2018, 2022).
Abbott publicly downplayed the tight polls and took new steps against data centers, the issue that has become central to the race.

Abbott started 2026 with $105.7M cash on hand after raising $22.7M in the second half of 2025. Hinojosa raised $1.3M in the last 10 weeks of 2025. Abbott said he would spend most of his roughly $90M in Harris County.

In the March 3 primaries, Abbott won the Republican nomination with 81.8% (1,764,924 votes) and Hinojosa won the Democratic nomination with 58.5% (1,289,576 votes). Libertarian Pat Dixon is also on the ballot and polled at 3% in a University of Houston survey.

Early voting in Texas starts Oct 19, 2026, and Election Day is Nov 3, 2026. The question closes Nov 4 at 04:59 UTC. It resolves once AP, Fox News and NBC all call the race; if they don't all agree, it goes by official certification.

Republicans have won every Texas governor race since 1994, which is 8 in a row (1994–2022). The last Democrat to win was Ann Richards in 1990. Abbott won in 2022 by 10.9 points (54.75% to 43.86%) and in 2018 by 13.3 points.
In 2020, the final RealClearPolitics average in Texas had Trump up only 1 point. He won 52% to 46%, so polls understated his share by a little over 4 points.

In 2024, Quinnipiac, Morning Consult and Emerson showed a tied presidential race in Texas, but Trump won 56.2% to 42.4%. Cruz beat Allred 53% to 44.6%. Republicans running better than the polls in more years than these two is the desk's recollection only (unverified).

market.question: US announces end of Iranian blockade by October 15, 2026?
market.rules:
On July 13, 2026, Trump announced the United States would reinstate its naval blockade of Iran, targeting Iranian ships and customers.

This market will resolve to “Yes” if the United States government, or an authorized representative of the United States government, publicly and officially announces the end, termination, lifting, or suspension of the United States’ naval blockade on Iranian ships and ships of Iranian customers, between market creation and the specified date, 11:59 PM ET. Otherwise, this market will resolve to “No”.

An announcement qualifies if it communicates that the United States will generally cease blocking vessel traffic for Iranian ships and customers, including an announcement that the blockade will not take effect at all, even if some restrictions remain (for example, an imposition of fees). An announcement does not qualify if it reflects only a limited or partial change that stops short of a general end or suspension of the blockade, for example, an exemption for a specific vessel, cargo, or port.

A qualifying announcement must be a declarative statement of the United States government’s present termination or suspension of the blockade, previously-unannounced prior termination or suspension of the blockade, or definitive decision to terminate or suspend the blockade.

A qualifying announcement must clearly and unambiguously identify the end or suspension of the blockade. Statements that merely allude to, reference, or describe an end to the blockade, without clearly communicating it, do not qualify. The announcement need not use specific terminology or reference the end of a blockade by name; an announcement of a resumption of prior obligations, the maintenance of a status quo, or a return to a previously agreed baseline qualifies, provided the substantive policy of ending or suspending the blockade is clearly and unambiguously communicated.

A qualifying announcement must be made through official channels, by an individual acting in an official capacity. Statements made incidentally or informally in a context not intended for official communication do not qualify.

The following do not qualify:

Anonymous, unattributed, or leaked statements not confirmed as official;
Statements by persons not authorized to speak for the United States government;
Third-party speculation, analysis, or predictions that the United States government will announce or implement an end to the blockade;
Satirical, fabricated, hacked, or impersonated communications; and
Statements that describe a prospective, contingent, probable, or conditional end to the blockade rather than announcing a present and decided position.

Once a qualifying announcement is made, this market will resolve to “Yes” regardless of whether it is later reversed, or whether the blockade actually ends in practice.

Resolution will be based on official information from the United States government, including the President, the Department of Defense, the Department of State, and United States Central Command (CENTCOM), or the official representatives of the United States government.

recent_facts.fact: The US blockade of Iranian ports is still being enforced. CENTCOM has turned back 130 commercial vessels since the blockade restarted in mid-July, most recently on October 5. It says it will 'swiftly act against any vessels trying to run the blockade.'
Over the past 12 weeks, CENTCOM has disabled 3 vessels that refused orders and destroyed 13 ships it linked to blockade violations or the IRGC's 'shadow network'.

State media quoted Iranian President Pezeshkian saying 'negotiations are meaningless' with the US, because it 'breaks its commitments' and has 'attacked us three times after talks.' Iran's legal affairs minister said Iran is still reviewing the US response to Araghchi's seven-day proposal. Trump said the conflict is 'essentially almost over.'

Parliament Speaker Ghalibaf said the Strait of Hormuz stays closed until the US meets seven conditions based on the June memorandum of understanding. Iran rejected US nuclear demands and insists the blockade must be settled first. An Iranian official said the strait could reopen within seven days if the conditions are met.
Iran said it has received the official US response to its latest proposal to end the war, which has lasted about seven months. Araghchi delivered the US proposal to Tehran around September 30.

Araghchi proposed that Iran reopen Hormuz and resume nuclear talks within 7 days if the US lifts the naval blockade, waives oil sanctions and agrees to a ceasefire that includes Lebanon. Trump publicly rejected it ('It is what we would have maybe agreed to a year ago') but told Axios he expected talks to continue. (Date approximate: the weekend after the September 22 UN meeting.)

Unnamed sources said US and Iranian negotiators in New York were discussing a phased deal: Iran reopens Hormuz and the US lifts its blockade. The main obstacle is that neither side wants to give up its leverage first. A deal would mean Trump accepting another temporary fix after the earlier understanding collapsed in July.

At the UN, Araghchi met US envoys Witkoff and Kushner for three hours, the first structured face-to-face US–Iran contact of this conflict. Witkoff called the talks 'promising, constructive.' Qatar is passing messages between the two sides.
Iran loaded no crude onto tankers in September 2026, down from about 250,000 barrels per day in August. It is the first such month since the war began in February.

Precedent: the first blockade began April 13, 2026, and was lifted after Trump and Iran announced an agreement on June 14. The MOU was signed at Versailles on June 17 and CENTCOM removed the blockade on June 18, about 9 weeks after it started. The deal gave both sides 60 days to negotiate.

The June lifting held for less than a month. Trump announced the blockade's return on July 13 and enforcement began July 14. As of October 6 the second blockade has lasted about 12 weeks, with no official announcement ending it.

Only an official, declarative US government announcement of a general end or suspension of the blockade counts; exemptions for specific vessels or ports do not. Reports of talks about a phased deal from unnamed sources do not count. The deadlines are October 15 and October 31, 2026, 11:59 PM ET.

market.question: Will Benjamin Netanyahu be the next Prime Minister of Israel?
market.rules:
Legislative elections are schedule to be held in Israel on October 27, 2026. 

This market will resolve to the next individual who is officially appointed and sworn in as Prime Minister of Israel following the 2026 parliamentary election. If an election is called early, this market will immediately resolve to the individual who is officially appointed and sworn in after that election.

To count for resolution, the individual must be formally sworn in. Any interim or caretaker Prime Minister will not count toward the resolution of this market.

If no such Prime Minister is sworn in by December 31, 2027, 11:59 PM ET, this market will resolve to “Other”.

The primary resolution source for this market will be official information from the Government of Israel; however, a consensus of credible reporting may also be used.

recent_facts.source: Question resolution rules / Israeli Basic Law (via Times of Israel)
recent_facts.fact: The question resolves on whoever is formally sworn in as PM after the October 27, 2026 election. Caretaker PMs do not count, and it resolves 'Other' if nobody is sworn in by 2027-12-31. After results are certified, the president has one week to task a candidate, who gets 28 days plus a possible 14-day extension (42 days total) to form a coalition, so a swearing-in before the question closes on 2026-10-28 is effectively impossible.

After the November 1, 2022 election, Netanyahu announced he had formed a government on December 21, 2022, with a deadline of January 2. From memory (unverified): it was sworn in on December 29, 2022, about 58 days after the vote.

Unverified, from memory: of the last 7 Knesset elections (2009 to 2022), Netanyahu was sworn in after 5 (2009, 2013, 2015, 2020, 2022). Bennett was sworn in after March 2021, and the April and September 2019 elections produced no government. The election-to-swearing-in gap was about 76 days in 2020 and 82 days in 2021.

Poll average as of October 5: Likud 23, Yashar (Eisenkot) 22, B'Yachad/Together (Bennett) 11. Blocs: Netanyahu 52, Change/opposition 50, Arab parties 13, so no bloc reaches the 61 needed for a majority.

Kan poll: Yashar 23, Likud 21, B'Yachad 11, Democrats 9, Yisrael Beytenu 9, Otzma 7, RZP/Zehut 6, Joint List 7, Ra'am 5, Reservists 4, People of Israel 4. Blocs tied 52-52. Preferred PM: Netanyahu 39% vs Eisenkot 38%, and Netanyahu 42% vs Bennett 33%.
In the first poll after candidate lists were filed (Lazar Research, 506 respondents), Netanyahu's bloc was projected at 52 seats, five behind the opposition.

recent_facts.source: Search summaries of Channel 13 and Maariv polls
recent_facts.fact: Channel 13 poll: Netanyahu bloc 54 vs 52 for the Jewish opposition parties. Maariv poll: Netanyahu bloc 51 vs opposition 53.

market.question: Will there be no change in Fed interest rates after the October 2026 meeting?
market.rules:
The FED interest rates are defined in this market by the upper bound of the target federal funds range. The decisions on the target federal funds range are made by the Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) meetings.

This market will resolve to the amount of basis points the upper bound of the target federal funds rate is changed by versus the level it was prior to the Federal Reserve's October 2026 meeting.

If the target federal funds rate is changed to a level not expressed in the displayed options, the change will be rounded up to the nearest 25 and will resolve to the relevant bracket. (e.g. if there's a cut/increase of 12.5 bps it will be considered to be 25 bps)

The resolution source for this market is the FOMC’s statement after its meeting scheduled for October 27-28, 2026 according to the official calendar: https://www.federalreserve.gov/monetarypolicy/fomccalendars.htm.

The level and change of the target federal funds rate is also published at the official website of the Federal Reserve at https://www.federalreserve.gov/monetarypolicy/openmarket.htm.

This market may resolve as soon as the FOMC’s statement for their October meeting with relevant data is issued. If no statement is released by the end date of the next scheduled meeting, this market will resolve to the "No change" bracket.

recent_facts.fact: At its September 15-16, 2026 meeting the FOMC raised the federal funds target range by 25 bps to 3.75%-4.00%, its first hike since 2023. The vote was 12-0. The upper bound going into the October meeting is therefore 4.00%.

recent_facts.source: J.P. Morgan Asset Management (FOMC statement/SEP summary)
recent_facts.fact: The September 2026 dot plot's median has the fed funds rate ending 2026 at 4.1%, one more 25 bp hike this year. It shows no change in 2027 and cuts in 2028-2029. Only two FOMC meetings remain in 2026: October 27-28 and December.

In separate speeches during the week of September 28, Vice Chair Philip Jefferson and New York Fed President John Williams said the Fed has time to assess the economy before considering another rate increase. Bloomberg reported that their remarks reined in expectations of a hike this month.
August 2026 PCE prices rose 0.3% month over month and 3.4% year over year. Core PCE rose 0.2% m/m and 3.0% y/y, below the expected 3.3% y/y. The release included BEA's annual revisions.
Fed Chair Kevin Warsh described the September hike as having 'removed a dose of accommodation.' The article says he has been cryptic about his own preference for further moves.

Before the weak jobs data, several officials leaned hawkish. On September 24, NY Fed President Williams called another hike before year-end 'reasonable,' and Philadelphia Fed President Paulson said further increases may be needed. Cleveland Fed President Hammack (September 25) and Governor Cook (September 28, citing AI-driven inflation pressure) raised inflation concerns.

CNBC reported that the September jobs report followed a softer-than-expected inflation report and that the weaker labor data could shift how the Fed balances its dual mandate. The article says inflation has been above target for five years.
The September 2026 CPI is due at 8:30 a.m. ET on October 14, 2026. It is the main inflation release still to come before the October 27-28 FOMC meeting.

recent_facts.source: Federal Reserve FOMC calendar (per question rules)
recent_facts.fact: The question resolves from the FOMC statement issued after the October 27-28, 2026 meeting, comparing the new upper bound with the current 4.00%. If no statement is released, it resolves to 'No change.' A move of less than 25 bps is rounded up to 25 bps.
Chase reported that core PCE inflation had run above 3% in every month of 2026 before the September hike. The FOMC statement also cited 'geopolitical developments.'

August was revised down from 162,000 to 133,000 and July from a gain to a loss of 10,000, for a combined downward revision of 60,000.

In the case of a delay in data caused by a federal government shutdown impacting the reliability of the Source Agency, the market’s latest Expiration Date will be extended to the sooner of the release of the Underlying or six months after the end of the government shutdown.

recent_facts.fact: BLS seasonally adjusted core CPI (all items less food and energy) rose 0.3% month over month in August 2026. The 12-month core rate was 2.4%, the lowest since March 2021.

Monthly core CPI changes in 2026: Jan 0.2%, Feb 0.2%, Mar 0.4%, Apr 0.2%, May 0.0%, Jun 0.2%, Jul 0.2%, Aug 0.3%. That is 7 of 8 months above 0.1% and 1 of 8 (May) at 0.1% or lower. This comes from one secondary source and was not checked against BLS directly.
The September 2026 CPI report is scheduled for release on October 14, 2026 at 8:30 a.m. ET, before the Fed's October 27–28 meeting.

Congress passed a continuing resolution (House vote 370–48) funding the federal government through December 11, 2026, and President Trump signed it on September 3. This averted an October 1 shutdown, so no shutdown delay to the BLS release is in place.

In August 2026, shelter rose 0.3% after two straight monthly gains of 0.1% (June and July). Used vehicles rose 0.4% month over month, transportation services rose 0.5%, and medical care services fell 0.2%.
August 2026 headline CPI rose 0.4% month over month (3.4% year over year). Gasoline rose 3.9% and accounted for over a third of the increase. Core's 0.3% came in above the 0.2% consensus.

The mid-September 2026 Manheim Used Vehicle Value Index fell 1.0% from August to 206.2 and was down 0.4% year over year, the first time in 2026 that wholesale used-vehicle prices fell below year-ago levels. Unadjusted wholesale prices fell 1.1% from August.

The question resolves on the one-decimal seasonally adjusted monthly percent change in CPI-U all items less food and energy as published by BLS. A reported 0.2% or higher resolves Yes; 0.1% or lower resolves No.

During the October 1–November 12, 2025 shutdown, BLS delayed the September 2025 CPI from October 15 to October 24 and canceled the October 2025 CPI. This is the only recent case of a shutdown disrupting a CPI release, and no shutdown is in effect for October 2026.

A "military encounter" is defined as any incident involving the use of force such as missile strikes, artillery fire, exchange of gunfire, or other forms of direct military engagement between NATO and Russian military forces. Non-violent actions, such as airspace violations, firing of warning shots (such as the June, 2021 Black Sea Confrontations between Russian forces and HMS Defender), or cyberattacks will not qualify.

Military contractors will qualify only if confirmed to be operating under the direct command or coordination of the respective state’s armed forces (e.g. the Battle of Khasham would not qualify).

This market will resolve to "Yes" if, at any point after market creation and during a trading session of October 2026, any Pyth 1-minute candle for the Active Month of ICE Futures Europe WTI Crude Futures (denoted by Pyth as "CLL") has a final "High" or "Low" price equal to or beyond (above for ↑ High Prices, below for ↓ Low Prices) the listed price. Otherwise, this market will resolve to "No".

Prices will be used exactly as published by Pyth, without rounding.

Only prices achieved during an applicable trading session of the specified timeframe's business days will be considered (See: "Trading Hours" at https://www.ice.com/products/213/WTI-Crude-Futures). The trading session for a given business day typically begins at 8:00 PM ET on the prior calendar date, except for the session dated Monday, which begins at 6:00 PM ET on the preceding Sunday, and where modified by holiday or other special hours (See: https://www.ice.com/holiday-hours).

The Active Month is the nearest listed contract, except during that contract's final three trading sessions. At the open of the third-to-last trading session, the next listed contract becomes the Active Month.

Each contract's last trading day will be determined by ICE Futures Europe per the WTI Crude Futures contract specification (generally the 4th US business day prior to the 25th calendar day of the month preceding the contract month, or five US business days prior if the 25th calendar day is not a US business day). The last trading day for each contract is posted at https://www.ice.com/products/213/WTI-Crude-Futures/expiry.

For example, if the last trading session for the nearest listed contract is the session for Monday the 20th, the next listed contract would become the Active Month at the start of the trading session for Thursday the 16th (8:00 PM ET on Wednesday), assuming a standard trading calendar.

If the relevant Pyth data is unavailable due to a system outage, data failure, or other disruption that prevents verification of the required 1-minute candle data, the official daily high/low price published for the Active Month WTI Crude Oil Futures contract by ICE Futures Europe may be used to determine whether the listed price was reached during the applicable trading session (See: https://www.ice.com/report/10 with "T-West Texas Intermediate Light Sweet Crude Future" selected).

In the event of a contract specification change, feed change, or similar structural modification affecting the underlying market during the listed time frame, this market will resolve based on adjusted prices as displayed on Pyth.

If the Active Month contract does not trade at all during the listed time frame, this market will resolve to "No".

The resolution source for this market is Pyth — specifically, the ICE Futures Europe WTI Crude Futures Active Month "High" and "Low" prices available at https://app.pyth.com/explore?search=CLL, with the chart settings configured for 1-minute candles. Historical 1-minute candles may be accessed by appending a Unix timestamp (seconds) to the Pyth chart URL using the "t=" parameter.

recent_facts.fact: On October 6, 2026 WTI crude was quoted at $89.37/bbl, down 1.93% from the prior close, and Brent at $100.45. To reach $105, WTI would need to rise about 17.5% from this level.
On October 5, 2026 WTI traded at $90.62/bbl and Brent at $102.30. Brent had dipped to about $101.59 earlier in the session.

Oil fell after shipping data showed Middle East crude exports above pre-war levels on 4 of the 7 days in the last week of September. G7 nations also plan to release about 100 million barrels of crude and diesel from emergency reserves.

Physical supply stayed tight. Crude exports through Hormuz were 33.7 million barrels for the week, roughly unchanged, and freight from the Gulf to Asia on very large crude carriers (VLCCs) added about $20/bbl. Possible US diesel export restrictions were also affecting WTI's discount to Brent.

Earlier in 2026, during the Iran war, WTI went above $105. The June WTI contract settled at $105.88 in one session, and WTI reached an intraday high of $110.93. Brent peaked at $114.70 in April. (Unverified: the exact dates of these peaks were not confirmed.)

In mid-September an attack on a Saudi pipeline briefly disrupted supply. Prices then fell on reports that Saudi Arabia would offer more crude through Hormuz. This shows how sharply prices have swung in both directions on headlines.

The November 2026 WTI contract (CLX26) expires around October 20, 2026, and the December contract (CLZ26) has a last trade date of November 20, 2026. Under the active-month rule, the December contract would become the Active Month about three sessions before the November contract expires, around October 16. Check ICE's own expiry page for the exact dates.

Iran's supreme national security council head said the Strait of Hormuz will stay shut until the US meets six conditions, including ending the war against Iran and its allies. No completed US-Iran deal to reopen the strait was reported in the sources reviewed as of early October.

market.question: Sense and Sensibility Rotten Tomatoes score? (Above 85)
market.rules:
If Sense and Sensibility has a Tomatometer score of above 85 on Oct 19, 2026 at 10:00 AM ET, then the market resolves to Yes.
The "Fresh!" and "Certified Fresh!" subtitles are meant for illustrative purposes only. The Tomatometer score must be above the strike value to resolve as YES (for example, a score of 75 would resolve "Above 75" as No.) The market will be determined the Monday after wide release at 10:00 AM ET.

This market and these products have not been endorsed by Rotten Tomatoes. Any references to Rotten Tomatoes or any associated marks are descriptive only and do not indicate an endorsement of this product or any affiliation between Rotten Tomatoes and Kalshi.

recent_facts.fact: The resolution page for Sense and Sensibility (2026) shows a 79% Tomatometer from 38 reviews, which works out to about 30 fresh and 8 rotten. It has fewer than 50 verified audience ratings, so there is no Popcornmeter score yet.

Wide US theatrical release is October 16, 2026, so the check time is Monday, October 19 at 10:00 AM ET. The film is rated PG and runs 2 hours 12 minutes. Many more reviews are likely to be added around release week.

The film debuted at 80% on Rotten Tomatoes from 10 reviews after its world premiere in London on September 15, 2026. Earlier reading: 80% from 10 reviews on Sept 21, compared with 79% from 38 reviews on Oct 6.
Gold Derby's review roundup reported 79% on Rotten Tomatoes and a Metacritic score of 72 ('generally favorable'). Critics were generally positive but said it doesn't match Ang Lee's 1995 version.
World of Reel's critics' roundup was headlined 'Critics say Georgia Oakley's version is fine, not essential.'
Empire's review called the film 'a handsome but derivative take on Jane Austen.'
Ready Steady Cut's October 3 review called it 'A Superb Jane Austen Adaptation.' Reviews are still coming in mixed, with positive and lukewarm verdicts.

The review summary on the page says critics praise the lead performances and cinematography ('a grounded, gorgeous makeover'), while some found it tedious and overly somber compared with earlier adaptations.
For comparison, Ang Lee's 1995 Sense and Sensibility holds a 97% Certified Fresh Tomatometer.

Five straight rotten reviews would bring it to 30/43 ≈ 70%, which fails 'above 70'. It would take about 18 straight fresh reviews (48/56 ≈ 86%) to clear 'above 85'.

market.question: Will Ilija Srdanović be the next prime minister of Serbia?
market.rules:
This market will resolve to the next individual who officially assumes the office of Prime Minister of Serbia by June 30, 2028, 11:59 PM ET.

To count for resolution, the individual must be elected by the National Assembly and be formally sworn-in, resulting in the official formation of a new government. Any interim or caretaker Prime Minister who is not elected by the National Assembly will not count toward the resolution of this market.

If no such Prime Minister takes office by June 30, 2028, 11:59 PM ET, this market will resolve to “Other”.

This market will resolve based on a consensus of credible reporting. If there is ambiguity, this market will resolve solely based on official information from the Serbian government.

recent_facts.fact: A Faktor plus poll of 986 respondents (16–20 Sept 2026) had 'Aleksandar Vučić – Ujedinjena Srbija' (SNS) at 48.6%, the Student List at 37.1%, SPS at 4.9%, Evropska Srbija at 3.6%, Autentična desnica at 2.8% and Mi snaga naroda at 1.2%. It also found 16% of voters undecided and put expected turnout at about 62%.
In the Faktor Plus poll, the Student List was at 37.1%, 5.6 points higher than in that pollster's previous survey. The Vučić-led list was at 48.6%.
A BIRODI poll from around late August or early September 2026 put the Student List at 48.5% and SNS at 38.6%. The publication date is approximate.

A June 2026 survey by CRTA and Stanford researchers had the Student List ahead of SNS among decided voters, 44.9% to 35.7%. The article also said Faktor Plus did not disclose who commissioned its September poll, which showed SNS ahead 48.6% to 37.1%.
Ilija Srdanović, a cardiologist and medical professor from Novi Sad, heads the Student List's 250-candidate slate on the ballot. However, the movement says the list has no figurehead leader.

The election guide names Srdanović as the Student List's list bearer but does not say he, or anyone else, is the list's designated candidate for prime minister. The Student List has often distanced itself from the opposition, though parties including DS, Kreni-Promeni and Dveri back its campaign and People's Serbia withdrew its own list to support it.

Aleksandar Vučić resigned as President of Serbia on 27 September 2026, about eight months before his term ended, to lead SNS's 'United Serbia' list and run for prime minister. Assembly Speaker Ana Brnabić became acting president.
Vučić signed a decree dissolving the National Assembly and calling early parliamentary elections for 25 October 2026. They had originally been due by December 2027.
Sixteen certified electoral lists are running in the 25 October 2026 parliamentary election, with about 6.44 million registered voters. Election day is the same day the question closes.

The 250 Assembly seats are allocated by closed-list proportional representation in one nationwide constituency, using d'Hondt with a 3% threshold that is waived for ethnic-minority lists. A prime minister must be elected by an Assembly majority, so a government is formed after the vote and not on election day.
The current Prime Minister is Đuro Macut, an independent who succeeded Miloš Vučević on 16 April 2025.

SNS has governed Serbia since 2012. UNVERIFIED (from memory): SNS-led lists came first in all 6 parliamentary elections since 2012 (2012, 2014, 2016, 2020, 2022, 2023), and every prime minister since 2014 has been from SNS or backed by it.

recent_facts.fact: Faktor plus's August–September poll (about 1,200 respondents) had SNS at 47.2%, the Student List at 31.5% and SPS at 4.9%. Its 26 June poll had SNS 47.1% and Student List 30.7%.

The article describes the race between SNS and the Student List as having tightened: some polls put SNS first and others put the Student List first. Across the polls it lists, SNS ranges from roughly 30% to 45% and the Student List from roughly 15% to 40%.

All 250 seats are allocated by closed-list proportional representation in a single nationwide constituency using the D'Hondt method. The threshold is 3% of votes and is waived for ethnic-minority lists, so the list with the most votes normally wins the most seats.

Vučić resigned as President of Serbia on 27 Sept 2026 to head the 'Aleksandar Vučić – United Serbia' list as its candidate for prime minister. He had called the early election in September 2026; parliamentary elections were otherwise due by December 2027.

RIK announced 17 electoral lists and one was withdrawn, leaving 16 lists competing for 250 seats. 'Aleksandar Vučić – United Serbia' is No. 1 on the ballot and 'Student List – Students Are Winning' is No. 3. Vreme describes these two as the dominant blocs in the polls.

The student movement submitted its 'Student List – Students Win' to RIK after thousands of supporters marched through Belgrade. The list has a full 250 candidates and is headed by Novi Sad cardiology professor Ilija Srdanović.

Controversies so far: fact-checkers documented pro-government tabloids using AI-manipulated photos against Srdanović; opposition parties and NGOs left a working group on improving election conditions, citing government obstruction; and the government has called the student movement a Western-funded 'colour revolution'. The 2023 election drew allegations of vote buying and transported voters.
Election day is 25 Oct 2026, with polls open 7 AM–8 PM at 8,210 polling stations for about 6.44 million registered voters. The voter-register and summary-list deadline is 9 Oct 2026.

market.question: Will the rate of CPI inflation be above 3.6% for the year ending in September 2026? (Above 3.6%)
market.rules:
If the Consumer Price Index (CPI) increases by more than 3.6% in the twelve months ending September 2026 (as represented by the one-decimal place value reported by the Bureau of Labor Statistics), then the market resolves to Yes.
In the case of a delay in data caused by a federal government shutdown impacting the reliability of the Source Agency, the market’s latest Expiration Date will be extended to the sooner of the release of the Underlying or six months after the end of the
government shutdown

recent_facts.fact: In August 2026, CPI-U was up 3.4% over 12 months. The not-seasonally-adjusted index stood at 334.980 (1982-84=100), and seasonally adjusted CPI rose 0.4% for the month.

recent_facts.source: U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics (via FRASER / news release)
recent_facts.fact: The not-seasonally-adjusted September 2025 CPI-U index was 324.800, which was 3.0% above a year earlier. September 2025 was up 0.3% from August 2025 before seasonal adjustment. This is the base for the September 2026 year-over-year figure.

recent_facts.source: Research desk arithmetic from BLS index levels
recent_facts.fact: Measured against the September 2025 base of 324.800, a reported figure of 3.6% or higher requires a September 2026 NSA index of at least about 336.33, which is roughly +0.40% NSA from August's 334.980. A reported figure of 3.7% or higher requires at least about 336.66, roughly +0.50% NSA. These figures are approximate and depend on rounding at the edges.
In August 2026, the energy index rose 2.1% for the month and 16.3% over 12 months. Gasoline rose 3.9% for the month and 27.4% year over year.
Core CPI rose 0.3% in August 2026, and its annual rate was 2.4%. Gasoline accounted for more than one-third of the headline gain.
AAA's national average gasoline price for September 2026 was $4.33/gal, a September record and 50 cents above the previous September record of $3.83 set in 2023.

AAA's weekly national averages in August 2026 were about $4.06 (Aug 6), $4.07 (Aug 13), $4.10 (Aug 20) and $4.09 (Aug 27). That puts the August level at roughly $4.08, about 6% below the September monthly average of $4.33.
AAA's national average rose through September 2026: $4.14 on Sep 3, $4.27 on Sep 10 and $4.48 on Sep 24. AAA said the rise was driven by Strait of Hormuz volatility and high crude prices.
The August 2026 core PCE price index was up 3.0% year over year, which CNBC described as lighter than expected.
BLS is scheduled to publish the September 2026 CPI on Wednesday, October 14, 2026, at 8:30 a.m. ET. The questions close at 12:29 UTC that day, which is 8:29 a.m. ET.

market.question: Will Brad Bradford win the 2026 Toronto mayoral election?
market.rules:
The 2026 Toronto mayoral election is currently scheduled to be held on October 26, 2026.

This market will resolve according to the candidate who becomes the next mayor of Toronto as a result of this election.

Temporary, interim, or placeholder mayors appointed before the election will not be considered.

If the result of this election isn't known by June 30, 2027, 11:59 PM ET, the market will resolve to "Other".

The primary resolution source for this market will be a consensus of credible reporting; however, if there is any ambiguity in the results, this market will resolve according to official information from Toronto.

recent_facts.fact: A Mainstreet Research poll released as the campaign entered its final month had Chow at 38.1%, Bradford at 32.2% and Alexander at 7.2%, a 6-point lead for Chow.

A Liaison Strategies Toronto Pulse poll had Chow ahead of Bradford 48% to 39% among decided and leaning voters, with Alexander at 10% and others at 3%. Chow's lead was slightly wider than in Liaison's previous poll, although her job approval had fallen below 50%.
An earlier Liaison poll had Chow at 47%, Bradford at 40% and Alexander at 10% among decided and leaning voters. Women backed Chow 56% to 32%, while men backed Bradford 47% to 41%.

On Tuesday, Oct. 6, the day advance voting began, Chris Alexander, a former Conservative minister who placed third, dropped out of the race. He endorsed no other candidate, and his name is likely to stay on the ballot.

Wikipedia's summary of the campaign polling says Chow has led Bradford in most polls, by 7 to 17 points. More than 60 candidates registered, and the main contenders are Chow, Bradford (councillor for Ward 19) and Alexander, who has now withdrawn.

Chow is endorsed by CUPE Local 79, LiUNA Local 183, the Toronto and York Region Labour Council and several NDP MPPs and MPs. Bradford is endorsed by Liberal MPs Yvan Baker and Judy Sgro, former MPs Peter Kent and John McKay, and musician Geddy Lee.

Bradford promised to scrap the municipal land transfer tax on homes under $1.1 million, a measure he puts at $300 million, with buyers saving up to $18,000. He also promised to cut water bills by 25%.
Advance voting began on Oct. 6, and election day is Oct. 26, 2026. The nomination period ran from May 1 to Aug. 21, 2026.

Toronto elects its mayor by first-past-the-post in a single round, so whoever gets the most votes on Oct. 26 wins and there is no runoff. Chow is the incumbent and is seeking her first full term after winning the 2023 by-election.

market.question: Will a new pneumonic plague case be confirmed in Russia by October 15?
market.rules:
This market will resolve to "Yes" if a confirmed case of pneumonic plague in a human is reported in the Russian Federation at any point between market creation and the specified date, 11:59 PM Moscow time, . Otherwise, this market will resolve to "No".

A "confirmed case" is a case explicitly identified by a qualifying source as laboratory-confirmed Yersinia pestis infection with pneumonic (pulmonary) involvement, or explicitly announced as a confirmed pneumonic plague case. Publication of the underlying laboratory results is not required. A bubonic or septicemic case that progresses to pneumonic plague qualifies. A case reported only as "plague" with no form specified, and a case described only as suspected or probable, do not qualify.

The case must be distinct from the Irkutsk Anti-Plague Research Institute employee who reportedly passed away on October 1, 2026; subsequent confirmation, reclassification, or post-mortem testing of that patient will not qualify. Resolution turns on the date a qualifying source publishes the confirmation, not the date of exposure, symptom onset, or laboratory result. A report published after the deadline does not count even if the infection occurred earlier.

The primary resolution sources for this market will be official information from Russian federal or regional public health authorities and the WHO; however a consensus of credible sources will also suffice.

recent_facts.fact: Graham Platner won the June 9 Democratic primary, then withdrew on July 10 after a sexual assault allegation, which he denies. On July 25, Democratic convention delegates in Bangor picked former state Senate President Troy Jackson as the replacement nominee: Jackson got 566 votes and Sandra Pelletier got 5.

The CBS/YouGov poll of 1,144 Maine registered voters (Sept 23–Oct 1, MoE ±4.7) found Collins and Jackson tied, and about 10% said they could still change their minds. Collins drew about 1 in 5 voters who disapprove of Trump, and Jackson ran behind Democratic governor nominee Hannah Pingree. Four in ten Democrats and most independents said they wished someone else were the Democratic nominee.
An AARP poll released around Oct 1, 2026 showed Jackson narrowly ahead of incumbent Collins, by a margin AARP called slim.

A late-September UMass Lowell Maine poll had Jackson at 51% and Collins at 47%, which the pollsters described as essentially a tie given the margin of error. Independents split 49% Jackson, 47% Collins.
A search-result summary gave the polling average as Jackson 47.6% and Collins 47.5%, about a tie. I did not read the RCP page itself to confirm this.
A July 2026 UNH poll, taken before Jackson was nominated, had Jackson at 49% and Collins at 46% among likely general election voters.

In 2020, Democrat Sara Gideon led Collins in every independent public poll that year. Collins trailed by 5.5 points in the final RCP average (Emerson had Gideon +6 at the end of October, Quinnipiac +12 in September), yet Collins won by about 9 points. That is a polling miss of roughly 14–15 points, all in Collins's favor.

In 2020, Collins won by about 9 points while Biden also carried Maine by about 9, which shows heavy ticket-splitting in her favor. Collins has won five straight Senate elections (1996, 2002, 2008, 2014, 2020); this count is from memory and was not checked against a source.
Three more Collins–Jackson debates are scheduled, on Oct 8, Oct 13 and Oct 15. The general election is Nov 3, 2026.

Maine uses ranked-choice voting for statewide federal races, so if no one wins a first-round majority, lower-ranked choices are redistributed until someone does. market.question: Will Bitcoin be above $100000 by November 1, 2026 at 12:00AM ET? (Before November 2026)
market.rules:
If the Bitcoin spot price according to the CF Bitcoin Real-Time Index is above $100000.00 starting Jul 21, 2026 and before Nov 1, 2026 at 12:00 AM ET, then the market resolves to Yes.
The market resolves based on the CF Bitcoin Real-Time Index (BRTI) using a trimmed mean calculation. The resolution value is calculated by taking all BRTI values for each minute from market issuance until the specified time on the target date, removing the top 20% and bottom 20% of values, then averaging the remaining 60% of values. If the BRTI crosses the threshold at any point during the measurement period (triggering early expiration), the market immediately resolves. If no data is available at the expiration time, the market resolves to No. The market can resolve early if Bitcoin definitively crosses the threshold before the target date and time.

The resolution source will be official information from the Bank of England, including the statement or release from its November 2026 Monetary Policy Committee meeting, scheduled for November 5, 2026, as listed on the official Bank of England calendar (https://www.bankofengland.co.uk/monetary-policy/upcoming-mpc-dates). This market may resolve as soon as the statement or release of the Bank of England's November 2026 Monetary Policy Committee meeting with relevant data is issued.

If the specified rate is defined by an upper and lower bound, the relevant change will be the change to the upper bound.

If the specified rate is changed to a level not expressed in the displayed options, the change will be rounded according to the following guidelines. Increases or decreases of less than 25 bps will be rounded to 25 bps (e.g. an increase or decrease of 10 bps would be considered to be an increase or decrease of 25 bps). Increases or decreases of greater than 25 bps will be rounded to the nearest 25 bps and will be rounded away from 0 in cases of equidistance (e.g., an increase or decrease of 37.5 bps would be considered to be an increase or decrease of 50 bps). Displayed options of “Increase” or “Decrease” will include policy rate increases or decreases of any size.

If the specified meeting is postponed to a date and time before the start of the next scheduled meeting, this market will resolve based on the outcome of that postponed meeting. If the specified meeting is cancelled, or postponed such that no decision is announced by the start of the next scheduled meeting, this market will resolve to the “No Change” bracket. Emergency changes to the specified rate not resulting from the specified meeting will not be considered.

recent_facts.fact: At its meeting ending 16 September 2026, the MPC voted 6–3 to keep Bank Rate at 3.75%. Bailey, Breeden, Dhingra, Lombardelli, Ramsden and Taylor voted to hold; Greene, Mann and Pill voted to raise it 25bp to 4.00%.

The September minutes say the Committee 'stands ready to act as necessary' to keep CPI on track for 2%, without explicit guidance on the next move. The MPC projects CPI inflation reaching slightly above 4% in early 2027.

Governor Bailey said: 'the longer this volatility persists, the bigger the impact it will have on inflation, and the more likely it is we will need to raise Bank Rate to ensure that inflation falls back to our 2% target.' CNBC reported the Bank held rates even though the Fed had raised its rate.

ING reported that Bailey described a possible November move as an 'insurance hike' based on risk management rather than incoming data. ING said whether the Bank hikes depends on whether oil and gas prices stay high over the six weeks to November.
The September minutes say the next MPC meeting concludes on 4 November 2026, with the decision and minutes published on 5 November 2026. That matches the market's resolution date.

The minutes say members who voted to hold pointed to weaker-than-expected pass-through of energy costs to other goods, few second-round effects in wages and prices so far, restrictive financial conditions, domestic slack and a soft labour market. One member said policy should respond to 'evidence of propagation rather than mechanically to volatile ticks in headline energy prices.'

Alan Taylor, who voted to hold, said the surge in gas and oil prices has 'clearly increased near-term inflation risks.' He added that higher energy costs 'still appear largely concentrated within the energy complex itself rather than spreading widely through the economy.'

According to the minutes, Lombardelli said oil and gas prices are currently closer to the July adverse scenario. Dhingra said repeated re-escalation of the Middle East conflict has amplified the adverse supply shock.
Brent crude rose to $100.84 a barrel on 6 October 2026. It was up 3.78% over the past month and 54.06% from a year earlier.
UK CPI inflation rose to 3.1% in August 2026 from 2.9% in July, driven mainly by motor fuels. Core CPI was unchanged at 2.6% and services inflation was unchanged at 3.4%.
ING said that if wholesale gas prices stay at current levels, the household energy price cap could rise by about 25% in January.
Bank Rate was also held at 3.75% in June and July 2026. Reports say it was last changed with a cut in December 2025, and there have been no rate increases in 2026 so far.

facts_dropped.fact: Before the 5 November decision, the remaining releases include September CPI (due mid-to-late October) and further labour market and GDP data. The November meeting will also come with a new Monetary Policy Report forecast.

market.question: Will Aleksandar Vučić be the next Prime Minister of Serbia?
market.rules:
This market will resolve to the next individual who officially assumes the office of Prime Minister of Serbia by June 30, 2028, 11:59 PM ET.

To count for resolution, the individual must be elected by the National Assembly and be formally sworn-in, resulting in the official formation of a new government. Any interim or caretaker Prime Minister who is not elected by the National Assembly will not count toward the resolution of this market.

If no such Prime Minister takes office by June 30, 2028, 11:59 PM ET, this market will resolve to “Other”.

This market will resolve based on a consensus of credible reporting. If there is ambiguity, this market will resolve solely based on official information from the Serbian government.

recent_facts.fact: A Faktor plus poll of 986 respondents (16–20 Sept 2026) had 'Aleksandar Vučić – Ujedinjena Srbija' (SNS) at 48.6%, the Student List at 37.1%, SPS at 4.9%, Evropska Srbija at 3.6%, Autentična desnica at 2.8% and Mi snaga naroda at 1.2%. It also found 16% of voters undecided and put expected turnout at about 62%.
In the Faktor Plus poll, the Student List was at 37.1%, 5.6 points higher than in that pollster's previous survey. The Vučić-led list was at 48.6%.
A BIRODI poll from around late August or early September 2026 put the Student List at 48.5% and SNS at 38.6%. The publication date is approximate.

A June 2026 survey by CRTA and Stanford researchers had the Student List ahead of SNS among decided voters, 44.9% to 35.7%. The article also said Faktor Plus did not disclose who commissioned its September poll, which showed SNS ahead 48.6% to 37.1%.
Ilija Srdanović, a cardiologist and medical professor from Novi Sad, heads the Student List's 250-candidate slate on the ballot. However, the movement says the list has no figurehead leader.

The election guide names Srdanović as the Student List's list bearer but does not say he, or anyone else, is the list's designated candidate for prime minister. The Student List has often distanced itself from the opposition, though parties including DS, Kreni-Promeni and Dveri back its campaign and People's Serbia withdrew its own list to support it.

Aleksandar Vučić resigned as President of Serbia on 27 September 2026, about eight months before his term ended, to lead SNS's 'United Serbia' list and run for prime minister. Assembly Speaker Ana Brnabić became acting president.
Vučić signed a decree dissolving the National Assembly and calling early parliamentary elections for 25 October 2026. They had originally been due by December 2027.
Sixteen certified electoral lists are running in the 25 October 2026 parliamentary election, with about 6.44 million registered voters. Election day is the same day the question closes.

The 250 Assembly seats are allocated by closed-list proportional representation in one nationwide constituency, using d'Hondt with a 3% threshold that is waived for ethnic-minority lists. A prime minister must be elected by an Assembly majority, so a government is formed after the vote and not on election day.
The current Prime Minister is Đuro Macut, an independent who succeeded Miloš Vučević on 16 April 2025.

SNS has governed Serbia since 2012. UNVERIFIED (from memory): SNS-led lists came first in all 6 parliamentary elections since 2012 (2012, 2014, 2016, 2020, 2022, 2023), and every prime minister since 2014 has been from SNS or backed by it.

market.question: Will the upper bound of the federal funds rate be above 4.00% following the Fed's Oct 28, 2026 meeting? (Above 4.00%)
market.rules:
If the upper bound of the target federal funds rate published on the Federal Reserve's official website is greater than 4.00% following the Federal Reserve's Oct 28, 2026 meeting, then the market resolves to Yes.
This market will expire the first 2:05 PM ET following the release of a Federal Reserve statement for their Oct 28, 2026 meeting or one week following the last day of that meeting.

recent_facts.fact: At its September 16, 2026 meeting the FOMC voted 12-0 to raise the federal funds target range by 25 bp to 3.75%–4.00%. The current upper bound is therefore exactly 4.00%, so only a hike at the Oct 27–28 meeting would put it above 4.00%.
The September hike was the first rate increase since 2023.

The September dot plot's median shows one more 25 bp hike by end-2026 (to about 4.1%). Sixteen of 18 participants projected at least one more hike this year, and four projected two. Two FOMC meetings remain in 2026: October 27–28 and December.
The September jobs report showed payrolls up only 29,000, against estimates of more than 80,000. Unemployment rose to 4.2% from 4.1%, and wage growth slowed.

NY Fed President John Williams said there is 'no need for urgency' and that 'one further upward adjustment' may be appropriate late this year. Vice Chair Jefferson said future moves should come from 'carefully examining trends in the data.' Minneapolis Fed's Kashkari said he had no strong view on hiking at the end of October. Dallas Fed's Logan called September's hike a 'first step' but did not say when the next one should come.

Yahoo Finance reported that the weak September jobs report is likely to keep the Fed on hold in October, with attention staying on inflation. The August PCE release on Sept 30 came in cooler than expected, though core PCE was still running at about 3%.

Fed officials including Williams, Barr, Hammack and Paulson said further hikes may be needed because inflation has been above 2% for 5.5 years. Governor Cook pointed to inflation pressure from the AI buildout and from oil prices. Diesel was $6.529/gal, up from $3.739 a year earlier.
September CPI comes out October 14, 2026 at 8:30 AM ET. It is the last CPI report before the October 27–28 FOMC meeting. The prior (August) headline CPI was 3.4% year over year.

market.question: Will WTI Crude Oil (WTI) hit (HIGH) $100 in October?
market.rules:
This market will resolve to "Yes" if, at any point after market creation and during a trading session of October 2026, any Pyth 1-minute candle for the Active Month of ICE Futures Europe WTI Crude Futures (denoted by Pyth as "CLL") has a final "High" or "Low" price equal to or beyond (above for ↑ High Prices, below for ↓ Low Prices) the listed price. Otherwise, this market will resolve to "No".

Prices will be used exactly as published by Pyth, without rounding.

Only prices achieved during an applicable trading session of the specified timeframe's business days will be considered (See: "Trading Hours" at https://www.ice.com/products/213/WTI-Crude-Futures). The trading session for a given business day typically begins at 8:00 PM ET on the prior calendar date, except for the session dated Monday, which begins at 6:00 PM ET on the preceding Sunday, and where modified by holiday or other special hours (See: https://www.ice.com/holiday-hours).

The Active Month is the nearest listed contract, except during that contract's final three trading sessions. At the open of the third-to-last trading session, the next listed contract becomes the Active Month.

Each contract's last trading day will be determined by ICE Futures Europe per the WTI Crude Futures contract specification (generally the 4th US business day prior to the 25th calendar day of the month preceding the contract month, or five US business days prior if the 25th calendar day is not a US business day). The last trading day for each contract is posted at https://www.ice.com/products/213/WTI-Crude-Futures/expiry.

For example, if the last trading session for the nearest listed contract is the session for Monday the 20th, the next listed contract would become the Active Month at the start of the trading session for Thursday the 16th (8:00 PM ET on Wednesday), assuming a standard trading calendar.

If the relevant Pyth data is unavailable due to a system outage, data failure, or other disruption that prevents verification of the required 1-minute candle data, the official daily high/low price published for the Active Month WTI Crude Oil Futures contract by ICE Futures Europe may be used to determine whether the listed price was reached during the applicable trading session (See: https://www.ice.com/report/10 with "T-West Texas Intermediate Light Sweet Crude Future" selected).

In the event of a contract specification change, feed change, or similar structural modification affecting the underlying market during the listed time frame, this market will resolve based on adjusted prices as displayed on Pyth.

If the Active Month contract does not trade at all during the listed time frame, this market will resolve to "No".

The resolution source for this market is Pyth — specifically, the ICE Futures Europe WTI Crude Futures Active Month "High" and "Low" prices available at https://app.pyth.com/explore?search=CLL, with the chart settings configured for 1-minute candles. Historical 1-minute candles may be accessed by appending a Unix timestamp (seconds) to the Pyth chart URL using the "t=" parameter.

market.question: Will the Democratic Party control the House after the 2026 Midterm elections?
market.rules:
This market will resolve according to the party that wins control of the United States House of Representatives in the 2026 United States midterm election.

A party wins control of the United States House of Representatives if it wins a majority of the chamber’s voting seats. If no party wins a majority of voting seats, the chamber will be deemed controlled by the party with which the first elected Speaker of the House of the Congress that convenes after the 2026 midterm election is affiliated.

The following rules govern the counting of seats for determining which party wins control of the chamber.

All House elections in the 2026 United States midterm election that elect voting members and determine representation in the upcoming 120th Congress are included. Where a seat is decided by a runoff, the runoff result will determine attribution of that seat.

Seats are attributed to the party under which the member was elected. If a member-elect changes party affiliation, or vacates their seat, between election day and the formal organization of Congress, the seat is attributed to the party under which the member was elected.

House members elected as independents who formally caucus with, or, for newly elected members, who announce their intent to caucus with, a party are included in that party’s count. If the caucus decisions of members of the House elected as independents cannot be determined on the date of the election, this market may remain open until the earlier of (i) an announcement from the relevant members of their intents to caucus, or (ii) January 4th, 11:59 PM ET of the following calendar year. If no such announcement is made by January 4th, 11:59 PM ET of the following calendar year, the member will not count towards the seat count of any party.

The resolution sources for this market will be official information from relevant state electoral authorities, the United States Congress, and a consensus of credible reporting.

recent_facts.source: Cook Political Report (via Universe News Network / Axios)
recent_facts.fact: Cook's September 25, 2026 update moved 15 House races toward Democrats, and all 15 moved the same way. Cook now rates 208 seats as favoring Democrats and 205 as favoring Republicans. Of its 22 Toss Ups, 17 are held by Republicans and 5 by Democrats.

recent_facts.source: Cook Political Report (via Universe News Network)
recent_facts.fact: Some Texas seats, including Rep. Monica De La Cruz's district, moved from Likely Republican to Toss Up. According to Cook, Republicans would need to win a majority of the Toss Up races to keep the House.
Decision Desk HQ's polling average shows Democrats ahead of Republicans by about 6 points on the generic ballot, 46% to 40%.

CBS News' House seat estimate shows Democrats keeping their edge for a narrow majority of seats and their lead in national vote preference. CBS attributes this to opposition to Trump administration policies and a Republican base that is less likely to turn out.

As of about October 5, 2026, the House had 218 Republicans, 214 Democrats and 1 independent (Kevin Kiley of California, who caucuses with Republicans), with 2 seats vacant. Democrats need a net gain of 3 districts for a majority; Republicans can lose no more than 2.
A handicapper's seat count cited by Fox News shows Democrats ahead of Republicans 215–201 in projected seats, with 19 races rated Toss Up.

Wikipedia lists the following new maps in effect for 2026 and the seats they are expected to shift: Texas R+5, Ohio R+2, North Carolina R+1, Utah R+1, Florida R+4 (enacted May 4, 2026), Tennessee R+1, Louisiana R+1, Alabama R+1, and California D+5 (Prop 50). Wikipedia's own summary gives the net as 'Republican +12, Democratic +1', which does not match these per-state figures, so treat that summary total as unverified.

Virginia's Democratic redraw, aimed at about D+4, failed. Voters approved it in a referendum on April 21, 2026, but the Virginia Supreme Court struck the amendment down on May 8, and the U.S. Supreme Court denied an emergency appeal on May 15. Missouri's new map (R+1) was blocked for 2026 by a referendum petition.

Louisiana enacted a new map on May 29, 2026, after the Louisiana v. Callais decision, and suspended its primary. New election dates are November 3 and December 12, 2026, so some Louisiana seats may be decided in a December runoff, which counts under the resolution rules.
Election Day is November 3, 2026, and all 435 House seats are up. Both questions close on November 4, 2026 at 04:59 UTC.
Since 1946, the president's party has lost an average of about 25–26 House seats in midterm elections. Its party has gained seats in the House or Senate in only eight midterms in U.S. history.
In Gallup's analysis, presidents with job approval below 50% saw their party lose an average of 37 House seats in midterms, compared with an average loss of 14 seats when approval was above 50%.

facts_dropped.source: Nate Silver Bulletin generic ballot average
facts_dropped.fact: In early October 2026, Democrats led the generic congressional ballot average by about 8–8.9 points (about 51.1% to 43.4% as of Oct 6). This is their highest point of the cycle, and the first time their average has been above 50%.
facts_dropped.reason: cites a forecaster

Rams DE Myles Garrett, the reigning Defensive Player of the Year, is on injured reserve with a knee injury. TE Colby Parkinson (shoulder/knee) was inactive in Week 4, and WR Konata Mumpfield (shoulder) returned during that game.

Buffalo has a new staff this year. Joe Brady was promoted to head coach after Sean McDermott was fired following the January playoff loss to Denver. Pete Carmichael Jr. is offensive coordinator and Jim Leonhard is defensive coordinator. The Bills also traded for WR D.J. Moore.

The all-time series is Bills 9, Rams 6 across 15 regular-season games, which is a small sample. The last two meetings: Buffalo won 31-10 on Sept 8, 2022, and the Rams won 44-42 at home on Dec 8, 2024.

If no party wins a majority of voting seats, the party that wins control of the chamber is the party that wins half of the voting seats and holds the Vice Presidency. If the outcome remains ambiguous after applying the above criteria, the chamber will be deemed controlled by the party with which the first selected President Pro Tempore of the Congress that convenes after the specified election is affiliated.

A party wins control of the United States House of Representatives if it wins a majority of the chamber’s voting seats. If no party wins a majority of voting seats, the chamber will be deemed controlled by the party with which the first elected Speaker of the House of the Congress that convenes after the 2026 midterm election is affiliated.

The following rules govern the counting of seats for determining which party wins control of the chambers.

market.question: Will the Republicans win the Texas Senate race in 2026?
market.rules:
This market will resolve according to the winner of the 2026 midterm Texas U.S. Senate election, inclusive of any run-offs.

A candidate shall be considered to represent a party in the event that he or she is the nominee of the party in question. Candidates other than the Democratic or Republican nominee (e.g., Greens, Libertarian, independent) may be added at a later date.

Candidates who run as independents will not be encompassed by the “Democrat” or “Republican” options regardless of any affiliation they may have with the party.

The candidates may be named in the contract for the convenience of traders. In the event that any named candidate is replaced as the nominee of their respective party prior to election day, the name in the contract will be updated and the market will resolve based on the replacement nominee of the party.

The resolution source for this market is the Associated Press, Fox News, and NBC. This market will resolve once all three sources call the race for the same candidate. If all three sources haven’t called the race in this state for the same candidate, this market will resolve based on the official certification.

recent_facts.fact: A New York Times/Siena poll of 615 Texas voters, taken Sept. 21–30, 2026, had Democrat James Talarico at 51% and Republican Ken Paxton at 45%, with a margin of error of ±4.5. The same pollster's June 2026 poll had the race tied 47–47.

A Fox News poll of 881 likely voters, taken Sept. 24–28, 2026, had Talarico at 51% and Paxton at 49%, with a margin of error of ±3. Talarico's favorability was 52% favorable to 44% unfavorable; Paxton's was 40% to 58%.

As of Oct. 5, 2026, the RealClearPolitics polling average had Talarico at 48.4% and Paxton at 45.3%, so Talarico was ahead by 3.1 points. About 6% of voters were undecided or backing other candidates.

A recent Texas Southern University poll had Talarico at 47% and Paxton at 46%. A University of Texas/Texas Politics Project poll had Talarico at 42% and Paxton at 39%, leaving a large share undecided. Exact field dates were not confirmed.

AP projected that Attorney General Ken Paxton won the Republican runoff, beating Sen. John Cornyn after President Trump endorsed Paxton the week before. Cornyn had led the March 3 primary but fell short of a majority. Cornyn is the first Republican senator from Texas to lose his party's renomination.

As of early October, ad spending in the race had reached $442 million, making it the second-most expensive non-presidential race in U.S. history. Republicans accounted for $326 million and Democrats for $116 million. In the NYT/Siena poll, 57% disapproved of Trump's job performance, up 5 points from June.

In the Fox News poll, 53% of likely voters said they were concerned Talarico is too liberal and 51% said they were concerned Paxton is too close to Trump. 68% called cost of living extremely important to their vote.

Talarico accepted TV debates on Oct. 6 (WFAA, Dallas) and Oct. 13 (KXAN, Austin). As of late September, Paxton had not committed to any specific debate date, and WFAA reported his campaign had not responded since Aug. 24.

In the same polling cycle, Republican Gov. Greg Abbott led Democrat Gina Hinojosa by 4 points (50–46) in one poll, and another poll showed the governor's race tied. Libertarian Ted Brown also appears in some Senate polls.
Early voting in Texas starts Oct. 19, 2026, and Election Day is Nov. 3, 2026.

In the 2024 Texas Senate race, the final polling average had Ted Cruz up about 3.8 points (49.0 to 45.2), but he won by 8.5 points (53.05% to 44.56%). The polls underestimated the Republican margin by about 4.7 points.

In 2018, final polls mostly had Cruz ahead of Beto O'Rourke by 3 to 6 points (Emerson +3, UT-Tyler +3.6, Quinnipiac +5, Texas Tribune +6). Cruz won by about 2.6 points (51% to 48%), so the Democrat did slightly better than most polls showed.
Texas has not elected a Democrat to any statewide office in about 30 years, since 1994. From memory and unverified: the last Democrat to win a Texas U.S. Senate race was Lloyd Bentsen in 1988.

The question resolves once AP, Fox News and NBC all call the race for the same candidate, and otherwise on official certification. Paxton is the Republican nominee. From memory and unverified: Texas general elections are decided by plurality, with no general-election runoff.

recent_facts.fact: Republicans hold the Senate 53-47; the 47 includes two independents who caucus with Democrats. Democrats need a net gain of four seats for a 51-49 majority. Vice President JD Vance is a Republican, so under the resolution rules a 50-50 split counts as Republican control.

35 Senate seats are up in 2026, including specials in Florida and Ohio; 23 of them are held by Republicans. Cook rates 9 Solid D, 2 Likely D, 1 Lean D, 7 Toss-up, 1 Lean R, 2 Likely R and 13 Solid R. The toss-ups are Alaska, Iowa, Maine, Michigan, New Hampshire, Ohio and Texas.

Cook's most recent update moved Georgia from Lean to Likely Democratic, Kansas from Likely to Lean Republican, and South Carolina from Safe to Likely Republican. Separately, Cook moved Iowa from Lean Republican to Toss-up.

CNN ranks North Carolina (open GOP seat) as the seat most likely to flip. An Elon University/YouGov poll released in September had Democrat Roy Cooper 11 points ahead of Republican Michael Whatley among likely voters.

Ohio special: a New York Times/Siena poll of likely voters from late September had Democrat Sherrod Brown at 49% and Republican Sen. Jon Husted at 46%, within the margin of error. CNN says Brown has led Husted in most polls.

Texas: a Fox News poll of likely voters had Democrat James Talarico at 51% and Republican Ken Paxton at 49%, within the 3-point margin of error. Talarico's favorability was net +8 and Paxton's net -18. A polling average reported alongside had Talarico ahead 48.2% to 45.4%.

Alaska (ranked-choice voting): a NYT/Siena poll of 504 likely voters taken Sept 24–Oct 1 had Democrat Mary Peltola at 50% and Republican Sen. Dan Sullivan at 43%. A Quantus Insights poll had them tied 46-46. An AARP poll had Peltola ahead 46-41 on first choices and 53-47 after ranked-choice tabulation.

recent_facts.source: AARP / Portland Press Herald / CBS News
recent_facts.fact: Maine: an NYT/Press Herald/Siena poll (Sept 24) had Republican Sen. Susan Collins at 49% and Democrat Troy Jackson at 46% (margin ±4.9). An AARP poll had Jackson ahead 50-47, a UNH poll had Jackson ahead 51-47, and a CBS News poll (Oct 2) found the race tied.
Troy Jackson became the Maine Democratic nominee at a nominating convention on July 25, 2026. He replaced Graham Platner, who withdrew in July after sexual assault allegations.

Iowa (open GOP seat): an InsiderAdvantage poll from Sept 22–23 had Democrat Josh Turek at 47% and Republican Ashley Hinson at 46%. A Marist poll had Turek ahead about 50-42. An average of 14 polls had Turek at 46.3 and Hinson at 45.1.

Michigan (open Democratic seat): a Fox News poll had Democrat Abdul El-Sayed at 50% and Republican Mike Rogers at 49% among likely voters, and 51-48 among registered voters. In Fox's August poll Rogers led 51-47. A Mitchell Research poll had El-Sayed ahead 45.6% to 41.4%.

Election day is November 3, 2026. Alaska uses ranked-choice voting, so the result there may take longer than election night. Under the resolution rules, any runoffs, such as a possible Georgia runoff, decide those seats even if held after November.

recent_facts.source: Ripon Society / UCSB American Presidency Project
recent_facts.fact: Since 1934 the president's party has lost an average of 3.4 Senate seats in midterms and has lost Senate seats about two-thirds of the time. It gained seats in 1934, 1998 and 2002. Unverified: these counts come from a secondary summary.

Recent midterms in which Senate control changed include 1994, 2006 and 2014, all moving against the president's party; in 2002 control moved to the president's party. Big Senate midterm losses include 13 seats in 1958, 12 in 1946, 9 in 2014 and 8 in 1986 and 1994. Unverified: this is not a complete count from one source.

market.question: Will the ECB announce no change at the October 2026 meeting?
market.rules:
This market will resolve according to the change in basis points in the deposit facility rate resulting from the October 2026 meeting of the European Central Bank, relative to the level it was prior to this meeting.

The resolution source will be official information from the European Central Bank, including the statement or release from its October 2026 meeting, scheduled for October 28-29, 2026, as listed on the official European Central Bank calendar (https://www.ecb.europa.eu/press/calendars/mgcgc/html/index.en.html). This market may resolve as soon as the statement or release of the European Central Bank's October 2026 meeting with relevant data is issued.

If the specified rate is defined by an upper and lower bound, the relevant change will be the change to the upper bound.

If the specified rate is changed to a level not expressed in the displayed options, the change will be rounded according to the following guidelines. Increases or decreases of less than 25 bps will be rounded to 25 bps (e.g. an increase or decrease of 10 bps would be considered to be an increase or decrease of 25 bps). Increases or decreases of greater than 25 bps will be rounded to the nearest 25 bps and will be rounded away from 0 in cases of equidistance (e.g., an increase or decrease of 37.5 bps would be considered to be an increase or decrease of 50 bps). Displayed options of “Increase” or “Decrease” will include policy rate increases or decreases of any size.

If the specified meeting is postponed to a date and time before the start of the next scheduled meeting, this market will resolve based on the outcome of that postponed meeting. If the specified meeting is cancelled, or postponed such that no decision is announced by the start of the next scheduled meeting, this market will resolve to the “No Change” bracket. Emergency changes to the specified rate not resulting from the specified meeting will not be considered.

recent_facts.fact: On September 10, 2026 the ECB raised the deposit facility rate by 25 bps to 2.50%, effective September 16. The main refinancing rate went to 2.65% and the marginal lending rate to 2.90%. This was the second hike of 2026.
In 2026 the ECB hiked 25 bps on June 11, which was its first hike in three years, held on July 23 and hiked 25 bps again on September 10. That puts the 2026 pattern so far at hike, pause, hike.

Bundesbank President Joachim Nagel said there are 'no clear signs of second-round effects' and no 'inflation feeding through to price and wage setting'. The report took this to mean the ECB has room to wait in October. Nagel also said inflation risks 'remain tilted to the upside', which keeps a December hike open.
September's 3.8% inflation reading came in above the 3.7% Bloomberg consensus.
At the same hearing Lagarde said risks to growth are tilted to the downside and inflation risks to the upside. She repeated that decisions are taken meeting by meeting.

Executive Board member Isabel Schnabel named three factors for the next move: price expectations, demand, and global borrowing costs. She said 'As long as expectations are firmly anchored... monetary policy can tolerate a more gradual return of inflation to target.' She also noted that rising US yields could dampen growth more than models expect.

A Bloomberg report published right after the September hike was headlined 'ECB Officials Expect Further Rate Hikes with October in Play'. Unnamed officials said more tightening was expected and did not rule out October.
Latvia's Martins Kazaks said 'The case is building up for more tightening.' He would not say whether a hike could come in October, but said the ECB can move 'stepwise' and 'without rush'.
Eurostat will publish the full September 2026 HICP data on October 16, 2026, before the October 29 decision. The October flash estimate is due after the meeting.
