market.question: Bank of England increases interest rates by 25 bps after November 2026 meeting?
market.rules:
This market will resolve according to the change in basis points in the Bank Rate resulting from the November 2026 meeting of the Bank of England’s Monetary Policy Committee, relative to the level it was prior to this meeting.

The resolution source will be official information from the Bank of England, including the statement or release from its November 2026 Monetary Policy Committee meeting, scheduled for November 5, 2026, as listed on the official Bank of England calendar (https://www.bankofengland.co.uk/monetary-policy/upcoming-mpc-dates). This market may resolve as soon as the statement or release of the Bank of England's November 2026 Monetary Policy Committee meeting with relevant data is issued.

If the specified rate is defined by an upper and lower bound, the relevant change will be the change to the upper bound.

If the specified rate is changed to a level not expressed in the displayed options, the change will be rounded according to the following guidelines. Increases or decreases of less than 25 bps will be rounded to 25 bps (e.g. an increase or decrease of 10 bps would be considered to be an increase or decrease of 25 bps). Increases or decreases of greater than 25 bps will be rounded to the nearest 25 bps and will be rounded away from 0 in cases of equidistance (e.g., an increase or decrease of 37.5 bps would be considered to be an increase or decrease of 50 bps). Displayed options of “Increase” or “Decrease” will include policy rate increases or decreases of any size.

If the specified meeting is postponed to a date and time before the start of the next scheduled meeting, this market will resolve based on the outcome of that postponed meeting. If the specified meeting is cancelled, or postponed such that no decision is announced by the start of the next scheduled meeting, this market will resolve to the “No Change” bracket. Emergency changes to the specified rate not resulting from the specified meeting will not be considered.

recent_facts.fact: At its meeting ending 16 September 2026, the MPC voted 6–3 to keep Bank Rate at 3.75%. Bailey, Breeden, Dhingra, Lombardelli, Ramsden and Taylor voted to hold; Greene, Mann and Pill voted to raise it 25bp to 4.00%.

The September minutes say the Committee 'stands ready to act as necessary' to keep CPI on track for 2%, without explicit guidance on the next move. The MPC projects CPI inflation reaching slightly above 4% in early 2027.

Governor Bailey said: 'the longer this volatility persists, the bigger the impact it will have on inflation, and the more likely it is we will need to raise Bank Rate to ensure that inflation falls back to our 2% target.' CNBC reported the Bank held rates even though the Fed had raised its rate.

ING reported that Bailey described a possible November move as an 'insurance hike' based on risk management rather than incoming data. ING said whether the Bank hikes depends on whether oil and gas prices stay high over the six weeks to November.
The September minutes say the next MPC meeting concludes on 4 November 2026, with the decision and minutes published on 5 November 2026. That matches the market's resolution date.

The minutes say members who voted to hold pointed to weaker-than-expected pass-through of energy costs to other goods, few second-round effects in wages and prices so far, restrictive financial conditions, domestic slack and a soft labour market. One member said policy should respond to 'evidence of propagation rather than mechanically to volatile ticks in headline energy prices.'

Alan Taylor, who voted to hold, said the surge in gas and oil prices has 'clearly increased near-term inflation risks.' He added that higher energy costs 'still appear largely concentrated within the energy complex itself rather than spreading widely through the economy.'

According to the minutes, Lombardelli said oil and gas prices are currently closer to the July adverse scenario. Dhingra said repeated re-escalation of the Middle East conflict has amplified the adverse supply shock.
Brent crude rose to $100.84 a barrel on 6 October 2026. It was up 3.78% over the past month and 54.06% from a year earlier.
UK CPI inflation rose to 3.1% in August 2026 from 2.9% in July, driven mainly by motor fuels. Core CPI was unchanged at 2.6% and services inflation was unchanged at 3.4%.
ING said that if wholesale gas prices stay at current levels, the household energy price cap could rise by about 25% in January.
Bank Rate was also held at 3.75% in June and July 2026. Reports say it was last changed with a cut in December 2025, and there have been no rate increases in 2026 so far.

market.question: Will the upper bound of the federal funds rate be above 4.00% following the Fed's Oct 28, 2026 meeting? (Above 4.00%)
market.rules:
If the upper bound of the target federal funds rate published on the Federal Reserve's official website is greater than 4.00% following the Federal Reserve's Oct 28, 2026 meeting, then the market resolves to Yes.
This market will expire the first 2:05 PM ET following the release of a Federal Reserve statement for their Oct 28, 2026 meeting or one week following the last day of that meeting.

recent_facts.fact: At its September 16, 2026 meeting the FOMC voted 12-0 to raise the federal funds target range by 25 bp to 3.75%–4.00%. The current upper bound is therefore exactly 4.00%, so only a hike at the Oct 27–28 meeting would put it above 4.00%.
The September hike was the first rate increase since 2023.

The September dot plot's median shows one more 25 bp hike by end-2026 (to about 4.1%). Sixteen of 18 participants projected at least one more hike this year, and four projected two. Two FOMC meetings remain in 2026: October 27–28 and December.
The September jobs report showed payrolls up only 29,000, against estimates of more than 80,000. Unemployment rose to 4.2% from 4.1%, and wage growth slowed.

NY Fed President John Williams said there is 'no need for urgency' and that 'one further upward adjustment' may be appropriate late this year. Vice Chair Jefferson said future moves should come from 'carefully examining trends in the data.' Minneapolis Fed's Kashkari said he had no strong view on hiking at the end of October. Dallas Fed's Logan called September's hike a 'first step' but did not say when the next one should come.

Yahoo Finance reported that the weak September jobs report is likely to keep the Fed on hold in October, with attention staying on inflation. The August PCE release on Sept 30 came in cooler than expected, though core PCE was still running at about 3%.

Fed officials including Williams, Barr, Hammack and Paulson said further hikes may be needed because inflation has been above 2% for 5.5 years. Governor Cook pointed to inflation pressure from the AI buildout and from oil prices. Diesel was $6.529/gal, up from $3.739 a year earlier.
September CPI comes out October 14, 2026 at 8:30 AM ET. It is the last CPI report before the October 27–28 FOMC meeting. The prior (August) headline CPI was 3.4% year over year.

market.question: Will **real GDP** increase by more than 4.0% in Q3 2026? (Above 4.0%)
market.rules:
If real GDP (as measured by the BEA’s seasonally adjusted and annualized Advance Estimate) increases by more than 4.0, then the market resolves to Yes.
The market will close at 8:29 AM on the day of the expected release of the data. The market will expire at the first 10:00 AM following the release of the data for Q3 2026, or 3 months following that expected date of data release. Please note the Expiration Value is the one-decimal value published by the BEA.

recent_facts.fact: In BEA's third estimate, Q2 2026 real GDP grew at a 2.2% annual rate. That is 0.7 percentage point higher than the second estimate, which implies the second estimate was about 1.5%. Q1 2026 was revised up 0.4 point to 2.5%.
Real final sales to private domestic purchasers rose 4.6% in Q2 2026, revised up 0.4 point. Consumer spending, investment and exports added to Q2 growth, and imports subtracted from it.
Real PCE rose 0.6% month over month in August 2026, up $92.8 billion, after a 0.1% rise in July. Nominal PCE rose 0.9% ($190.8B): $114.1B on goods and $76.7B on services.
The PCE price index rose 0.3% in August 2026 (core +0.2%). Year over year it was up 3.4% (core 3.0%). Disposable personal income rose 0.3% in August.

recent_facts.source: U.S. Bureau of Economic Analysis / Census Bureau
recent_facts.fact: The August 2026 goods and services trade deficit widened to $105.6B from $92.8B in July (revised). Exports rose $4.5B to $315.2B, and imports rose $17.2B to a record $420.8B. The goods deficit was $136.6B.

recent_facts.source: U.S. Bureau of Economic Analysis / Census Bureau
recent_facts.fact: The three-month average trade deficit rose $9.9B to $89.9B for the period ending in August. Year to date, the deficit is down $138.2B (19.9%) from the same period in 2025.

CNBC reported that the $105.6B August deficit was the widest since just before last year's tariffs took effect. Reuters said economists had expected $102.0B, and that goods imports jumped 5.3% to $342.2B.
Reuters reported that domestic demand grew in Q2 at its fastest pace in more than 3-1/2 years, driven by consumer spending and AI-related business equipment spending.

BEA will release the Q3 2026 GDP advance estimate on Thursday, October 29, 2026, at 8:30 a.m. ET. September personal spending and the advance September goods trade and inventory figures will be available before or with that release.

The question resolves on the advance estimate's seasonally adjusted annualized real GDP growth, rounded to one decimal. It must be above 2.0; exactly 2.0 resolves No. BEA's 2026 annual update has already revised data from Q1 2021 through Q1 2026.

recent_facts.source: Various reposted news items (low-quality mirror sites)
recent_facts.fact: Unverified: low-quality mirror sites report that the Q1 2026 advance estimate was exactly 2.0%, which would not count as above 2.0. In later estimates, Q1 was revised to 2.5%.

AAA's national average gasoline price for September 2026 was $4.33/gal, a September record and 50 cents above the previous September record of $3.83 set in 2023.

AAA's weekly national averages in August 2026 were about $4.06 (Aug 6), $4.07 (Aug 13), $4.10 (Aug 20) and $4.09 (Aug 27). That puts the August level at roughly $4.08, about 6% below the September monthly average of $4.33.

He said inflation is expected to edge up in the coming months and named oil (near US$100/bbl), trade uncertainty and inflation expectations as the factors that could bring the timing of hikes forward.

CIBC argues that Canada's inflation is narrow and mostly driven by fuel: gasoline adds about 0.8 percentage points of the 3% CPI, and only 38% of 55 major CPI components are above 3%. It suggests a Canadian hike could come in 2027 rather than October.

September CPI is due around October 19–20, 2026, before the decision. The Bank of Canada announces its rate decision, together with the October Monetary Policy Report, on October 28, 2026 at 9:45 am ET.

market.rules:
If the seasonally adjusted Consumer Price Index for All Urban Consumers: All Items less Food and Energy for September 2026, as published by the Bureau of Labor Statistics, increases by above 0.2%, then the market resolves to Yes.
Please note that the value of the Underlying is the single-decimal value reported by the BLS.

In the case of a delay in data caused by a federal government shutdown impacting the reliability of the Source Agency, the market’s latest Expiration Date will be extended to the sooner of the release of the Underlying or six months after the end of the government shutdown.

recent_facts.fact: BLS seasonally adjusted core CPI (all items less food and energy) rose 0.3% month over month in August 2026. The 12-month core rate was 2.4%, the lowest since March 2021.

Monthly core CPI changes in 2026: Jan 0.2%, Feb 0.2%, Mar 0.4%, Apr 0.2%, May 0.0%, Jun 0.2%, Jul 0.2%, Aug 0.3%. That is 7 of 8 months above 0.1% and 1 of 8 (May) at 0.1% or lower. This comes from one secondary source and was not checked against BLS directly.
The September 2026 CPI report is scheduled for release on October 14, 2026 at 8:30 a.m. ET, before the Fed's October 27–28 meeting.

Congress passed a continuing resolution (House vote 370–48) funding the federal government through December 11, 2026, and President Trump signed it on September 3. This averted an October 1 shutdown, so no shutdown delay to the BLS release is in place.

In August 2026, shelter rose 0.3% after two straight monthly gains of 0.1% (June and July). Used vehicles rose 0.4% month over month, transportation services rose 0.5%, and medical care services fell 0.2%.
August 2026 headline CPI rose 0.4% month over month (3.4% year over year). Gasoline rose 3.9% and accounted for over a third of the increase. Core's 0.3% came in above the 0.2% consensus.

The mid-September 2026 Manheim Used Vehicle Value Index fell 1.0% from August to 206.2 and was down 0.4% year over year, the first time in 2026 that wholesale used-vehicle prices fell below year-ago levels. Unadjusted wholesale prices fell 1.1% from August.

The question resolves on the one-decimal seasonally adjusted monthly percent change in CPI-U all items less food and energy as published by BLS. A reported 0.2% or higher resolves Yes; 0.1% or lower resolves No.

During the October 1–November 12, 2025 shutdown, BLS delayed the September 2025 CPI from October 15 to October 24 and canceled the October 2025 CPI. This is the only recent case of a shutdown disrupting a CPI release, and no shutdown is in effect for October 2026.

market.question: Will the Democratic Party control the House after the 2026 Midterm elections?
market.rules:
This market will resolve according to the party that wins control of the United States House of Representatives in the 2026 United States midterm election.

A party wins control of the United States House of Representatives if it wins a majority of the chamber’s voting seats. If no party wins a majority of voting seats, the chamber will be deemed controlled by the party with which the first elected Speaker of the House of the Congress that convenes after the 2026 midterm election is affiliated.

The following rules govern the counting of seats for determining which party wins control of the chamber.

All House elections in the 2026 United States midterm election that elect voting members and determine representation in the upcoming 120th Congress are included. Where a seat is decided by a runoff, the runoff result will determine attribution of that seat.

Seats are attributed to the party under which the member was elected. If a member-elect changes party affiliation, or vacates their seat, between election day and the formal organization of Congress, the seat is attributed to the party under which the member was elected.

House members elected as independents who formally caucus with, or, for newly elected members, who announce their intent to caucus with, a party are included in that party’s count. If the caucus decisions of members of the House elected as independents cannot be determined on the date of the election, this market may remain open until the earlier of (i) an announcement from the relevant members of their intents to caucus, or (ii) January 4th, 11:59 PM ET of the following calendar year. If no such announcement is made by January 4th, 11:59 PM ET of the following calendar year, the member will not count towards the seat count of any party.

The resolution sources for this market will be official information from relevant state electoral authorities, the United States Congress, and a consensus of credible reporting.

recent_facts.source: Cook Political Report (via Universe News Network / Axios)
recent_facts.fact: Cook's September 25, 2026 update moved 15 House races toward Democrats, and all 15 moved the same way. Cook now rates 208 seats as favoring Democrats and 205 as favoring Republicans. Of its 22 Toss Ups, 17 are held by Republicans and 5 by Democrats.

recent_facts.source: Cook Political Report (via Universe News Network)
recent_facts.fact: Some Texas seats, including Rep. Monica De La Cruz's district, moved from Likely Republican to Toss Up. According to Cook, Republicans would need to win a majority of the Toss Up races to keep the House.
Decision Desk HQ's polling average shows Democrats ahead of Republicans by about 6 points on the generic ballot, 46% to 40%.

CBS News' House seat estimate shows Democrats keeping their edge for a narrow majority of seats and their lead in national vote preference. CBS attributes this to opposition to Trump administration policies and a Republican base that is less likely to turn out.

As of about October 5, 2026, the House had 218 Republicans, 214 Democrats and 1 independent (Kevin Kiley of California, who caucuses with Republicans), with 2 seats vacant. Democrats need a net gain of 3 districts for a majority; Republicans can lose no more than 2.
A handicapper's seat count cited by Fox News shows Democrats ahead of Republicans 215–201 in projected seats, with 19 races rated Toss Up.

Wikipedia lists the following new maps in effect for 2026 and the seats they are expected to shift: Texas R+5, Ohio R+2, North Carolina R+1, Utah R+1, Florida R+4 (enacted May 4, 2026), Tennessee R+1, Louisiana R+1, Alabama R+1, and California D+5 (Prop 50). Wikipedia's own summary gives the net as 'Republican +12, Democratic +1', which does not match these per-state figures, so treat that summary total as unverified.

Virginia's Democratic redraw, aimed at about D+4, failed. Voters approved it in a referendum on April 21, 2026, but the Virginia Supreme Court struck the amendment down on May 8, and the U.S. Supreme Court denied an emergency appeal on May 15. Missouri's new map (R+1) was blocked for 2026 by a referendum petition.

Louisiana enacted a new map on May 29, 2026, after the Louisiana v. Callais decision, and suspended its primary. New election dates are November 3 and December 12, 2026, so some Louisiana seats may be decided in a December runoff, which counts under the resolution rules.
Election Day is November 3, 2026, and all 435 House seats are up. Both questions close on November 4, 2026 at 04:59 UTC.
Since 1946, the president's party has lost an average of about 25–26 House seats in midterm elections. Its party has gained seats in the House or Senate in only eight midterms in U.S. history.
In Gallup's analysis, presidents with job approval below 50% saw their party lose an average of 37 House seats in midterms, compared with an average loss of 14 seats when approval was above 50%.

facts_dropped.source: Nate Silver Bulletin generic ballot average
facts_dropped.fact: In early October 2026, Democrats led the generic congressional ballot average by about 8–8.9 points (about 51.1% to 43.4% as of Oct 6). This is their highest point of the cycle, and the first time their average has been above 50%.
facts_dropped.reason: cites a forecaster

market.question: 2026 Balance of Power: R Senate, R House
market.rules:
This market will resolve according to the party that wins control of the United States Senate and the party that wins control of the United States House of Representatives in the 2026 United States midterm election.

A party wins control of the United States Senate if it wins a majority of the chamber’s voting seats. If no party wins a majority of voting seats, the party that wins control of the chamber is the party that wins half of the voting seats and holds the Vice Presidency. If the outcome remains ambiguous after applying the above criteria, the chamber will be deemed controlled by the party with which the first selected President Pro Tempore of the Congress that convenes after the specified election is affiliated.

A party wins control of the United States House of Representatives if it wins a majority of the chamber’s voting seats. If no party wins a majority of voting seats, the chamber will be deemed controlled by the party with which the first elected Speaker of the House of the Congress that convenes after the 2026 midterm election is affiliated.

The following rules govern the counting of seats for determining which party wins control of the chambers.

For determining Senate control, all regular and special Senate elections that determine representation in the upcoming 120th Congress and are scheduled to take place in November 2026 as of October 31, 2026 are included. Vacant Senate seats for which no election or special election to fill the seat is scheduled to take place in November 2026 as of October 31, 2026 will be treated as held by the party affiliation of the most recent member to hold that seat. For determining House control, all House elections in the 2026 United States midterm election that elect voting members and determine representation in the upcoming 120th Congress are included. Where a Senate or House seat is decided by a runoff, the runoff result will determine attribution of that seat, even if it takes place after November 2026.

For seats contested in the specified election, seats are attributed to the party under which the member was elected. If a member-elect changes party affiliation, or vacates their seat, between election day and the formal organization of Congress, the seat is attributed to the party under which the member was elected.

market.question: Will the Republicans win the Texas Senate race in 2026?
market.rules:
This market will resolve according to the winner of the 2026 midterm Texas U.S. Senate election, inclusive of any run-offs.

A candidate shall be considered to represent a party in the event that he or she is the nominee of the party in question. Candidates other than the Democratic or Republican nominee (e.g., Greens, Libertarian, independent) may be added at a later date.

Candidates who run as independents will not be encompassed by the “Democrat” or “Republican” options regardless of any affiliation they may have with the party.

The candidates may be named in the contract for the convenience of traders. In the event that any named candidate is replaced as the nominee of their respective party prior to election day, the name in the contract will be updated and the market will resolve based on the replacement nominee of the party.

The resolution source for this market is the Associated Press, Fox News, and NBC. This market will resolve once all three sources call the race for the same candidate. If all three sources haven’t called the race in this state for the same candidate, this market will resolve based on the official certification.

recent_facts.fact: A New York Times/Siena poll of 615 Texas voters, taken Sept. 21–30, 2026, had Democrat James Talarico at 51% and Republican Ken Paxton at 45%, with a margin of error of ±4.5. The same pollster's June 2026 poll had the race tied 47–47.

A Fox News poll of 881 likely voters, taken Sept. 24–28, 2026, had Talarico at 51% and Paxton at 49%, with a margin of error of ±3. Talarico's favorability was 52% favorable to 44% unfavorable; Paxton's was 40% to 58%.

As of Oct. 5, 2026, the RealClearPolitics polling average had Talarico at 48.4% and Paxton at 45.3%, so Talarico was ahead by 3.1 points. About 6% of voters were undecided or backing other candidates.

A recent Texas Southern University poll had Talarico at 47% and Paxton at 46%. A University of Texas/Texas Politics Project poll had Talarico at 42% and Paxton at 39%, leaving a large share undecided. Exact field dates were not confirmed.

AP projected that Attorney General Ken Paxton won the Republican runoff, beating Sen. John Cornyn after President Trump endorsed Paxton the week before. Cornyn had led the March 3 primary but fell short of a majority. Cornyn is the first Republican senator from Texas to lose his party's renomination.

As of early October, ad spending in the race had reached $442 million, making it the second-most expensive non-presidential race in U.S. history. Republicans accounted for $326 million and Democrats for $116 million. In the NYT/Siena poll, 57% disapproved of Trump's job performance, up 5 points from June.

In the Fox News poll, 53% of likely voters said they were concerned Talarico is too liberal and 51% said they were concerned Paxton is too close to Trump. 68% called cost of living extremely important to their vote.

Talarico accepted TV debates on Oct. 6 (WFAA, Dallas) and Oct. 13 (KXAN, Austin). As of late September, Paxton had not committed to any specific debate date, and WFAA reported his campaign had not responded since Aug. 24.

In the same polling cycle, Republican Gov. Greg Abbott led Democrat Gina Hinojosa by 4 points (50–46) in one poll, and another poll showed the governor's race tied. Libertarian Ted Brown also appears in some Senate polls.
Early voting in Texas starts Oct. 19, 2026, and Election Day is Nov. 3, 2026.

In the 2024 Texas Senate race, the final polling average had Ted Cruz up about 3.8 points (49.0 to 45.2), but he won by 8.5 points (53.05% to 44.56%). The polls underestimated the Republican margin by about 4.7 points.

In 2018, final polls mostly had Cruz ahead of Beto O'Rourke by 3 to 6 points (Emerson +3, UT-Tyler +3.6, Quinnipiac +5, Texas Tribune +6). Cruz won by about 2.6 points (51% to 48%), so the Democrat did slightly better than most polls showed.
Texas has not elected a Democrat to any statewide office in about 30 years, since 1994. From memory and unverified: the last Democrat to win a Texas U.S. Senate race was Lloyd Bentsen in 1988.

The question resolves once AP, Fox News and NBC all call the race for the same candidate, and otherwise on official certification. Paxton is the Republican nominee. From memory and unverified: Texas general elections are decided by plurality, with no general-election runoff.

recent_facts.fact: Republicans hold the Senate 53-47; the 47 includes two independents who caucus with Democrats. Democrats need a net gain of four seats for a 51-49 majority. Vice President JD Vance is a Republican, so under the resolution rules a 50-50 split counts as Republican control.

35 Senate seats are up in 2026, including specials in Florida and Ohio; 23 of them are held by Republicans. Cook rates 9 Solid D, 2 Likely D, 1 Lean D, 7 Toss-up, 1 Lean R, 2 Likely R and 13 Solid R. The toss-ups are Alaska, Iowa, Maine, Michigan, New Hampshire, Ohio and Texas.

Cook's most recent update moved Georgia from Lean to Likely Democratic, Kansas from Likely to Lean Republican, and South Carolina from Safe to Likely Republican. Separately, Cook moved Iowa from Lean Republican to Toss-up.

CNN ranks North Carolina (open GOP seat) as the seat most likely to flip. An Elon University/YouGov poll released in September had Democrat Roy Cooper 11 points ahead of Republican Michael Whatley among likely voters.

Ohio special: a New York Times/Siena poll of likely voters from late September had Democrat Sherrod Brown at 49% and Republican Sen. Jon Husted at 46%, within the margin of error. CNN says Brown has led Husted in most polls.

Texas: a Fox News poll of likely voters had Democrat James Talarico at 51% and Republican Ken Paxton at 49%, within the 3-point margin of error. Talarico's favorability was net +8 and Paxton's net -18. A polling average reported alongside had Talarico ahead 48.2% to 45.4%.

Alaska (ranked-choice voting): a NYT/Siena poll of 504 likely voters taken Sept 24–Oct 1 had Democrat Mary Peltola at 50% and Republican Sen. Dan Sullivan at 43%. A Quantus Insights poll had them tied 46-46. An AARP poll had Peltola ahead 46-41 on first choices and 53-47 after ranked-choice tabulation.

recent_facts.source: AARP / Portland Press Herald / CBS News
recent_facts.fact: Maine: an NYT/Press Herald/Siena poll (Sept 24) had Republican Sen. Susan Collins at 49% and Democrat Troy Jackson at 46% (margin ±4.9). An AARP poll had Jackson ahead 50-47, a UNH poll had Jackson ahead 51-47, and a CBS News poll (Oct 2) found the race tied.
Troy Jackson became the Maine Democratic nominee at a nominating convention on July 25, 2026. He replaced Graham Platner, who withdrew in July after sexual assault allegations.

Iowa (open GOP seat): an InsiderAdvantage poll from Sept 22–23 had Democrat Josh Turek at 47% and Republican Ashley Hinson at 46%. A Marist poll had Turek ahead about 50-42. An average of 14 polls had Turek at 46.3 and Hinson at 45.1.

Michigan (open Democratic seat): a Fox News poll had Democrat Abdul El-Sayed at 50% and Republican Mike Rogers at 49% among likely voters, and 51-48 among registered voters. In Fox's August poll Rogers led 51-47. A Mitchell Research poll had El-Sayed ahead 45.6% to 41.4%.

Election day is November 3, 2026. Alaska uses ranked-choice voting, so the result there may take longer than election night. Under the resolution rules, any runoffs, such as a possible Georgia runoff, decide those seats even if held after November.

recent_facts.source: Ripon Society / UCSB American Presidency Project
recent_facts.fact: Since 1934 the president's party has lost an average of 3.4 Senate seats in midterms and has lost Senate seats about two-thirds of the time. It gained seats in 1934, 1998 and 2002. Unverified: these counts come from a secondary summary.

Recent midterms in which Senate control changed include 1994, 2006 and 2014, all moving against the president's party; in 2002 control moved to the president's party. Big Senate midterm losses include 13 seats in 1958, 12 in 1946, 9 in 2014 and 8 in 1986 and 1994. Unverified: this is not a complete count from one source.

market.question: Will Jynxzi, Ron and Los beat the Minecraft challenge by October 10?
market.rules:
Jynxzi, StableRonaldo, and Los Pollos are scheduled to begin a hardcore Minecraft marathon on October 5, 2026. Their goal, as of market creation, is to defeat the Ender Dragon in a hardcore Minecraft world without any of the three dying.

This market will resolve to "Yes" if Jynxzi, StableRonaldo, and Los Pollos defeat the Ender Dragon live on stream, as accepted by them as a successful completion of their challenge, between market creation and the specified date, 11:59 PM ET. Otherwise, this market will resolve to "No".

Only events occurring while at least one of the three players is broadcasting the challenge live will count. Footage of off-stream or previously recorded attempts will not qualify.

If the challenge is cancelled, abandoned before completion, or delayed to a point after the specified date, this market will resolve to "No".

The resolution source for this market will be footage from the official broadcasts of the challenge on Jynxzi's, StableRonaldo's, and Los Pollos's official broadcasts on YouTube and Twitch.

recent_facts.fact: Dexerto reported that the StableRonaldo/Jynxzi/Los Pollos hardcore Minecraft marathon was under way and that the streamers say they won't sleep until they defeat the Ender Dragon. As of 2026-10-06, no source found reports a completion or the current attempt count.
Jynxzi announced the rules for the three-person marathon: Los Pollos must deal the main damage to the Ender Dragon, and enchantments and totems are not allowed.
StableRonaldo posted: 'Tomorrow I will be playing HardCore Minecraft with @jynxzi and @LosPollosTV until we beat it.' This confirms an October 5 start in a stream-until-complete format.
When Jynxzi went over the official rules, Los pushed back, saying: 'You wanna have a 10-day marathon.'
While Los and Jynxzi were discussing the October marathon, Jynxzi realized Los had not played Minecraft in nearly 7 years.

Day 1 of the previous two-person run: 8 hours 14 minutes played, 22 world resets, furthest progress the Nether (no fortress or bastion found), Jynxzi 18 deaths, Ron 7 deaths.

About 32 hours into the previous run (36 combined deaths), Ron died to an Enderman in The End, wiping a near-complete attempt. Full completion took another ~41 hours.
The previous marathon was announced for May 16, but the Day 1 stats are dated about May 29. That suggests the earlier run started later than first announced (inferred from post dates, unverified).

market.question: Will a new pneumonic plague case be confirmed in Russia by October 31?
market.rules:
This market will resolve to "Yes" if a confirmed case of pneumonic plague in a human is reported in the Russian Federation at any point between market creation and the specified date, 11:59 PM Moscow time, . Otherwise, this market will resolve to "No".

A "confirmed case" is a case explicitly identified by a qualifying source as laboratory-confirmed Yersinia pestis infection with pneumonic (pulmonary) involvement, or explicitly announced as a confirmed pneumonic plague case. Publication of the underlying laboratory results is not required. A bubonic or septicemic case that progresses to pneumonic plague qualifies. A case reported only as "plague" with no form specified, and a case described only as suspected or probable, do not qualify.

The case must be distinct from the Irkutsk Anti-Plague Research Institute employee who reportedly passed away on October 1, 2026; subsequent confirmation, reclassification, or post-mortem testing of that patient will not qualify. Resolution turns on the date a qualifying source publishes the confirmation, not the date of exposure, symptom onset, or laboratory result. A report published after the deadline does not count even if the infection occurred earlier.

The primary resolution sources for this market will be official information from Russian federal or regional public health authorities and the WHO; however a consensus of credible sources will also suffice.

market.question: Russia-Ukraine peace talks by October 31, 2026?

The resolution sources for this market will be official information from the governments of Russia and Ukraine, and a consensus of credible reporting.

Renewed Iranian attacks in the Strait of Hormuz pushed Brent crude above $101 a barrel, and risk appetite cooled. Trump reportedly rejected Iran's terms for reopening the strait.
Reports that US spot Bitcoin ETFs recorded fresh outflows ahead of the Fed minutes, alongside $546M in liquidations.
Minutes of the Sept 15–16 FOMC meeting are due at 2:00 p.m. ET on Wed Oct 7. The meeting included a hawkish dissent. The next CPI release is Oct 14, after the Oct 9 settlement.
BTC made a brief move to about $87,000 shortly before Oct 7 but stayed below its 2026 opening price. KuCoin described BTC as stalling under $87,200 before the minutes.
BTC also fell to about $83,000 on Sept 28 as oil climbed back above $100. On Sept 23 it dropped to $85,686, putting the recent range at roughly $83K–$87K.

Unverified aggregate figure: 30-day price volatility is about 3.5%, with 50% green days. A 2.3-day move of about ±2–3% would be ordinary at that level. One source reported a daily move of -2.9% on Oct 7.

market.question: Will Mykola Kuleba win the Nobel Peace Prize in 2026?
market.rules:
This market will resolve according to the winner of the 2026 Nobel Peace Prize, as announced by the Norwegian Nobel Committee.

If multiple listed individuals or entities jointly receive the prize, the market will resolve to a single winner. If Donald Trump, Volodymyr Zelenskyy,  Benjamin Netanyahu, Vladimir Putin, or Elon Musk are among the recipients, the market will resolve to the highest-ranked among them in that exact order of precedence. If none of those five are among the winners and the prize is awarded jointly to at least one listed individual and at least one listed organization, the market will resolve in favor of the individual. If no prioritized individuals are among the winners and all listed recipients are of the same type (all individuals or all organizations), the market will resolve to the person whose last name, or the entity’s name, comes first in alphabetical order as listed in this market.

If no official announcement regarding the 2026 Nobel Peace Prize has been made by March 31, 2027, 11:59 PM ET, this market will resolve to "Other."

The resolution source for this market will be the first official announcement from the Norwegian Nobel Committee.

market.rules: In the upcoming Serie B game between UC Sampdoria and SS Arezzo, scheduled for October 18, 2026 at 1:30 PM ET: This market will resolve based on the final score of the UC Sampdoria vs. SS Arezzo match originally scheduled for October 18, 2026 at 1:30 PM ET, considering only the result at the end of 90 minutes of regulation plus stoppage time; extra time and penalty shoot-outs are excluded. If the actual score is not one of the explicitly listed outcomes, the market resolves to "Any Other Score." If the match is postponed, the market will remain open until it is completed; if it is canceled with no make-up game, the market resolves to "0-0." The primary resolution source for this market is the official statistics of the event as recognized by the governing body or event organizers. However, if the governing body or event organizers have not published final match statistics within 2 hours after the event's conclusion, data from Flashscore may be used; if Flashscore data is unavailable, data from Sofascore may be used; if neither is available, a consensus of credible reporting may be used instead. All markets will settle based on the official final result as recognized by the governing body or event organizers. Revisions to officially declared final scores made after market resolution will not be accounted for in determining the outcome. If no acceptable data is available within 24 hours of the event's conclusion, this market will resolve 50-50, or to "Draw" where applicable.

recent_facts.fact: The Padres beat the Brewers 4-3 in NLDS Game 3 at Petco Park. That ended Milwaukee's sweep attempt, and the Brewers now lead the best-of-five series 2-1. Game 4 is Wednesday night, with Milwaukee either advancing to the NLCS or facing a deciding game.
MLB.com says this is only the 13th postseason series in which each of the first three games was decided by one run. All three Brewers–Padres NLDS games so far have been one-run games.
NLDS Game 4 is Wednesday Oct 7 at 10 p.m. ET (7 p.m. PT) at Petco Park in San Diego, the Padres' home field, on FS1. If San Diego wins, Game 5 is set for Oct 9 in Milwaukee.
The Padres named Walker Buehler (9-6, 4.63 ERA, 32 starts) to start Game 4. He is 32, has not yet pitched this postseason, and this will be his first postseason start for San Diego.

The Brewers have not announced a Game 4 starter. Robert Gasser, Shane Drohan and Chad Patrick are the options, with a combined 45 starts this season, and a bullpen-heavy or opener approach is possible. Ace Jacob Misiorowski is being saved for a possible Game 5 at home.
In Game 3, Padres starter Michael King pitched a six-out save on two days' rest. Closer Mason Miller was put on the paternity list before the game, and reliever Adrian Morejon was unavailable.

MLB.com describes the Padres' bullpen as heavily depleted after Game 3, while Milwaukee has several rested relievers. Hot hitters: Manny Machado (.375, 1.212 OPS) and Xander Bogaerts for San Diego; William Contreras (4-for-11) and Christian Yelich (4-for-10) for Milwaukee.

The Brewers have lost 12 straight postseason road games, which ties the MLB record. Their last postseason road win was in October 2018 at Dodger Stadium, and their all-time postseason road record is 6-24. This is a franchise history fact, not a current-roster sample.
Regular-season records: Milwaukee 103-59 (48-33 on the road) and San Diego 91-71 (51-30 at home).

In Game 3, Milwaukee stranded runners in the fifth, sixth and seventh innings, including a bases-loaded double play in the fifth. Jake Cronenworth then hit a go-ahead solo homer, and the game ended with Yelich grounding into a double play.

In two regular-season games found from August 2026, the Padres beat the Brewers 3-2 on Aug 10 and 11-2 on Aug 12. This is only part of the season series and a small sample; the full season head-to-head was not confirmed.
The Padres reached the NLDS by eliminating the Cubs in the Wild Card Series.

market.question: Will Likud win 30-34 seats in the 2026 Israeli legislative election?
market.rules:
Legislative elections are expected to be held in Israel on October 27, 2026.

This market will resolve according to the number of seats won by the Likud party in the Israeli Knesset as a result of this election.

If the Likud party contests this election as part of a joint candidate list with one or more parties, all seats won by the joint candidate list will be counted. If the Likud party merges with another party prior to the election, all seats won by the resultant merged party, or any joint candidate list through which it contests the election, will be counted.

If the results of this election are not definitively known by October 31, 2027, 11:59 PM ET, this market will resolve to the lowest range bracket.

This market's resolution will be based solely on the number of seats won by the Likud party in this election.

This market will resolve based on the election results, as indicated by a consensus of credible reporting. If there is ambiguity, this market will resolve based solely on the official results as reported by Israel’s Central Election Committee (Va'adet HaBehirot HaMerkazit) (https://www.gov.il/en/departments/central-elections-committee/govil-landing-page).

recent_facts.fact: Between Sep 17 and Oct 5, only one pollster series (Shlomo Filber/Channel 14) had Likud inside 30–34: 31, 32, 31 and 32 seats. Every other pollster had Likud at 18–28 (Direct Polls 27–28; Kantar, Midgam and Tatika 20–21; Maagar Mochot, Lazar and Channel 13 18–19).

recent_facts.fact: Likud is running on its own list with no joint ticket. The page lists 2026 Likud figures ranging from 18–19 at the low end (Lazar/Maariv, Channel 13) to 32–35 at the high end (Channel 14).

recent_facts.source: JPost / search summary of published polls
recent_facts.fact: A five-poll average had Likud at 21.8 seats. A recent i24NEWS poll had Likud first with 27 seats against 22 for Eisenkot's Yashar, and a Channel 13 poll had Likud at 19.

Pollsters gave Likud: Channel 14 32, i24NEWS 27, Zman Yisrael 21, N12 20, Maariv 18, Channel 13 18. Their Netanyahu-bloc totals ran from 49 to 63, and the article attributes the spread partly to differences over Likud's support and over which small parties clear the 3.25% threshold.
A poll published three weeks before the election gave the opposition bloc 54 seats and Netanyahu's coalition 49, so neither side reached the 61 needed for a majority.
A new poll reported that the opposition bloc's refusal to rely on Arab parties gives Netanyahu's bloc an edge over its rivals.

This analysis says Likud trails Eisenkot's Yashar in every poll of the final campaign, with no precedent since 2009 because Likud has always been the largest single party at election time. Channel 14 and i24NEWS polls showing Likud ahead contradict the 'every poll' claim.
Parties submitted their final slates for the October Knesset election. Likud's list is headed by Netanyahu, followed by Eli Cohen, Amir Ohana and Yariv Levin.
The election is on October 27, 2026, and the question closes Oct 28, 03:59 UTC. Final results come from the Central Elections Committee, usually certified about a week after the vote.
Likud won 32 seats in 2022. From memory (unverified), its final poll averages were roughly 30–32 that year, so the result landed close to the average.

market.question: Will the Democrats win the Texas Senate race in 2026?
market.rules:
This market will resolve according to the winner of the 2026 midterm Texas U.S. Senate election, inclusive of any run-offs.

A candidate shall be considered to represent a party in the event that he or she is the nominee of the party in question. Candidates other than the Democratic or Republican nominee (e.g., Greens, Libertarian, independent) may be added at a later date.

Candidates who run as independents will not be encompassed by the “Democrat” or “Republican” options regardless of any affiliation they may have with the party.

The candidates may be named in the contract for the convenience of traders. In the event that any named candidate is replaced as the nominee of their respective party prior to election day, the name in the contract will be updated and the market will resolve based on the replacement nominee of the party.

The resolution source for this market is the Associated Press, Fox News, and NBC. This market will resolve once all three sources call the race for the same candidate. If all three sources haven’t called the race in this state for the same candidate, this market will resolve based on the official certification.

recent_facts.fact: A New York Times/Siena poll of 615 Texas voters, taken Sept. 21–30, 2026, had Democrat James Talarico at 51% and Republican Ken Paxton at 45%, with a margin of error of ±4.5. The same pollster's June 2026 poll had the race tied 47–47.

A Fox News poll of 881 likely voters, taken Sept. 24–28, 2026, had Talarico at 51% and Paxton at 49%, with a margin of error of ±3. Talarico's favorability was 52% favorable to 44% unfavorable; Paxton's was 40% to 58%.

As of Oct. 5, 2026, the RealClearPolitics polling average had Talarico at 48.4% and Paxton at 45.3%, so Talarico was ahead by 3.1 points. About 6% of voters were undecided or backing other candidates.

A recent Texas Southern University poll had Talarico at 47% and Paxton at 46%. A University of Texas/Texas Politics Project poll had Talarico at 42% and Paxton at 39%, leaving a large share undecided. Exact field dates were not confirmed.

AP projected that Attorney General Ken Paxton won the Republican runoff, beating Sen. John Cornyn after President Trump endorsed Paxton the week before. Cornyn had led the March 3 primary but fell short of a majority. Cornyn is the first Republican senator from Texas to lose his party's renomination.

As of early October, ad spending in the race had reached $442 million, making it the second-most expensive non-presidential race in U.S. history. Republicans accounted for $326 million and Democrats for $116 million. In the NYT/Siena poll, 57% disapproved of Trump's job performance, up 5 points from June.

In the Fox News poll, 53% of likely voters said they were concerned Talarico is too liberal and 51% said they were concerned Paxton is too close to Trump. 68% called cost of living extremely important to their vote.

Talarico accepted TV debates on Oct. 6 (WFAA, Dallas) and Oct. 13 (KXAN, Austin). As of late September, Paxton had not committed to any specific debate date, and WFAA reported his campaign had not responded since Aug. 24.

In the same polling cycle, Republican Gov. Greg Abbott led Democrat Gina Hinojosa by 4 points (50–46) in one poll, and another poll showed the governor's race tied. Libertarian Ted Brown also appears in some Senate polls.
Early voting in Texas starts Oct. 19, 2026, and Election Day is Nov. 3, 2026.

In the 2024 Texas Senate race, the final polling average had Ted Cruz up about 3.8 points (49.0 to 45.2), but he won by 8.5 points (53.05% to 44.56%). The polls underestimated the Republican margin by about 4.7 points.

In 2018, final polls mostly had Cruz ahead of Beto O'Rourke by 3 to 6 points (Emerson +3, UT-Tyler +3.6, Quinnipiac +5, Texas Tribune +6). Cruz won by about 2.6 points (51% to 48%), so the Democrat did slightly better than most polls showed.
Texas has not elected a Democrat to any statewide office in about 30 years, since 1994. From memory and unverified: the last Democrat to win a Texas U.S. Senate race was Lloyd Bentsen in 1988.

The question resolves once AP, Fox News and NBC all call the race for the same candidate, and otherwise on official certification. Paxton is the Republican nominee. From memory and unverified: Texas general elections are decided by plurality, with no general-election runoff.

market.question: Will Jynxzi, Ron and Los beat the Minecraft challenge by October 7?
market.rules:
Jynxzi, StableRonaldo, and Los Pollos are scheduled to begin a hardcore Minecraft marathon on October 5, 2026. Their goal, as of market creation, is to defeat the Ender Dragon in a hardcore Minecraft world without any of the three dying.

This market will resolve to "Yes" if Jynxzi, StableRonaldo, and Los Pollos defeat the Ender Dragon live on stream, as accepted by them as a successful completion of their challenge, between market creation and the specified date, 11:59 PM ET. Otherwise, this market will resolve to "No".

Only events occurring while at least one of the three players is broadcasting the challenge live will count. Footage of off-stream or previously recorded attempts will not qualify.

If the challenge is cancelled, abandoned before completion, or delayed to a point after the specified date, this market will resolve to "No".

The resolution source for this market will be footage from the official broadcasts of the challenge on Jynxzi's, StableRonaldo's, and Los Pollos's official broadcasts on YouTube and Twitch.

recent_facts.fact: Dexerto reported that the StableRonaldo/Jynxzi/Los Pollos hardcore Minecraft marathon was under way and that the streamers say they won't sleep until they defeat the Ender Dragon. As of 2026-10-06, no source found reports a completion or the current attempt count.
Jynxzi announced the rules for the three-person marathon: Los Pollos must deal the main damage to the Ender Dragon, and enchantments and totems are not allowed.
StableRonaldo posted: 'Tomorrow I will be playing HardCore Minecraft with @jynxzi and @LosPollosTV until we beat it.' This confirms an October 5 start in a stream-until-complete format.
When Jynxzi went over the official rules, Los pushed back, saying: 'You wanna have a 10-day marathon.'
While Los and Jynxzi were discussing the October marathon, Jynxzi realized Los had not played Minecraft in nearly 7 years.

In the previous two-person run, under similar no-enchantment/no-totem rules, StableRonaldo and Jynxzi beat the Ender Dragon after 73 hours, with 77 total deaths. The winning run was attempt 78 and took about 2 hours.
Day 1 of the previous two-person run: 8 hours 14 minutes played, 22 world resets, furthest progress the Nether (no fortress or bastion found), Jynxzi 18 deaths, Ron 7 deaths.
About 12 hours into the previous run (25 combined deaths), Jynxzi and Ron had already reached The End but died when an explosion hit them while they were destroying a tower.
About 32 hours into the previous run (36 combined deaths), Ron died to an Enderman in The End, wiping a near-complete attempt. Full completion took another ~41 hours.
The previous marathon was announced for May 16, but the Day 1 stats are dated about May 29. That suggests the earlier run started later than first announced (inferred from post dates, unverified).

recent_facts.fact: Reports say Ravens QB Lamar Jackson has a sprained ankle and only an 'outside chance' to play against Atlanta. They say he could miss multiple games, though the injury is not considered long-term or surgical.

On Monday, Ravens head coach Jesse Minter said he did not yet know Jackson's chances of playing Sunday, but did not think the ankle injury would be 'crazy long-term.' Jackson left the locker room in a walking boot and was scheduled for an MRI.

Baltimore beat Tennessee 24-18 on Oct 4. Jackson was 15-of-20 for 222 yards and 2 TDs in the first half, then left with the ankle injury. Backup Tyler Huntley went 8-of-9 for 63 yards in the second half. CB Marlon Humphrey (calf), G Andrew Vorhees (foot) and TE Durham Smythe (Achilles) also left the game and did not return.
The Ravens are 3-1 in 2026. They beat Indianapolis 41-23 (Week 1), lost to New Orleans 17-24 (Week 2), beat Dallas 34-31 (Week 3) and beat Tennessee 24-18 (Week 4).

The Falcons are 2-2. They went 0-2 with Cooper Rush at QB, scoring 16 points total, then 2-0 with Michael Penix Jr., scoring 80 points over those two games. Penix was 15-of-20 for 233 yards and 1 TD in the 45-24 win at New Orleans on Monday, Oct 5.
In the 45-24 win over the Saints, Bijan Robinson ran for 145 yards and 2 TDs, and Brian Robinson Jr. scored 3 rushing TDs. Atlanta never trailed and outrushed New Orleans 205-50.
Falcons LT Jake Matthews was hurt after 11 snaps against the Saints and was ruled out for the rest of the game. One injury listing gave his estimated return date as Oct 11.

recent_facts.source: Sharp Football Analysis IR tracker / CBS Sports
recent_facts.fact: On injured reserve: the Falcons' DL Da'Shawn Hand (quad, eligible to return this week) and CB A.J. Terrell (groin, not eligible until the following week). The Ravens' CB T.J. Tampa (knee) and WR Ja'Kobi Lane (wrist) are both eligible to return this week.

Ravens at Falcons is the Sunday Night Football game on Oct 11, 2026, at 8:20 p.m. ET (00:20 UTC Oct 12) at Mercedes-Benz Stadium in Atlanta, so the Falcons are the home team. Atlanta plays on a short week after its Monday night game, while Baltimore played on Sunday.
The Week 4 win over Tennessee ended Baltimore's four-game home losing streak dating back to the previous season. Minter said the offense would have to adjust if Jackson cannot play against Atlanta.

Finishing Position, Make the Cut, Head-to-Head, and 3-Ball markets will resolve to Fair Market Value

recent_facts.fact: The 2026 Baycurrent Classic runs October 8-11, 2026 at Yokohama Country Club in Japan. The field is 72 players, the purse is $8 million, and it is the third of eight FedExCup Fall events. Schauffele is the defending champion, and Wyndham Clark is in the field.
The event has no cut for its 72 players. Under the market rules, a golfer who withdraws or does not tee off resolves No for Tournament Winner.
No player in the tournament's history (it was the Zozo Championship before the name change) has successfully defended the title. Schauffele is trying to be the first.
Schauffele is world No. 10 and has seven top-10 finishes in 2026. He won the event last year at 19-under, one shot ahead of Max Greyserman.

Schauffele has no win in 2026. He finished 14th in the FedExCup, with a 3rd at The Players Championship and a 2nd at the Rocket Classic. He shot 63 and 64 in rounds on the way to last year's Yokohama win.

Schauffele's recent form: T4 at the Tour Championship, with all four rounds in the 60s at East Lake. At the Presidents Cup he won the clinching point for the U.S. by beating Min Woo Lee in Sunday singles.
Wyndham Clark is world No. 5 and the highest-ranked player in the field. In 2026 he won the CJ Cup Byron Nelson, the U.S. Open and the BMW Championship.
Clark's three wins came in his last 11 starts. He went 1-4 at the 2026 Presidents Cup at Medinah, about two weeks before this event.
Clark's course history at Yokohama: T48 in 2025, and he did not break 70 until a closing 68.

Clark won the 2026 U.S. Open at Shinnecock Hills on June 21 by one shot over Sam Burns, going wire to wire after starting the final round six ahead. Earlier in 2026 his world ranking had fallen as low as 75th.

Other contenders in the field: past winner Collin Morikawa, Justin Thomas, Hideki Matsuyama, Jordan Spieth, Min Woo Lee, Adam Scott, Sungjae Im, Keegan Bradley, and Jacob Bridgeman, who has won twice in 2026, most recently at the Biltmore Championship Asheville.
13 players in the field played in the 2026 Presidents Cup, including Morikawa, Matsuyama and Thomas.
Tom Kim withdrew from the Baycurrent Classic after winning at the Asian Games. Search results showed no withdrawal by Schauffele or Clark.

Unverified, from memory: winners of the event from 2019 to 2025 were Woods, Cantlay, Matsuyama, Bradley, Morikawa, Echavarria and Schauffele. That is 7 different winners in 7 editions, and only 2020, played in California, was away from Japan.

market.question: Perim Island no longer under Houthi control by October 31?
market.rules:
This market will resolve to "Yes" if Perim Island is no longer under Houthi control by the specified date, 11:59 PM ET. Otherwise, this market will resolve to "No".

“The Houthis” refers to the Houthi movement (Ansar Allah), including its governing institutions and any armed force operating under its direction or on its behalf. “Perim Island” refers to Perim (Mayyun) Island in the Bab el-Mandeb Strait, Yemen.

“No longer under the control of the Houthis” means that the Houthis no longer exercise primary military control over Perim Island, and another state, occupying force, the internationally recognized government of Yemen, or an internationally backed authority has established control over the island.

Temporary raids, isolated landings, special operations, bombardment, sabotage, naval presence offshore, or temporary disruption of Houthi activity will not qualify on their own.

An announcement, threat, or claim that the Houthis have lost control will not qualify without actual control being established.

If control changes pursuant to a negotiated settlement, ceasefire term, surrender, or transfer agreement, this will qualify only once actual control has been established on the island.

If control over Perim Island is contested, unclear, disputed, or not sufficiently established by the resolution date, this will not qualify, and the market will resolve to “No”.

The primary resolution source will be official statements from the relevant governments and militaries, along with a consensus of credible reporting.

A candidate shall be considered to represent a party in the event that he or she is the nominee of the party in question. Candidates other than the Democratic or Republican nominee (e.g., Greens, Libertarian, independent) may be added at a later date.

Candidates who run as independents will not be encompassed by the “Democrat” or “Republican” options regardless of any affiliation they may have with the party.

The candidates may be named in the contract for the convenience of traders. In the event that any named candidate is replaced as the nominee of their respective party prior to election day, the name in the contract will be updated and the market will resolve based on the replacement nominee of the party.

The resolution source for this market is the Associated Press, Fox News, and NBC. This market will resolve once all three sources call the race for the same candidate. If all three sources haven’t called the race in this state for the same candidate, this market will resolve based on the official certification.

recent_facts.fact: Change Research's Sept. 25-27 poll had Republican Ashley Moody at 48% and Democrat Angie Nixon at 47%, a 1-point Moody lead. This is the latest general-election poll found.

recent_facts.source: Stetson University Center for Public Opinion Research
recent_facts.fact: Stetson's Sept. 14-21 poll had Moody leading Nixon 51% to 40% in the Senate special election.
InsiderAdvantage's Sept. 20-21 survey had Moody at 49.3% and Nixon at 41.8%, a lead of about 7 points.

recent_facts.source: Political Wire / St. Pete Polls for Florida Politics
recent_facts.fact: A St. Pete Polls survey of 913 likely voters, taken Sept. 15-17, had Moody at 45.2% and Nixon at 44.8%, a statistical tie.
Change Research's Sept. 7-9 poll had Nixon and Moody tied at 47% each.

recent_facts.source: Search summary of political press (Cook Political Report, Sabato's Crystal Ball)
recent_facts.fact: According to press summaries, Cook Political Report and Sabato's Crystal Ball still rate the Florida Senate special election as Solid/Safe Republican.

In the primary, state Rep. Angie Nixon won the Democratic nomination with 56.1%, an upset over the better-funded frontrunner Alex Vindman. Appointed Sen. Ashley Moody won the Republican nomination with about 79.6%.
As of July 31, 2026, Florida had 5.61 million registered Republicans and 4.07 million registered Democrats, a Republican edge of 1.54 million.
Republicans won the last four Florida Senate races: 2016 Rubio by 7.7 points, 2018 Scott by 0.1, 2022 Rubio by 16.4, and 2024 Scott by 12.8. Democrats have not won a Florida Senate race since 2012.
Before the primary, a July University of North Florida poll had Moody leading Nixon 50% to 42%. An earlier Emerson poll had Moody ahead 47% to 36%.
The special election is on November 3, 2026, and the winner serves the rest of Marco Rubio's term through January 2029. Moody (R) and Nixon (D) are the major-party nominees.

The question resolves once AP, Fox News and NBC all call the race for the same candidate; otherwise it resolves on official certification. Florida has no Senate general-election runoff, so the plurality winner takes the seat.

Iowa is 4-1 (1-1 Big Ten) and ranked No. 20 AP / No. 18 Coaches. Results: beat Northern Illinois 40-0, Iowa State 16-13, Northern Iowa (FCS) 55-0 and at No. 18 Michigan 20-19, then lost 14-31 at home to No. 5 Ohio State on Oct. 3.

Iowa starting QB Hank Brown left the Ohio State game injured after throwing for 132 yards with an interception and a fumble, and backup Jeremy Hecklinski finished the game. Kirk Ferentz said the injury isn't believed to be serious, but Brown's status for the short-week Friday game is being monitored. The date is approximate: the article is undated and was published after the Oct. 3 game.

Ferentz gave encouraging early news on three injured Iowa starters from the Ohio State game: QB Hank Brown and defenders Zach Lutmer and Deshaun Lee. Lutmer and Lee were reported as cramping, and none of the three injuries is expected to be serious. The date is approximate, and this comes from a search summary rather than a full read of the article.

Iowa's defense ranks 8th nationally in scoring defense (12.6 points per game) with two shutouts, and Iowa runs for 180.2 yards per game (46th). Hank Brown has completed 62.9% of his passes for 832 yards and 5 TDs through four games.

Ohio State's 31 points ended Iowa's streak of 66 straight games without allowing an opponent 30 or more points. Iowa travels to Seattle on a short week (Saturday to Friday), and this game completes a stretch of Michigan, Ohio State and Washington within about 20 days.

Iowa has won 13 of its last 15 Friday games dating back to 2015 and 3 in a row. It is 4-1 in its last five Friday games, the loss coming 17-20 at UCLA in 2024 (a West Coast road game). The Michigan win in Week 4 was Iowa's first Big Ten road win over a ranked team since 2015.
Iowa leads the all-time series 4-3, but that is a small sample of 7 games. Iowa won the most recent meeting 40-16 in Iowa City in 2024. Iowa's last game in Seattle was a 17-7 win in October 1963.
Washington lost 21-25 at USC after a late USC rally. That was its second straight one-possession Big Ten loss, following 24-27 against Minnesota. The date is approximate (the game was played Oct. 3).

In an early-season report, Washington RBs Quaid Carr (hand surgery) and Jayden Limar (elbow), both hurt in the Washington State game, were ruled out until at least November, and WR Christian Moss was out long-term. WR Rashid Williams (oblique) and CB Emmanuel Karnley (soft tissue) were listed week-to-week. The date is approximate, and their status for Oct. 9 was not confirmed in anything I found.

recent_facts.fact: The Oct 7 game is Game 2 of a best-of-five WNBA semifinal. Golden State leads 1-0 after winning Game 1 71-60 on Oct 4.

Game 2 tips off Wednesday Oct 7 at 9:30pm ET at Chase Center in San Francisco, which is Golden State's home court, so Las Vegas plays away. Game 3 is Oct 9, Game 4 is Oct 11 and Game 5, if needed, is Oct 14.

In Game 1, Gabby Williams had 25 points and 11 rebounds, and Kiah Stokes had 14 rebounds and 4 blocks. Golden State's bench outscored Las Vegas's 27-7, and the Valkyries took a franchise-high 52 rebounds. The Aces shot a season-low 33.9%.
In Game 1, Golden State's biggest lead was 13 points, and Las Vegas never led by more than 3. The Aces' 60 points were their lowest total of the season.
A'ja Wilson scored 24 points on 8-21 shooting with 4 rebounds in 35 minutes in Game 1. She does not appear on the Game 2 injury report.
For Las Vegas, Jewell Loyd (leg) and Stephanie Talbot (leg) were both sidelined during Game 1. Neither was on the Aces' injury report as of Tuesday morning, Oct 6.
After Game 1, Aces coach Becky Hammon said: "We played like ass and only lost by 10."

Las Vegas won all 3 regular-season meetings in 2026, by 19, 5 and 10 points. Game 1 of the semifinal was Golden State's first win over Las Vegas this year. That makes 4 meetings this season, a small sample.
Golden State is the No. 2 seed with a 31-12 regular-season record. Las Vegas, the defending champion, is the No. 3 seed. The Aces' regular-season record was not confirmed.

Both teams needed a deciding Game 3 in the first round. Golden State beat No. 7 Dallas after losing Game 2 108-100 in overtime, when Arike Ogunbowale scored 45. Las Vegas beat No. 6 Indiana after facing elimination.
The Aces have lost Game 1 in five earlier best-of-five series and won three of those series. This is series-level history over 5 cases, not Game 2 results.
Before this semifinal, the Valkyries, an expansion franchise, had only one win over the Aces in their history.

market.question: US-Iran Hormuz Agreement by October 31?
market.rules:
This market will resolve to “Yes” if a diplomatic agreement between the United States and Iran over traffic in the strait of Hormuz is announced by the specified date, 11:59 PM ET.

A diplomatic agreement refers to an official agreement, treaty, deal, or substantially similar diplomatic instrument that establishes agreed actions, policies, obligations, or commitments between the United States and Iran.

A qualifying diplomatic agreement must establish Iranian policies, obligations, or commitments  aimed at permitting, restoring, or increasing vessel or shipping traffic through the Strait of Hormuz.

All listed countries must announce their acceptance of the same qualifying diplomatic agreement for the Payout Condition to be met. A joint announcement will qualify, as will separate announcements from each entity of its own acceptance of an agreement which, taken together, directly indicate that all the listed countries accepted the same agreement. Separate announcements of individual policies will not qualify if the policies are not announced as part of a diplomatic agreement.

Each announcement must be a declarative statement that clearly and unambiguously communicates acceptance of an agreement. Statements that reference ongoing negotiations or a prospective agreement, or that allude to or express support for an agreement without confirming acceptance of the agreement, do not qualify. A qualifying announcement need not reference the agreement by name or use specific terminology, provided it clearly communicates acceptance of an agreement.
 
Whether announcements from the listed countries represent a diplomatic agreement and whether such an agreement qualifies will be primarily determined through the announcements themselves. Where an announcement is made by all listed countries but, based on the announcements, it remains ambiguous whether the announcements represent a qualifying diplomatic agreement between the countries, this market will remain open until either i) definitive confirmation that the announcements represent a qualifying diplomatic agreement between the listed entities is achieved through further announcements from the listed countries or a consensus of credible reporting or ii) 14 calendar days (ET) have passed after the date that the last country made their first potentially qualifying announcement. If, at the end of the fourteenth calendar day, no definitive confirmation has been achieved, this market will resolve based on the totality of information available from the resolution sources at that time. market.question: 2026 Balance of Power: R Senate, D House
market.rules:
This market will resolve according to the party that wins control of the United States Senate and the party that wins control of the United States House of Representatives in the 2026 United States midterm election.

A party wins control of the United States Senate if it wins a majority of the chamber’s voting seats. If no party wins a majority of voting seats, the party that wins control of the chamber is the party that wins half of the voting seats and holds the Vice Presidency. If the outcome remains ambiguous after applying the above criteria, the chamber will be deemed controlled by the party with which the first selected President Pro Tempore of the Congress that convenes after the specified election is affiliated.

A party wins control of the United States House of Representatives if it wins a majority of the chamber’s voting seats. If no party wins a majority of voting seats, the chamber will be deemed controlled by the party with which the first elected Speaker of the House of the Congress that convenes after the 2026 midterm election is affiliated.

The following rules govern the counting of seats for determining which party wins control of the chambers.

For determining Senate control, all regular and special Senate elections that determine representation in the upcoming 120th Congress and are scheduled to take place in November 2026 as of October 31, 2026 are included. Vacant Senate seats for which no election or special election to fill the seat is scheduled to take place in November 2026 as of October 31, 2026 will be treated as held by the party affiliation of the most recent member to hold that seat. For determining House control, all House elections in the 2026 United States midterm election that elect voting members and determine representation in the upcoming 120th Congress are included. Where a Senate or House seat is decided by a runoff, the runoff result will determine attribution of that seat, even if it takes place after November 2026.

For seats contested in the specified election, seats are attributed to the party under which the member was elected. If a member-elect changes party affiliation, or vacates their seat, between election day and the formal organization of Congress, the seat is attributed to the party under which the member was elected. 

For seats not contested in the specified election, seats are attributed to the party that holds the seat as of the date of the election. If a current sitting member of the U.S. Senate who is not up for election changes party affiliation or vacates their seat after the date of the election, the seat is attributed to the party under which the member was affiliated at the time of the election.

Senate and House members elected as independents who formally caucus with, or, for newly elected members, who announce their intent to caucus with, a party are included in that party’s count. If the caucus decisions of members of the Senate or House elected as independents cannot be determined on the date of the election, this market may remain open until the earlier of (i) an announcement from the relevant members of their intents to caucus, or (ii) January 4th, 11:59 PM ET of the following calendar year. If no such announcement is made by January 4th, 11:59 PM ET of the following calendar year, the member will not count towards the seat count of any party.

The resolution sources for this market will be official information from relevant state electoral authorities, the United States Congress, and a consensus of credible reporting.

market.question: Will Student List – Students Win win the most seats in the 2026 Serbian parliamentary election?
market.rules:
Parliamentary elections to elect the 250 members of the National Assembly of Serbia are scheduled to take place on October 25, 2026.

This market will resolve to the electoral list that wins the greatest number of seats in the National Assembly of Serbia as a result of this election.

Electoral lists will be primarily ranked by the number of seats won in the specified election. If two or more lists are tied on seats, ties will be broken by the total number of valid votes received, with higher vote totals ranking higher. If lists remain tied, ties will be broken by alphabetical order of the listed names. This market will resolve to the list that occupies the highest finishing position after applying this ranking.

This market's resolution will be based solely on the number of seats won by the named electoral list, as it appears on the ballot and official proclamations, regardless of which parties make up the list or how its members later organize themselves in the National Assembly.

If the results of the specified election are not definitively known by March 31, 2027, 11:59 PM ET, this market will resolve to "Other".

This market will resolve based on the results of the elections, as indicated by a consensus of credible reporting. In the case of ambiguity, this market will resolve solely based on the results as reported by the Republic Electoral Commission of Serbia (https://www.rik.parlament.gov.rs/).

recent_facts.fact: In CRTA's poll, fielded 13–27 September 2026, 44% of citizens backed the Student List and 32% backed the Vučić-led bloc (United Serbia). These shares appear to be of the whole sample, not only of decided voters.

In Faktor Plus's September poll, the Student List rose 5.6 points from the previous poll and United Serbia rose 1.4 points. Faktor Plus's director said the opposition vote had consolidated because the People's Movement of Serbia, Ecological Uprising and New Face of Serbia had withdrawn from the race.
Faktor Plus's previous poll had SNS/United Serbia at 47.2% and the Student List at 31.5%.

An earlier CRTA/Stanford Democracy Action Lab face-to-face poll of 2,324 adults, fielded from 10 June, found 44.9% of decided voters (about 70% of the sample) for the Student List, 35.7% for SNS and 3.8% for SPS, with all others below the threshold. The article date is unconfirmed. Vučić publicly rejected CRTA's findings as propaganda.

The main lists on the ballot are: 1 'Aleksandar Vučić – United Serbia' (SNS-led); 2 'Ivica Dačić – Factor of Stability' (SPS, JS, SDPS, Zeleni); 3 'Student List – Students Are Winning' (ballot carrier Ilija Srdanović); 8 'Authentic Right – Dr. Miloš Jovanović' (NADA); 9 'European Serbia' (SSP and SRCE, led by Tepić and Ponoš). Wikipedia says polls are split, with some putting SNS first and others putting the Student List first.

DS, Green–Left Front, PSG (which left the Platform for European Serbia), New Face of Serbia and Ecological Uprising endorsed the Student List. SSP/SRCE (European Serbia) and NADA are running their own lists, so the opposition vote is split across several lists.
Vučić said he would resign as president on 27 September to campaign as the head of the United Serbia list. SNS nominated him as its candidate for prime minister.

All 250 seats are elected by closed-list proportional representation in one nationwide constituency, allocated by the D'Hondt method. There is a 3% threshold, which does not apply to ethnic-minority lists, and 126 seats is a majority. Because seats closely follow vote share among lists that pass the threshold, the list with the most votes would almost certainly also win the most seats.
16 lists are officially registered for the 25 October election: 17 were submitted, 1 was withdrawn and 1 was cancelled by the Republic Electoral Commission (RIK). Five of the 16 have minority status.

The early election was called on 9 September 2026 and will be held on 25 October 2026. The OSCE/ODIHR and CeSID will observe it, and TV debates are running on N1, RTS, Nova and Insajder through late September and October.

CRTA accused Vučić of trying to discredit it as an election observer and as a witness to possible fraud. The article date is unconfirmed. Separately, monitors report that Student List leader Ilija Srdanović has had no live appearances on national-coverage TV channels since 15 September.

Unverified, partly from memory: an SNS-led list won the most seats in each Serbian parliamentary election from 2012 to 2023 (2012, 2014, 2016, 2020, 2022, 2023, so 6 of 6). In December 2023 it won about 46.7% against about 23.6% for Serbia Against Violence.

market.question: Israeli airspace closed by October 31, 2026?
market.rules:
This market will resolve to “Yes” if Israeli Airspace (The Tel Aviv Flight Information Region (FIR)/LLLL) is closed between market creation and the specified date, 11:59 PM ET. Otherwise, this market will resolve to “No”.

A qualifying closure occurs when the aviation or governmental authority responsible for overseeing the specified airspace region issues a Notice to Airmen (NOTAM), or other official order under the regulations of the jurisdiction responsible for that airspace region, which generally cancels or suspends commercial aviation across the specified airspace region, and such closure is not excluded under the exclusions provision below. A qualifying closure must apply generally to commercial flights transiting, arriving in, and departing from the specified airspace region. A closure is not disqualified because the order permits limited exceptions, including humanitarian, medical, repatriation, or emergency flights, or select flights authorized by the responsible authority, provided that commercial flights are prohibited by default, rather than permitted subject to conditions or restrictions.
