recent_facts.fact: This is a 2026 Week 5 game: the 49ers (4-0) play at the Seattle Seahawks (3-1) at Lumen Field in Seattle, and FOX has the broadcast. The kickoff listed elsewhere is Sunday, Oct 11, at 1:25 p.m. PT (4:25 p.m. ET).

Season team stats: the 49ers score 30.5 points per game (2nd) and gain 389 yards per game (7th), with 6 sacks (26th), 1 interception (25th) and a +1 turnover differential. The Seahawks score 26.2 points per game (10th) and gain 347.3 yards per game (13th), with 11 sacks (7th), 6 interceptions (1st) and a +3 turnover differential (4th).

Team leaders: Brock Purdy has 1,007 passing yards, 11 TD and 1 INT, Christian McCaffrey has 218 rushing yards and 4 TD, and George Kittle has 244 receiving yards and 4 TD. For Seattle, Sam Darnold is listed at 560 passing yards, 6 TD and 3 INT; this conflicts with a Fox box score that has him at 379 yards in Week 3 alone. Jaxon Smith-Njigba has 481 receiving yards and 6 TD.

Shanahan said DL Nick Bosa and DL James Thompson Jr. are not expected back this week. FB Kyle Juszczyk has a knee bone bruise and will miss a few weeks. S Marques Sigle has a high ankle sprain and will miss time, and DB Upton Stout has an AC shoulder sprain and is day-to-day.

DL Mykel Williams (knee) did some team drills and could be activated at the end of the week. WR Mike Evans played through a rib injury in Week 4, catching 5 passes, with no setback reported. DL Romello Height returned while playing with a club on his hand.

recent_facts.source: ESPN (Seahawks injuries page, via search summary)
recent_facts.fact: Seahawks LB Chazz Surratt and S Ty Okada are listed as questionable. Coach Mike Macdonald expects DL Leonard Williams (ankle) to be available. RB Zach Charbonnet (reserve/PUP) won't be activated for this game, and first-round RB Jadarian Price is on IR with a chest injury.

In Week 4 the 49ers beat Denver 24-14 while missing core front-seven starters, and some secondary players left mid-game. Seattle beat the Chargers 30-23 at home, with Emanuel Wilson gaining 120 rushing yards and scoring 2 TDs, but the Seahawks also had a franchise-record 150 penalty yards.

The 49ers' 2026 results: Week 1, beat the Rams 27-7 in Melbourne; Week 2, beat Miami 35-13 at home; Week 3, beat Arizona 36-30 at home after giving up much of a big lead; Week 4, beat Denver 24-14. Their only road game so far was the neutral-site game in Melbourne.

The Seahawks' 2026 results: Week 1, beat New England 13-10 at home; Week 2, won 31-7 at Arizona with Drew Lock starting; Week 3, lost 33-31 at Washington, whose QB was backup Marcus Mariota; Week 4, beat the Chargers 30-23 at home. Darnold threw for 379 yards, 4 TD and 2 INT in the Week 3 loss.

Darnold suffered a short-term glute soft-tissue injury on Seattle's opening drive of Week 1 and missed Week 2. He came back to start in Weeks 3 and 4. No Week 5 injury designation for him turned up in searches.

Seattle won the last two meetings, 13-3 at San Francisco on Jan 3, 2026 and 41-6 at Seattle in the divisional round on Jan 17, 2026. The 49ers won the 2025 opener 17-13 at Seattle on Sep 7, 2025. Wikipedia lists the all-time series as Seahawks 33-24. Seattle is the defending Super Bowl champion.
The 49ers practice Wednesday, Oct 7, and official injury reports and game designations come out during the week, with final statuses on Friday. Kickoff is Sunday, Oct 11, at 1:25 p.m. PT.

recent_facts.fact: The Eagles are 2-2. They lost 24-20 at home to the Rams on Oct 4 after leading 20-10 at halftime and lost 27-7 at Chicago the week before. Their two wins were over Tennessee and Washington.
The Jaguars are 3-1. They won 22-17 at Cincinnati on Oct 4 and beat the Patriots 35-6 on Sept 27.

Starting right tackle Lane Johnson announced his immediate retirement on Tuesday, Oct 6. On Wednesday, Oct 7, the Eagles traded center Cam Jurgens, who is in the concussion protocol, to Baltimore. With LG Landon Dickerson on IR, Philadelphia is missing three of the offensive line starters it opened the season with, and Drew Kendall is expected to play center.

Philadelphia could be without up to six offensive starters. RB Saquon Barkley hurt his hamstring in Week 4 and NFL Network reports he is week-to-week. WR DeVonta Smith (hamstring) could miss multiple games, TE Dallas Goedert (knee) has missed two straight games, RB Tank Bigsby is going to IR after core muscle surgery, and backup RT Fred Johnson (knee) missed Week 4.
WR Hollywood Brown (ankle) has missed two straight games with no clear timeline. DE Jonathan Greenard (ankle) is listed as day-to-day.
Against the Rams, Jalen Hurts went 12-of-27 for 93 yards with 2 TDs. The Eagles gained 172 total yards, went 0-for-12 on third down and 1-of-4 on fourth down, and did not score in the second half.
Against Cincinnati, Trevor Lawrence threw for 227 yards and a TD to Brian Thomas Jr. NextGenStats had him pressured on 8 dropbacks, 4 of which ended in sacks.

recent_facts.source: CBS Sports / ESPN injury pages (via search summary)
recent_facts.fact: Jaguars injuries: S Caleb Ransaw (knee) went to IR on Tuesday. CB Christian Braswell (knee) and S Eric Murray (concussion) are listed as questionable. Patrick Mekari, Sam Mustipher and BJ Green II are on IR.

The game is Sunday, Oct 11, 2026, at 9:30 a.m. ET on NFL Network, at Tottenham Hotspur Stadium in London. It is a neutral site, although Jacksonville is the designated home team (PFR lists it as 'at Jacksonville').
Jacksonville plays back-to-back games in London, and this is the first of the two. The Eagles' official Week 5 injury report designations are still to come and are expected by Friday.

recent_facts.fact: In the 12 months to August 2026, the CPI-U all-items index rose 3.4% (not seasonally adjusted), the same rate as for the 12 months to July. The NSA index was 334.980 in August 2026, up 0.3% from July before seasonal adjustment. On a seasonally adjusted basis it rose 0.4%.

The September 2025 CPI-U NSA index was 324.800, and August 2025 was 323.976, so September 2025 rose about 0.25% NSA month over month. My own calculation: a published 12-month rate above 3.6% (3.7% or higher after rounding, i.e. at least 3.65%) needs a September 2026 index of about 336.66 or more. That is roughly a +0.50% NSA rise from August's 334.980. A rise of about +0.40% NSA (index about 336.33) would round to 3.6%.
BLS will release September 2026 CPI on Wednesday, October 14, 2026, at 8:30 a.m. ET.

AAA put the September 2026 national average gasoline price at $4.33/gal, a record for September and 50 cents above the previous September record of $3.83 (2023). The national average peaked at $4.48 on September 24 and was $4.41 by October 1.

Through August 20, AAA's August 2026 national average gasoline price was $4.06/gal. Daily readings were about $4.07 on August 13 and $4.09 on August 27. If the full August average was around $4.06–4.09, September's $4.33 would be roughly a 6–7% month-over-month rise in retail gasoline.

EIA's weekly U.S. regular gasoline price was $4.319 on September 14, $4.478 on September 21 and $4.465 on September 28, 2026. The September 28 price was about $1.35 higher than a year earlier. Third-party sites reported early-September EIA readings of about $4.07–4.29, which don't line up cleanly with each other.

In August 2026, energy was up 16.3% over 12 months and gasoline up 27.4%. Gasoline rose 3.9% seasonally adjusted (2.5% NSA) in August. Natural gas fell 1.1% and electricity fell 0.2% on the month. Core CPI was up 2.4% year over year.
Headline CPI inflation was 3.4% year over year in August 2026, after a 0.1% seasonally adjusted rise in July and 0.4% in August. Gasoline accounted for more than a third of August's monthly increase.

AAA said the national gas average reached $4.48/gal on September 24, 2026, the highest ever for that time of year. It attributed the rise to volatility in the Strait of Hormuz and high crude oil prices.

The market resolves based on the CF Bitcoin Real-Time Index (BRTI) using a trimmed mean calculation. The resolution value is calculated by taking all BRTI values for each minute from market issuance until the specified time on the target date, removing the top 20% and bottom 20% of values, then averaging the remaining 60% of values. If the BRTI crosses the threshold at any point during the measurement period (triggering early expiration), the market immediately resolves. If no data is available at the expiration time, the market resolves to No. The market can resolve early if Bitcoin definitively crosses the threshold before the target date and time.

Disclosed spending on the race is over $205 million. Since the start of 2025, Rogers and groups backing him have outspent El-Sayed and his allies by almost 2 to 1. For October, Republicans plan to spend more than $43 million, against about $25 million in Democratic reservations.

A CNN headline from Oct 7 reads: 'Abdul El-Sayed is certain he'll win Michigan's Senate race. Some key Democrats quietly aren't so sure.' The article body could not be retrieved.

Republicans have not won a U.S. Senate race in Michigan since 1994. Democrats won every Michigan Senate race from 1996 through 2024.

market.question: Will the Democratic Party control the Senate after the 2026 Midterm elections?
market.rules:
This market will resolve according to the party that wins control of the United States Senate in the 2026 United States midterm election.

A party wins control of the United States Senate if it wins a majority of the chamber’s voting seats. If no party wins a majority of voting seats, the party that wins control of the chamber is the party that wins half of the voting seats and holds the Vice Presidency. If the outcome remains ambiguous after applying the above criteria, the chamber will be deemed controlled by the party with which the first selected President Pro Tempore of the Congress that convenes after the specified election is affiliated.

The following rules govern the counting of seats for determining which party wins control of the chamber.

All regular and special Senate elections that determine representation in the upcoming 120th Congress and are scheduled to take place in November 2026 as of October 31, 2026 are included. Runoffs for qualifying elections will determine attribution of the relevant seat, even if they take place after November 2026. Vacant seats for which no election or special election to fill the seat is scheduled to take place in November 2026 as of October 31, 2026 will be treated as held by the party affiliation of the most recent member to hold that seat.

For seats contested in the specified election, seats are attributed to the party under which the member was elected. If a member-elect changes party affiliation, or vacates their seat, between election day and the formal organization of Congress, the seat is attributed to the party under which the member was elected.

For seats not contested in the specified election, seats are attributed to the party that holds the seat as of the date of the election. If a current sitting member of the U.S. Senate who is not up for election changes party affiliation or vacates their seat after the date of the election, the seat is attributed to the party under which the member was affiliated at the time of the election.

Senate members elected as independents who formally caucus with, or, for newly elected members, who announce their intent to caucus with, a party are included in that party’s count. If the caucus decisions of members of the Senate elected as independents cannot be determined on the date of the election, this market may remain open until the earlier of (i) an announcement from the relevant members of their intents to caucus, or (ii) January 4th, 11:59 PM ET of the following calendar year. If no such announcement is made by January 4th, 11:59 PM ET of the following calendar year, the member will not count towards the seat count of any party.

The resolution sources for this market will be official information from relevant state electoral authorities, the United States Congress, and a consensus of credible reporting.

recent_facts.fact: In the 12 months to August 2026, the CPI-U all-items index rose 3.4% (not seasonally adjusted), the same rate as for the 12 months to July. The NSA index was 334.980 in August 2026, up 0.3% from July before seasonal adjustment. On a seasonally adjusted basis it rose 0.4%.

The September 2025 CPI-U NSA index was 324.800, and August 2025 was 323.976, so September 2025 rose about 0.25% NSA month over month. My own calculation: a published 12-month rate above 3.6% (3.7% or higher after rounding, i.e. at least 3.65%) needs a September 2026 index of about 336.66 or more. That is roughly a +0.50% NSA rise from August's 334.980. A rise of about +0.40% NSA (index about 336.33) would round to 3.6%.
BLS will release September 2026 CPI on Wednesday, October 14, 2026, at 8:30 a.m. ET.

AAA put the September 2026 national average gasoline price at $4.33/gal, a record for September and 50 cents above the previous September record of $3.83 (2023). The national average peaked at $4.48 on September 24 and was $4.41 by October 1.

Through August 20, AAA's August 2026 national average gasoline price was $4.06/gal. Daily readings were about $4.07 on August 13 and $4.09 on August 27. If the full August average was around $4.06–4.09, September's $4.33 would be roughly a 6–7% month-over-month rise in retail gasoline.

EIA's weekly U.S. regular gasoline price was $4.319 on September 14, $4.478 on September 21 and $4.465 on September 28, 2026. The September 28 price was about $1.35 higher than a year earlier. Third-party sites reported early-September EIA readings of about $4.07–4.29, which don't line up cleanly with each other.

In August 2026, energy was up 16.3% over 12 months and gasoline up 27.4%. Gasoline rose 3.9% seasonally adjusted (2.5% NSA) in August. Natural gas fell 1.1% and electricity fell 0.2% on the month. Core CPI was up 2.4% year over year.
Headline CPI inflation was 3.4% year over year in August 2026, after a 0.1% seasonally adjusted rise in July and 0.4% in August. Gasoline accounted for more than a third of August's monthly increase.

AAA said the national gas average reached $4.48/gal on September 24, 2026, the highest ever for that time of year. It attributed the rise to volatility in the Strait of Hormuz and high crude oil prices.

market.question: Will CPI Core rise more than 0.2% in September? (Above 0.2%)
market.rules:
If the seasonally adjusted Consumer Price Index for All Urban Consumers: All Items less Food and Energy for September 2026, as published by the Bureau of Labor Statistics, increases by above 0.2%, then the market resolves to Yes.
Please note that the value of the Underlying is the single-decimal value reported by the BLS.

In the case of a delay in data caused by a federal government shutdown impacting the reliability of the Source Agency, the market’s latest Expiration Date will be extended to the sooner of the release of the Underlying or six months after the end of the government shutdown.

recent_facts.fact: BLS seasonally adjusted core CPI (all items less food and energy) rose 0.3% month over month in August 2026. The 12-month core rate was 2.4%, the lowest since March 2021.

Monthly core CPI changes in 2026: Jan 0.2%, Feb 0.2%, Mar 0.4%, Apr 0.2%, May 0.0%, Jun 0.2%, Jul 0.2%, Aug 0.3%. That is 7 of 8 months above 0.1% and 1 of 8 (May) at 0.1% or lower. This comes from one secondary source and was not checked against BLS directly.
The September 2026 CPI report is scheduled for release on October 14, 2026 at 8:30 a.m. ET, before the Fed's October 27–28 meeting.

Congress passed a continuing resolution (House vote 370–48) funding the federal government through December 11, 2026, and President Trump signed it on September 3. This averted an October 1 shutdown, so no shutdown delay to the BLS release is in place.

In August 2026, shelter rose 0.3% after two straight monthly gains of 0.1% (June and July). Used vehicles rose 0.4% month over month, transportation services rose 0.5%, and medical care services fell 0.2%.
August 2026 headline CPI rose 0.4% month over month (3.4% year over year). Gasoline rose 3.9% and accounted for over a third of the increase. Core's 0.3% came in above the 0.2% consensus.

The mid-September 2026 Manheim Used Vehicle Value Index fell 1.0% from August to 206.2 and was down 0.4% year over year, the first time in 2026 that wholesale used-vehicle prices fell below year-ago levels. Unadjusted wholesale prices fell 1.1% from August.

The question resolves on the one-decimal seasonally adjusted monthly percent change in CPI-U all items less food and energy as published by BLS. A reported 0.2% or higher resolves Yes; 0.1% or lower resolves No.

During the October 1–November 12, 2025 shutdown, BLS delayed the September 2025 CPI from October 15 to October 24 and canceled the October 2025 CPI. This is the only recent case of a shutdown disrupting a CPI release, and no shutdown is in effect for October 2026.

market.question: Will the Democratic Party control the House after the 2026 Midterm elections?
market.rules:
This market will resolve according to the party that wins control of the United States House of Representatives in the 2026 United States midterm election.

A party wins control of the United States House of Representatives if it wins a majority of the chamber’s voting seats. If no party wins a majority of voting seats, the chamber will be deemed controlled by the party with which the first elected Speaker of the House of the Congress that convenes after the 2026 midterm election is affiliated.

The following rules govern the counting of seats for determining which party wins control of the chamber.

All House elections in the 2026 United States midterm election that elect voting members and determine representation in the upcoming 120th Congress are included. Where a seat is decided by a runoff, the runoff result will determine attribution of that seat.

Seats are attributed to the party under which the member was elected. If a member-elect changes party affiliation, or vacates their seat, between election day and the formal organization of Congress, the seat is attributed to the party under which the member was elected.

House members elected as independents who formally caucus with, or, for newly elected members, who announce their intent to caucus with, a party are included in that party’s count. If the caucus decisions of members of the House elected as independents cannot be determined on the date of the election, this market may remain open until the earlier of (i) an announcement from the relevant members of their intents to caucus, or (ii) January 4th, 11:59 PM ET of the following calendar year. If no such announcement is made by January 4th, 11:59 PM ET of the following calendar year, the member will not count towards the seat count of any party.

The resolution sources for this market will be official information from relevant state electoral authorities, the United States Congress, and a consensus of credible reporting.

recent_facts.source: Cook Political Report (via Universe News Network / Axios)
recent_facts.fact: Cook's September 25, 2026 update moved 15 House races toward Democrats, and all 15 moved the same way. Cook now rates 208 seats as favoring Democrats and 205 as favoring Republicans. Of its 22 Toss Ups, 17 are held by Republicans and 5 by Democrats.

recent_facts.source: Cook Political Report (via Universe News Network)
recent_facts.fact: Some Texas seats, including Rep. Monica De La Cruz's district, moved from Likely Republican to Toss Up. According to Cook, Republicans would need to win a majority of the Toss Up races to keep the House.
Decision Desk HQ's polling average shows Democrats ahead of Republicans by about 6 points on the generic ballot, 46% to 40%.

CBS News' House seat estimate shows Democrats keeping their edge for a narrow majority of seats and their lead in national vote preference. CBS attributes this to opposition to Trump administration policies and a Republican base that is less likely to turn out.

As of about October 5, 2026, the House had 218 Republicans, 214 Democrats and 1 independent (Kevin Kiley of California, who caucuses with Republicans), with 2 seats vacant. Democrats need a net gain of 3 districts for a majority; Republicans can lose no more than 2.
A handicapper's seat count cited by Fox News shows Democrats ahead of Republicans 215–201 in projected seats, with 19 races rated Toss Up.

Wikipedia lists the following new maps in effect for 2026 and the seats they are expected to shift: Texas R+5, Ohio R+2, North Carolina R+1, Utah R+1, Florida R+4 (enacted May 4, 2026), Tennessee R+1, Louisiana R+1, Alabama R+1, and California D+5 (Prop 50). Wikipedia's own summary gives the net as 'Republican +12, Democratic +1', which does not match these per-state figures, so treat that summary total as unverified.

Virginia's Democratic redraw, aimed at about D+4, failed. Voters approved it in a referendum on April 21, 2026, but the Virginia Supreme Court struck the amendment down on May 8, and the U.S. Supreme Court denied an emergency appeal on May 15. Missouri's new map (R+1) was blocked for 2026 by a referendum petition.

Louisiana enacted a new map on May 29, 2026, after the Louisiana v. Callais decision, and suspended its primary. New election dates are November 3 and December 12, 2026, so some Louisiana seats may be decided in a December runoff, which counts under the resolution rules.
Election Day is November 3, 2026, and all 435 House seats are up. Both questions close on November 4, 2026 at 04:59 UTC.
Since 1946, the president's party has lost an average of about 25–26 House seats in midterm elections. Its party has gained seats in the House or Senate in only eight midterms in U.S. history.
In Gallup's analysis, presidents with job approval below 50% saw their party lose an average of 37 House seats in midterms, compared with an average loss of 14 seats when approval was above 50%.

facts_dropped.source: Nate Silver Bulletin generic ballot average
facts_dropped.fact: In early October 2026, Democrats led the generic congressional ballot average by about 8–8.9 points (about 51.1% to 43.4% as of Oct 6). This is their highest point of the cycle, and the first time their average has been above 50%.

market.question: 2026 Balance of Power: D Senate, D House
market.rules:
This market will resolve according to the party that wins control of the United States Senate and the party that wins control of the United States House of Representatives in the 2026 United States midterm election.

A party wins control of the United States Senate if it wins a majority of the chamber’s voting seats. If no party wins a majority of voting seats, the party that wins control of the chamber is the party that wins half of the voting seats and holds the Vice Presidency. If the outcome remains ambiguous after applying the above criteria, the chamber will be deemed controlled by the party with which the first selected President Pro Tempore of the Congress that convenes after the specified election is affiliated.

A party wins control of the United States House of Representatives if it wins a majority of the chamber’s voting seats. If no party wins a majority of voting seats, the chamber will be deemed controlled by the party with which the first elected Speaker of the House of the Congress that convenes after the 2026 midterm election is affiliated.

The following rules govern the counting of seats for determining which party wins control of the chambers.

For determining Senate control, all regular and special Senate elections that determine representation in the upcoming 120th Congress and are scheduled to take place in November 2026 as of October 31, 2026 are included. Vacant Senate seats for which no election or special election to fill the seat is scheduled to take place in November 2026 as of October 31, 2026 will be treated as held by the party affiliation of the most recent member to hold that seat. For determining House control, all House elections in the 2026 United States midterm election that elect voting members and determine representation in the upcoming 120th Congress are included. Where a Senate or House seat is decided by a runoff, the runoff result will determine attribution of that seat, even if it takes place after November 2026.

For seats contested in the specified election, seats are attributed to the party under which the member was elected. If a member-elect changes party affiliation, or vacates their seat, between election day and the formal organization of Congress, the seat is attributed to the party under which the member was elected. 

For seats not contested in the specified election, seats are attributed to the party that holds the seat as of the date of the election. If a current sitting member of the U.S. Senate who is not up for election changes party affiliation or vacates their seat after the date of the election, the seat is attributed to the party under which the member was affiliated at the time of the election.

Senate and House members elected as independents who formally caucus with, or, for newly elected members, who announce their intent to caucus with, a party are included in that party’s count. If the caucus decisions of members of the Senate or House elected as independents cannot be determined on the date of the election, this market may remain open until the earlier of (i) an announcement from the relevant members of their intents to caucus, or (ii) January 4th, 11:59 PM ET of the following calendar year. If no such announcement is made by January 4th, 11:59 PM ET of the following calendar year, the member will not count towards the seat count of any party.

The resolution sources for this market will be official information from relevant state electoral authorities, the United States Congress, and a consensus of credible reporting.

market.question: Will the Republicans win the Texas Senate race in 2026?
market.rules:
This market will resolve according to the winner of the 2026 midterm Texas U.S. Senate election, inclusive of any run-offs.

A candidate shall be considered to represent a party in the event that he or she is the nominee of the party in question. Candidates other than the Democratic or Republican nominee (e.g., Greens, Libertarian, independent) may be added at a later date.

Candidates who run as independents will not be encompassed by the “Democrat” or “Republican” options regardless of any affiliation they may have with the party.

The candidates may be named in the contract for the convenience of traders. In the event that any named candidate is replaced as the nominee of their respective party prior to election day, the name in the contract will be updated and the market will resolve based on the replacement nominee of the party.

The resolution source for this market is the Associated Press, Fox News, and NBC. This market will resolve once all three sources call the race for the same candidate. If all three sources haven’t called the race in this state for the same candidate, this market will resolve based on the official certification.

recent_facts.fact: A New York Times/Siena poll of 615 Texas voters, taken Sept. 21–30, 2026, had Democrat James Talarico at 51% and Republican Ken Paxton at 45%, with a margin of error of ±4.5. The same pollster's June 2026 poll had the race tied 47–47.

A Fox News poll of 881 likely voters, taken Sept. 24–28, 2026, had Talarico at 51% and Paxton at 49%, with a margin of error of ±3. Talarico's favorability was 52% favorable to 44% unfavorable; Paxton's was 40% to 58%.

As of Oct. 5, 2026, the RealClearPolitics polling average had Talarico at 48.4% and Paxton at 45.3%, so Talarico was ahead by 3.1 points. About 6% of voters were undecided or backing other candidates.

A recent Texas Southern University poll had Talarico at 47% and Paxton at 46%. A University of Texas/Texas Politics Project poll had Talarico at 42% and Paxton at 39%, leaving a large share undecided. Exact field dates were not confirmed.

AP projected that Attorney General Ken Paxton won the Republican runoff, beating Sen. John Cornyn after President Trump endorsed Paxton the week before. Cornyn had led the March 3 primary but fell short of a majority. Cornyn is the first Republican senator from Texas to lose his party's renomination.

As of early October, ad spending in the race had reached $442 million, making it the second-most expensive non-presidential race in U.S. history. Republicans accounted for $326 million and Democrats for $116 million. In the NYT/Siena poll, 57% disapproved of Trump's job performance, up 5 points from June.

Talarico accepted TV debates on Oct. 6 (WFAA, Dallas) and Oct. 13 (KXAN, Austin). As of late September, Paxton had not committed to any specific debate date, and WFAA reported his campaign had not responded since Aug. 24.

In the same polling cycle, Republican Gov. Greg Abbott led Democrat Gina Hinojosa by 4 points (50–46) in one poll, and another poll showed the governor's race tied. Libertarian Ted Brown also appears in some Senate polls.

recent_facts.fact: Trend poll (fieldwork Sep 26–Oct 2, 2026; 1,003 face-to-face interviews; ±3.1%): among people intending to vote, Iotova–Valchev 47.8%, Gyurov–Kandev 24.6%, Kostadinov–Volgin (Vazrazhdane) 9.7%, MECh 4.6%, Velichie 2.4%, Hristanov–Cherkezova 1.9%. Sova Harris poll: Iotova–Valchev 50.2%, Gyurov–Kandev 23.7%, Kostadinov–Volgin 12.7%.

market.question: Will WTI Crude Oil (WTI) hit (HIGH) $95 in October?
market.rules:
This market will resolve to "Yes" if, at any point after market creation and during a trading session of October 2026, any Pyth 1-minute candle for the Active Month of ICE Futures Europe WTI Crude Futures (denoted by Pyth as "CLL") has a final "High" or "Low" price equal to or beyond (above for ↑ High Prices, below for ↓ Low Prices) the listed price. Otherwise, this market will resolve to "No".

Prices will be used exactly as published by Pyth, without rounding.

Only prices achieved during an applicable trading session of the specified timeframe's business days will be considered (See: "Trading Hours" at https://www.ice.com/products/213/WTI-Crude-Futures). The trading session for a given business day typically begins at 8:00 PM ET on the prior calendar date, except for the session dated Monday, which begins at 6:00 PM ET on the preceding Sunday, and where modified by holiday or other special hours (See: https://www.ice.com/holiday-hours).

The Active Month is the nearest listed contract, except during that contract's final three trading sessions. At the open of the third-to-last trading session, the next listed contract becomes the Active Month.

Each contract's last trading day will be determined by ICE Futures Europe per the WTI Crude Futures contract specification (generally the 4th US business day prior to the 25th calendar day of the month preceding the contract month, or five US business days prior if the 25th calendar day is not a US business day). The last trading day for each contract is posted at https://www.ice.com/products/213/WTI-Crude-Futures/expiry.

For example, if the last trading session for the nearest listed contract is the session for Monday the 20th, the next listed contract would become the Active Month at the start of the trading session for Thursday the 16th (8:00 PM ET on Wednesday), assuming a standard trading calendar.

If the relevant Pyth data is unavailable due to a system outage, data failure, or other disruption that prevents verification of the required 1-minute candle data, the official daily high/low price published for the Active Month WTI Crude Oil Futures contract by ICE Futures Europe may be used to determine whether the listed price was reached during the applicable trading session (See: https://www.ice.com/report/10 with "T-West Texas Intermediate Light Sweet Crude Future" selected).

In the event of a contract specification change, feed change, or similar structural modification affecting the underlying market during the listed time frame, this market will resolve based on adjusted prices as displayed on Pyth.

If the Active Month contract does not trade at all during the listed time frame, this market will resolve to "No".

The resolution source for this market is Pyth — specifically, the ICE Futures Europe WTI Crude Futures Active Month "High" and "Low" prices available at https://app.pyth.com/explore?search=CLL, with the chart settings configured for 1-minute candles. Historical 1-minute candles may be accessed by appending a Unix timestamp (seconds) to the Pyth chart URL using the "t=" parameter.

recent_facts.fact: On Oct 7, 2026, US WTI futures fell $1.16 to settle at $88.28/bbl and Brent lost 38 cents to $100.20. The drop followed an agreement by IEA member states to prioritize releasing diesel stocks to address surging fuel prices. WTI therefore needs about a 13% rise to reach $100.

Recent WTI daily ranges have been wide, often $3–6 from high to low (for example, Oct 2: 88.06–93.51; Sep 29: 88.78–94.74; Sep 10: 95.37–104.04). On Sep 10, WTI closed up about $6.4 (96.05 to 102.48) in a single session.

Prices fell for five straight days (about 17% in total) after Sep 17, when Saudi crude was reportedly routed through Hormuz after a pipeline loss. WTI's Sep 17 close of $101.91 was the period high, and WTI recovered to $92.16 on Sep 23 after Iran's president said the country would not surrender.

Escalating US-Iran fighting pushed Brent above $100 (closing at $101.21) on Sep 9, 2026, with WTI at $96.05, both the highest closes since May. In August, prices swung on Hormuz reopening hopes, the US blockade of the strait, and new sanctions on Iran, with WTI between about $78 and $87.

market.rules:

recent_facts.fact: The 2026 Baycurrent Classic runs October 8-11, 2026 at Yokohama Country Club in Japan. The field is 72 players, the purse is $8 million, and it is the third of eight FedExCup Fall events. Schauffele is the defending champion, and Wyndham Clark is in the field.
The event has no cut for its 72 players. Under the market rules, a golfer who withdraws or does not tee off resolves No for Tournament Winner.
No player in the tournament's history (it was the Zozo Championship before the name change) has successfully defended the title. Schauffele is trying to be the first.
Schauffele is world No. 10 and has seven top-10 finishes in 2026. He won the event last year at 19-under, one shot ahead of Max Greyserman.

Schauffele has no win in 2026. He finished 14th in the FedExCup, with a 3rd at The Players Championship and a 2nd at the Rocket Classic. He shot 63 and 64 in rounds on the way to last year's Yokohama win.

Schauffele's recent form: T4 at the Tour Championship, with all four rounds in the 60s at East Lake. At the Presidents Cup he won the clinching point for the U.S. by beating Min Woo Lee in Sunday singles.
Wyndham Clark is world No. 5 and the highest-ranked player in the field. In 2026 he won the CJ Cup Byron Nelson, the U.S. Open and the BMW Championship.
Clark's three wins came in his last 11 starts. He went 1-4 at the 2026 Presidents Cup at Medinah, about two weeks before this event.
Clark's course history at Yokohama: T48 in 2025, and he did not break 70 until a closing 68.

Clark won the 2026 U.S. Open at Shinnecock Hills on June 21 by one shot over Sam Burns, going wire to wire after starting the final round six ahead. Earlier in 2026 his world ranking had fallen as low as 75th.

Other contenders in the field: past winner Collin Morikawa, Justin Thomas, Hideki Matsuyama, Jordan Spieth, Min Woo Lee, Adam Scott, Sungjae Im, Keegan Bradley, and Jacob Bridgeman, who has won twice in 2026, most recently at the Biltmore Championship Asheville.
13 players in the field played in the 2026 Presidents Cup, including Morikawa, Matsuyama and Thomas.
Tom Kim withdrew from the Baycurrent Classic after winning at the Asian Games. Search results showed no withdrawal by Schauffele or Clark.

Unverified, from memory: winners of the event from 2019 to 2025 were Woods, Cantlay, Matsuyama, Bradley, Morikawa, Echavarria and Schauffele. That is 7 different winners in 7 editions, and only 2020, played in California, was away from Japan.

market.question: Will Flávio Bolsonaro win the second round of the 2026 Brazilian presidential election by 8–12%?
market.rules:
The second round of the presidential election is scheduled to take place in Brazil on October 25, 2026.

This market will resolve according to the margin of victory between the top two candidates in the second round of the next Brazil Presidential Election.

For the purpose of this market, the “margin of victory” is defined as the absolute difference between the percentages of valid votes received by the first- and second-place candidates. Percentages of the valid votes received by each candidate will be determined by dividing the total number of valid votes each of the top two candidates receives by the sum of all valid votes cast in the election.

If the reported value falls exactly between two brackets, then this market will resolve to the higher range bracket.

If a candidate other than Flávio Bolsonaro or Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva receives the most valid votes in the second round, or if the top two candidates receive exactly the same number of valid votes, this market will resolve to "Other".

This market will resolve based on the official vote count once the vote count has been made official.

If a recount is initiated before the vote total has been made official, the market will remain open until the recount is completed and the vote is made official.

If the result of this election isn't known definitively by June 30, 2027, 11:59 PM ET, the market will resolve to "Other".

This market will resolve based on the result of the election, as indicated by a consensus of credible reporting. If there is ambiguity, this market will resolve based solely on the official results as reported by the Brazilian government, specifically the Superior Electoral Court (Tribunal Superior Eleitoral, TSE) (e.g., https://dadosabertos.tse.jus.br/).

recent_facts.fact: Eliminated candidates' valid-vote shares: Augusto Cury 2.89% (3,448,569), Renan Santos 2.24% (2,675,887), Ronaldo Caiado 2.18% (2,605,148), Romeu Zema 0.27%. The left-wing minor candidates (UP, PSTU, PCB, PCO) together got about 0.17%. Abstention hit a record 21.08% (33.47M). Blank votes were 1.84% and null votes 2.93%.

Polls got Lula's first-round share roughly right but underestimated Flávio. Final valid-vote polls: Quaest Lula 46 / Flávio 45, Datafolha 45/42, AtlasIntel 47.0/44.1, CNT/MDA 47.8/42.1. Gerp was the only pollster with Flávio ahead (46/44). The actual result was Flávio 47.03, Lula 45.16.

The runoff between Flávio Bolsonaro and Lula is on October 25, 2026. The question closes 2026-10-26 03:59 UTC. To resolve Yes, Flávio must win by 4–8 points of valid votes, and a margin exactly on a bracket edge goes to the higher bracket.

market.rules:
If Jacob Bridgeman wins the Baycurrent Classic, then the market resolves to Yes.
If a golfer forfeits, withdraws, or does not participate prior to teeing off, their contracts will resolve as follows:
Tournament Winner and End of Round Leader markets will resolve to No
Finishing Position, Make the Cut, Head-to-Head, and 3-Ball markets will resolve to Fair Market Value

recent_facts.fact: The 2026 Baycurrent Classic runs October 8-11, 2026 at Yokohama Country Club in Japan. The field is 72 players, the purse is $8 million, and it is the third of eight FedExCup Fall events. Schauffele is the defending champion, and Wyndham Clark is in the field.
The event has no cut for its 72 players. Under the market rules, a golfer who withdraws or does not tee off resolves No for Tournament Winner.
No player in the tournament's history (it was the Zozo Championship before the name change) has successfully defended the title. Schauffele is trying to be the first.
Schauffele is world No. 10 and has seven top-10 finishes in 2026. He won the event last year at 19-under, one shot ahead of Max Greyserman.

Schauffele has no win in 2026. He finished 14th in the FedExCup, with a 3rd at The Players Championship and a 2nd at the Rocket Classic. He shot 63 and 64 in rounds on the way to last year's Yokohama win.

Schauffele's recent form: T4 at the Tour Championship, with all four rounds in the 60s at East Lake. At the Presidents Cup he won the clinching point for the U.S. by beating Min Woo Lee in Sunday singles.
Wyndham Clark is world No. 5 and the highest-ranked player in the field. In 2026 he won the CJ Cup Byron Nelson, the U.S. Open and the BMW Championship.
Clark's three wins came in his last 11 starts. He went 1-4 at the 2026 Presidents Cup at Medinah, about two weeks before this event.
Clark's course history at Yokohama: T48 in 2025, and he did not break 70 until a closing 68.

Clark won the 2026 U.S. Open at Shinnecock Hills on June 21 by one shot over Sam Burns, going wire to wire after starting the final round six ahead. Earlier in 2026 his world ranking had fallen as low as 75th.

Other contenders in the field: past winner Collin Morikawa, Justin Thomas, Hideki Matsuyama, Jordan Spieth, Min Woo Lee, Adam Scott, Sungjae Im, Keegan Bradley, and Jacob Bridgeman, who has won twice in 2026, most recently at the Biltmore Championship Asheville.
13 players in the field played in the 2026 Presidents Cup, including Morikawa, Matsuyama and Thomas.
Tom Kim withdrew from the Baycurrent Classic after winning at the Asian Games. Search results showed no withdrawal by Schauffele or Clark.

Unverified, from memory: winners of the event from 2019 to 2025 were Woods, Cantlay, Matsuyama, Bradley, Morikawa, Echavarria and Schauffele. That is 7 different winners in 7 editions, and only 2020, played in California, was away from Japan.

market.question: Bab el-Mandeb Strait effectively closed by October 31?
market.rules:
This market will resolve to “Yes” if IMF PortWatch publishes a 7-day moving average of transit calls (“Arrivals of Ships”) for the Bab el-Mandeb Strait less than or equal to 10 for any date between market creation and the listed date. Otherwise, this market will resolve to “No”.

This market will resolve according to the listed candidate who wins the next presidential election in Bulgaria. 

This market includes any potential second round. If the result of this election isn't known by December 31, 2027, 11:59 PM ET, the market will resolve to "Other".

This market will resolve based on the result of the election, as indicated by a consensus of credible reporting. If there is ambiguity, this market will resolve based solely on the official results as reported by the Bulgarian government, specifically the Central Election Commission (Centralna izbiratelna komisia, CEC) (www.cik.bg/).

recent_facts.source: BTA / Trend Research Center for 24 Chasa
recent_facts.fact: Trend poll (fieldwork Sep 26–Oct 2, 2026; 1,003 face-to-face interviews; ±3.1%): among people intending to vote, Iotova–Valchev 47.8%, Gyurov–Kandev 24.6%, Kostadinov–Volgin (Vazrazhdane) 9.7%, MECh 4.6%, Velichie 2.4%, Hristanov–Cherkezova 1.9%. Trend called a runoff certain given expected turnout.
Alpha Research poll: among people who had definitely decided to vote, Iotova–Valchev 44.5%, Gyurov–Kandev 26.1%, Kostadinov–Volgin 10.5%.
Market Links poll: among decided voters, Iotova–Valchev 41.4%, Gyurov–Kandev 21.9%.

Iotova, the incumbent president, is running as an independent with Kiril Valchev. Her ticket is backed by Progressive Bulgaria (Radev's party; Radev is now prime minister), BSP–OL, ISBG and VMRO-BND. Gyurov–Kandev run as independents backed by PP–DB. DPS registered but nominated no candidate, and BSP withdrew its own registration to support Iotova.
For the first time in its 20-year history, GERB is neither fielding nor formally backing a presidential candidate. Borissov argued a GERB nominee would split the pro-European vote and help Iotova.
The first round is on 25 October 2026 and any runoff is on 1 November 2026. A record 27 candidate tickets are on the ballot, which also has a 'none of the above' option.

Winning in the first round requires a majority of valid votes plus turnout above 50% of the electorate. Otherwise the top two go to a runoff, where a plurality wins. Pollsters say expected turnout below 50% makes a runoff between Iotova and Gyurov likely.
In the 2021 runoff, the incumbent Radev–Iotova ticket won 66.72% against Gerdjikov's 31.80%. In 2016, Radev won the runoff with 59.37% against Tsacheva's 36.16%.

Unverified, from memory: of Bulgarian incumbent presidents who ran for re-election in direct elections, Stoyanov lost in 2001, while Parvanov (2006) and Radev (2021) won. That is 2 of 3, a very small sample.

In the case of a delay in data caused by a federal government shutdown impacting the reliability of the Source Agency, the market’s latest Expiration Date will be extended to the sooner of the release of the Underlying or six months after the end of the

recent_facts.fact: In the 12 months to August 2026, the CPI-U all-items index rose 3.4% (not seasonally adjusted), the same rate as for the 12 months to July. The NSA index was 334.980 in August 2026, up 0.3% from July before seasonal adjustment. On a seasonally adjusted basis it rose 0.4%.

The September 2025 CPI-U NSA index was 324.800, and August 2025 was 323.976, so September 2025 rose about 0.25% NSA month over month. My own calculation: a published 12-month rate above 3.6% (3.7% or higher after rounding, i.e. at least 3.65%) needs a September 2026 index of about 336.66 or more. That is roughly a +0.50% NSA rise from August's 334.980. A rise of about +0.40% NSA (index about 336.33) would round to 3.6%.
BLS will release September 2026 CPI on Wednesday, October 14, 2026, at 8:30 a.m. ET.

AAA put the September 2026 national average gasoline price at $4.33/gal, a record for September and 50 cents above the previous September record of $3.83 (2023). The national average peaked at $4.48 on September 24 and was $4.41 by October 1.

Through August 20, AAA's August 2026 national average gasoline price was $4.06/gal. Daily readings were about $4.07 on August 13 and $4.09 on August 27. If the full August average was around $4.06–4.09, September's $4.33 would be roughly a 6–7% month-over-month rise in retail gasoline.

EIA's weekly U.S. regular gasoline price was $4.319 on September 14, $4.478 on September 21 and $4.465 on September 28, 2026. The September 28 price was about $1.35 higher than a year earlier. Third-party sites reported early-September EIA readings of about $4.07–4.29, which don't line up cleanly with each other.

recent_facts.fact: The 2026 Baycurrent Classic runs October 8-11, 2026 at Yokohama Country Club in Japan. The field is 72 players, the purse is $8 million, and it is the third of eight FedExCup Fall events. Schauffele is the defending champion, and Wyndham Clark is in the field.
The event has no cut for its 72 players. Under the market rules, a golfer who withdraws or does not tee off resolves No for Tournament Winner.
No player in the tournament's history (it was the Zozo Championship before the name change) has successfully defended the title. Schauffele is trying to be the first.
Schauffele is world No. 10 and has seven top-10 finishes in 2026. He won the event last year at 19-under, one shot ahead of Max Greyserman.

Schauffele has no win in 2026. He finished 14th in the FedExCup, with a 3rd at The Players Championship and a 2nd at the Rocket Classic. He shot 63 and 64 in rounds on the way to last year's Yokohama win.

Schauffele's recent form: T4 at the Tour Championship, with all four rounds in the 60s at East Lake. At the Presidents Cup he won the clinching point for the U.S. by beating Min Woo Lee in Sunday singles.
Wyndham Clark is world No. 5 and the highest-ranked player in the field. In 2026 he won the CJ Cup Byron Nelson, the U.S. Open and the BMW Championship.
Clark's three wins came in his last 11 starts. He went 1-4 at the 2026 Presidents Cup at Medinah, about two weeks before this event.
Clark's course history at Yokohama: T48 in 2025, and he did not break 70 until a closing 68.

Clark won the 2026 U.S. Open at Shinnecock Hills on June 21 by one shot over Sam Burns, going wire to wire after starting the final round six ahead. Earlier in 2026 his world ranking had fallen as low as 75th.

Other contenders in the field: past winner Collin Morikawa, Justin Thomas, Hideki Matsuyama, Jordan Spieth, Min Woo Lee, Adam Scott, Sungjae Im, Keegan Bradley, and Jacob Bridgeman, who has won twice in 2026, most recently at the Biltmore Championship Asheville.
13 players in the field played in the 2026 Presidents Cup, including Morikawa, Matsuyama and Thomas.
Tom Kim withdrew from the Baycurrent Classic after winning at the Asian Games. Search results showed no withdrawal by Schauffele or Clark.

Unverified, from memory: winners of the event from 2019 to 2025 were Woods, Cantlay, Matsuyama, Bradley, Morikawa, Echavarria and Schauffele. That is 7 different winners in 7 editions, and only 2020, played in California, was away from Japan.

market.question: Will the Democrats win the Texas Senate race in 2026?
market.rules:
This market will resolve according to the winner of the 2026 midterm Texas U.S. Senate election, inclusive of any run-offs.

A candidate shall be considered to represent a party in the event that he or she is the nominee of the party in question. Candidates other than the Democratic or Republican nominee (e.g., Greens, Libertarian, independent) may be added at a later date.

Candidates who run as independents will not be encompassed by the “Democrat” or “Republican” options regardless of any affiliation they may have with the party.

The candidates may be named in the contract for the convenience of traders. In the event that any named candidate is replaced as the nominee of their respective party prior to election day, the name in the contract will be updated and the market will resolve based on the replacement nominee of the party.

The resolution source for this market is the Associated Press, Fox News, and NBC. This market will resolve once all three sources call the race for the same candidate. If all three sources haven’t called the race in this state for the same candidate, this market will resolve based on the official certification.

recent_facts.fact: A New York Times/Siena poll of 615 Texas voters, taken Sept. 21–30, 2026, had Democrat James Talarico at 51% and Republican Ken Paxton at 45%, with a margin of error of ±4.5. The same pollster's June 2026 poll had the race tied 47–47.

A Fox News poll of 881 likely voters, taken Sept. 24–28, 2026, had Talarico at 51% and Paxton at 49%, with a margin of error of ±3. Talarico's favorability was 52% favorable to 44% unfavorable; Paxton's was 40% to 58%.

As of Oct. 5, 2026, the RealClearPolitics polling average had Talarico at 48.4% and Paxton at 45.3%, so Talarico was ahead by 3.1 points. About 6% of voters were undecided or backing other candidates.

A recent Texas Southern University poll had Talarico at 47% and Paxton at 46%. A University of Texas/Texas Politics Project poll had Talarico at 42% and Paxton at 39%, leaving a large share undecided. Exact field dates were not confirmed.

AP projected that Attorney General Ken Paxton won the Republican runoff, beating Sen. John Cornyn after President Trump endorsed Paxton the week before. Cornyn had led the March 3 primary but fell short of a majority. Cornyn is the first Republican senator from Texas to lose his party's renomination.

As of early October, ad spending in the race had reached $442 million, making it the second-most expensive non-presidential race in U.S. history. Republicans accounted for $326 million and Democrats for $116 million. In the NYT/Siena poll, 57% disapproved of Trump's job performance, up 5 points from June.

In the Fox News poll, 53% of likely voters said they were concerned Talarico is too liberal and 51% said they were concerned Paxton is too close to Trump. 68% called cost of living extremely important to their vote.

Talarico accepted TV debates on Oct. 6 (WFAA, Dallas) and Oct. 13 (KXAN, Austin). As of late September, Paxton had not committed to any specific debate date, and WFAA reported his campaign had not responded since Aug. 24.

In the same polling cycle, Republican Gov. Greg Abbott led Democrat Gina Hinojosa by 4 points (50–46) in one poll, and another poll showed the governor's race tied. Libertarian Ted Brown also appears in some Senate polls.
Early voting in Texas starts Oct. 19, 2026, and Election Day is Nov. 3, 2026.

In the 2024 Texas Senate race, the final polling average had Ted Cruz up about 3.8 points (49.0 to 45.2), but he won by 8.5 points (53.05% to 44.56%). The polls underestimated the Republican margin by about 4.7 points.

In 2018, final polls mostly had Cruz ahead of Beto O'Rourke by 3 to 6 points (Emerson +3, UT-Tyler +3.6, Quinnipiac +5, Texas Tribune +6). Cruz won by about 2.6 points (51% to 48%), so the Democrat did slightly better than most polls showed.
Texas has not elected a Democrat to any statewide office in about 30 years, since 1994. From memory and unverified: the last Democrat to win a Texas U.S. Senate race was Lloyd Bentsen in 1988.

The question resolves once AP, Fox News and NBC all call the race for the same candidate, and otherwise on official certification. Paxton is the Republican nominee. From memory and unverified: Texas general elections are decided by plurality, with no general-election runoff.

State Rep. Angie Nixon, who aligns with the Democratic Socialists of America, upset Alex Vindman 56–44 in the Democratic primary while spending about $0.7M to his roughly $9M. Moody, the appointed incumbent, won the GOP primary with 79.6%. Florida's baseline is R+10.3 (Inside Elections).

The only other declared candidate is independent Neil J. Gillespie. John Morgan (independent) declined to run, and the American Party and Veterans Party candidates did not qualify. Trump, Rick Scott and Ted Cruz have endorsed Moody.
Moody told Spectrum News she will not debate Nixon. Moody is campaigning on 'Stop socialism.' Nixon is tying Moody to Trump and to the Hope Florida controversy.
2024 Florida Senate: the final 270toWin average had Scott (R) up 4.8 (49.3–44.5). Scott won 55.6–42.8, a 12.8-point margin, so the polls understated the Republican by about 8 points.
2022 Florida Senate: the final 270toWin average had Rubio (R) up about 9 (51.6–42.4). Rubio won 57.7–41.3, a 16.4-point margin, so the polls understated the Republican by about 7 points.
2018 Florida Senate: the final RCP aggregate had Democrat Nelson up 2.4 points (approximate, from a single secondary source). Scott (R) won by about 10,000 votes (50.1–49.9) after a recount.
Democrats have not won a Florida U.S. Senate race since 2012. Republicans won the 2016, 2018, 2022 and 2024 races.
The special general election is November 3, 2026. The winner serves the rest of Rubio's term, through 2028. Florida has no general-election runoff, so the plurality winner takes the seat.

Candidates who run as independents will not be encompassed by the “Democrat” or “Republican” options regardless of any affiliation they may have with the party.

The candidates may be named in the contract for the convenience of traders. In the event that any named candidate is replaced as the nominee of their respective party prior to election day, the name in the contract will be updated and the market will resolve based on the replacement nominee of the party.

The resolution source for this market is the Associated Press, Fox News, and NBC. This market will resolve once all three sources call the race for the same candidate. If all three sources haven’t called the race in this state for the same candidate, this market will resolve based on the official certification.

recent_facts.source: Wikipedia (2026 United States Senate election in Michigan)
recent_facts.fact: The nominees are Democrat Abdul El-Sayed and Republican Mike Rogers. Four minor-party nominees are also running: Lydia Christensen (Libertarian), Douglas P. Marsh (Green), Tim Long (U.S. Taxpayers) and Walter P. Kristy (Natural Law). No major independent is listed in the Senate race.
YouGov poll of 3,949 likely voters, Sept 22 to Oct 4, 2026: El-Sayed 49%, Rogers 48%, other 1%, undecided 2%.

Mitchell Research poll of 682 likely voters on Oct 1, 2026: El-Sayed 45.6%, Rogers 41.4%, each of the four minor-party candidates at 3% or less, undecided 6%, margin of error 3.8%. The pollster cautioned that in past Michigan Senate races Republicans gained support in the final weeks of the campaign.

recent_facts.source: Trafalgar Group, Beacon/Shaw and Marist via Wikipedia
recent_facts.fact: Trafalgar, Sept 28–30 (1,085 likely voters): El-Sayed 47%, Rogers 45%, undecided 5%. Beacon/Shaw, Sept 24–28: El-Sayed 50%, Rogers 49% among likely voters. Marist, Sept 24–27 (1,235 registered voters): El-Sayed 51%, Rogers 44%.

recent_facts.source: Cook Political Report / Sabato's Crystal Ball / Inside Elections via Wikipedia
recent_facts.fact: Race ratings as of October: Cook Political Report has it as a Tossup, Sabato's Crystal Ball as Lean D and Inside Elections as Tilt D.
The RealClearPolling average shows El-Sayed at 47.8% and Rogers at 43.8%, a gap of about 4 points.

Disclosed spending on the race is over $205 million. Since the start of 2025, Rogers and groups backing him have outspent El-Sayed and his allies by almost 2 to 1. For October, Republicans plan to spend more than $43 million, against about $25 million in Democratic reservations.
Rogers skipped a Tuesday-night debate, saying moderator Roop Raj favored El-Sayed. El-Sayed debated next to an empty podium and was questioned about Hasan Piker, Israel and socialist ties.
Rogers acknowledged that El-Sayed is 'doing a good job on campuses' and called this 'a little scary.' Republican ads describe El-Sayed as 'dangerous' and 'radical.'
A CNN headline from Oct 7 reads: 'Abdul El-Sayed is certain he'll win Michigan's Senate race. Some key Democrats quietly aren't so sure.' The article body could not be retrieved.

Mallory McMorrow, who left the primary in July, endorsed El-Sayed after the primary. Haley Stevens, the runner-up, said she would work to keep the seat Democratic. Gov. Whitmer had endorsed Stevens before the primary.

El-Sayed won the Aug 4 Democratic primary with 48.5%, narrowly beating Rep. Haley Stevens. Rogers was unopposed for the Republican nomination. As of July 15, El-Sayed had raised $14.5M and had $2.5M cash on hand; Rogers had raised $10.9M and had $4.5M on hand.
Rogers and El-Sayed are scheduled to meet in a televised debate on Oct 8, 2026. Election day is Nov 3, 2026.
In 2024, Slotkin (D) beat Rogers 48.6% to 48.3% (D+0.3). She had led by about 5 points for much of the race, and final polls on Nov 3–4 showed her ahead by 1 point (49–48).
Republicans have not won a U.S. Senate race in Michigan since 1994. Democrats won every Michigan Senate race from 1996 through 2024.

market.question: Will the Republican Party control the Senate after the 2026 Midterm elections?
market.rules:
This market will resolve according to the party that wins control of the United States Senate in the 2026 United States midterm election.

A party wins control of the United States Senate if it wins a majority of the chamber’s voting seats. If no party wins a majority of voting seats, the party that wins control of the chamber is the party that wins half of the voting seats and holds the Vice Presidency. If the outcome remains ambiguous after applying the above criteria, the chamber will be deemed controlled by the party with which the first selected President Pro Tempore of the Congress that convenes after the specified election is affiliated.

The following rules govern the counting of seats for determining which party wins control of the chamber.

All regular and special Senate elections that determine representation in the upcoming 120th Congress and are scheduled to take place in November 2026 as of October 31, 2026 are included. Runoffs for qualifying elections will determine attribution of the relevant seat, even if they take place after November 2026. Vacant seats for which no election or special election to fill the seat is scheduled to take place in November 2026 as of October 31, 2026 will be treated as held by the party affiliation of the most recent member to hold that seat.

For seats contested in the specified election, seats are attributed to the party under which the member was elected. If a member-elect changes party affiliation, or vacates their seat, between election day and the formal organization of Congress, the seat is attributed to the party under which the member was elected.

For seats not contested in the specified election, seats are attributed to the party that holds the seat as of the date of the election. If a current sitting member of the U.S. Senate who is not up for election changes party affiliation or vacates their seat after the date of the election, the seat is attributed to the party under which the member was affiliated at the time of the election.

Senate members elected as independents who formally caucus with, or, for newly elected members, who announce their intent to caucus with, a party are included in that party’s count. If the caucus decisions of members of the Senate elected as independents cannot be determined on the date of the election, this market may remain open until the earlier of (i) an announcement from the relevant members of their intents to caucus, or (ii) January 4th, 11:59 PM ET of the following calendar year. If no such announcement is made by January 4th, 11:59 PM ET of the following calendar year, the member will not count towards the seat count of any party.

The resolution sources for this market will be official information from relevant state electoral authorities, the United States Congress, and a consensus of credible reporting.

recent_facts.fact: Cook's Senate ratings, updated Oct 6, 2026, list 7 Toss Up races. Six are Republican-held: Alaska (Sullivan), Iowa (open), Kansas (Marshall), Maine (Collins), Ohio (Husted) and Texas (open). One is Democratic-held: Michigan (open). Cook's estimate of possible Democratic pickups is 2 to 6 seats, and Democrats need a net gain of 4 for a majority.

The Senate currently stands at 53 R and 47 D, counting the 2 independents who caucus with Democrats. The Vice President is Republican JD Vance, so Republicans keep control at 50-50. Democrats therefore need 51 seats, which means a net gain of 4.

On Oct 6, Cook moved three races toward Democrats: Kansas from Lean R to Toss Up, New Hampshire from Toss Up to Lean D, and North Carolina from Lean D to Likely D. In late September, Cook had moved Georgia from Lean D to Likely D.

Recent Texas polls show Democrat Talarico ahead of Republican Paxton: NYT/Siena 51-45, YouGov 50-44 and Fox News 51-49. Ohio: NYT/Siena has Democrat Sherrod Brown at 49 and Republican Husted at 46, with a margin of error of about ±4.5.

Maine: a Marist poll has Democrat Troy Jackson at 51 and Collins at 47, while recent CNN/SSRS and NYT/Siena polls showed no clear leader. Iowa: NYT/Siena has Republican Hinson at 48 and Democrat Turek at 47, and an earlier Suffolk poll had Turek ahead 48-44.

Alaska: NYT/Siena has Democrat Mary Peltola at 50 and Republican Sullivan at 43 among likely voters, and Alaska Survey Research has her ahead 51-49. North Carolina: YouGov/Catawba has Democrat Cooper at 47 and Republican Whatley at 35.

In September polls of the Democratic-held open Michigan seat, Democrat El-Sayed led Republican Rogers in Trafalgar (47-45), NYT/Siena (49-44) and Suffolk (47-40). One co/efficient poll showed a tie. A Fox News poll from August had Rogers ahead 51-47.

Kansas: a Global Strategy Group poll (a Democratic firm) has Democrat Adam Hamilton at 47 and Sen. Roger Marshall at 43, with Libertarian Graham at 5%. An Emerson College poll, date not given, had Hamilton ahead by 2, within the margin of error.

Georgia, Democratic-held: a YouGov poll from Sept 15–18 of 3,447 registered voters (margin of error ±2.7) has Sen. Ossoff at 51 and Republican Mike Collins at 41, with 6% undecided. An InsiderAdvantage poll from Aug 16–17 had Ossoff ahead 50-43.

Nebraska: an internal GBAO poll (Sept 3–8, 800 likely voters) has independent Dan Osborn at 47 and Sen. Pete Ricketts at 46. No independent public poll from the fall was found. Under the rules, an independent counts toward a party only if he caucuses with it or announces he will, and no reporting was found on which party Osborn would caucus with.
Forbes's race tracker, updated Oct 6, reports Democrats leading in the Maine and New Hampshire Senate races, with historically Republican Kansas now a toss-up.

Election Day is Nov 3, 2026, and the question closes Nov 4, 04:59 UTC. Runoffs, such as Georgia's if no candidate passes 50%, decide those seats even if they happen after November. If an independent winner's caucus choice is unclear, the market may stay open until Jan 4.
Since WWII, the president's party has lost an average of about 4 Senate seats in midterms. Across 22 midterms from 1934 to 2018, it gained Senate seats only 6 times.

A 2006 editorial counted 3 midterms since WWII in which the president's party lost the Senate: 1946, 1954 and 1986. This count is unverified and looks incomplete, since 1994 is not listed and 2006 came after the editorial. Adding those makes about 5 of the 20 midterms from 1946 to 2022.

Revisions to officially declared final scores made after market resolution will not be accounted for in determining the outcome. If no acceptable data is available within 24 hours of the event's conclusion, this market will resolve 50-50, or to "Draw" where applicable.

market.rules:
This market will resolve according to the winner of the 2026 midterm Alaska U.S. Senate election, inclusive of any run-offs, currently scheduled for November 3, 2026.

If the results of the election are not confirmed by July 31, 2027, this market will resolve to "Other".

The resolution source for this market is the Associated Press, Fox News, and NBC. This market will resolve once all three sources call the race for the same candidate. If all three sources haven’t called the race in this state for the same candidate, this market will resolve based on official certification.

recent_facts.source: Wikipedia (2026 United States Senate election in Alaska)
recent_facts.fact: Polls since early September give mixed first-choice results. AARP (Fabrizio/Impact, Sep 8–11): Peltola 46, Sullivan 41. Alaska Survey Research (Sep 10–12): Peltola 48, Sullivan 44. Rasmussen (Sep 13–14): 39–39. co/efficient (R, Sep 14–17): Sullivan 48, Peltola 46. Trafalgar (R, Sep 22–24): Sullivan 47, Peltola 46. NYT/Siena (Sep 24–Oct 1, 504 LV, ±5.1): Peltola 50, Sullivan 43. Quantus (R, Sep 28–30): 46–46.

recent_facts.source: Wikipedia (2026 United States Senate election in Alaska)
recent_facts.fact: The polling average the page cites, as of 2026-10-03, is Peltola 48.7% and Sullivan 45.8%. In polls that ran the ranked-choice rounds, Peltola wins the final round 52–48 (ASR, Sep 10–12) and 53–47 (AARP, Sep 8–11).
In a new Alaska Survey Research poll of likely voters, Peltola leads Sullivan 51% to 49% after the third round of ranked-choice tabulation.
The RealClearPolitics average has Peltola at 48.5% and Sullivan at 47.3%, a Peltola lead of about 1.2 points.

In the Aug 18, 2026 top-four primary, Peltola (D) won 82,244 votes (49.5%) and incumbent Dan S. Sullivan (R) won 68,726 (41.4%). Daniel J. Sullivan Jr. took 2.5%, David Leslie (D) 1.1% and Gerald Heikes (R) 1.1%. Leslie withdrew under pressure from Democratic leadership, so the November ballot is Peltola, Dan S. Sullivan, Daniel J. Sullivan Jr. and Heikes. The two minor candidates are both registered Republicans.

A same-name candidate, Dan J. Sullivan of Petersburg, will appear on the November ballot with no party label. Republicans accuse him of being a Democratic plant meant to draw votes away from the incumbent. In polls he takes about 1–7% of first choices.

Since mid-July, outside groups backing Sullivan have spent about $15.5–20 million on ads and groups backing Peltola about $15.4 million. The Senate Leadership Fund has spent more than $8 million and Trump's super PAC about $3.6 million since early September.

market.question: 2026 Balance of Power: R Senate, D House
market.rules:
This market will resolve according to the party that wins control of the United States Senate and the party that wins control of the United States House of Representatives in the 2026 United States midterm election.

A party wins control of the United States Senate if it wins a majority of the chamber’s voting seats. If no party wins a majority of voting seats, the party that wins control of the chamber is the party that wins half of the voting seats and holds the Vice Presidency. If the outcome remains ambiguous after applying the above criteria, the chamber will be deemed controlled by the party with which the first selected President Pro Tempore of the Congress that convenes after the specified election is affiliated.

A party wins control of the United States House of Representatives if it wins a majority of the chamber’s voting seats. If no party wins a majority of voting seats, the chamber will be deemed controlled by the party with which the first elected Speaker of the House of the Congress that convenes after the 2026 midterm election is affiliated.

The following rules govern the counting of seats for determining which party wins control of the chambers.

For determining Senate control, all regular and special Senate elections that determine representation in the upcoming 120th Congress and are scheduled to take place in November 2026 as of October 31, 2026 are included. Vacant Senate seats for which no election or special election to fill the seat is scheduled to take place in November 2026 as of October 31, 2026 will be treated as held by the party affiliation of the most recent member to hold that seat. For determining House control, all House elections in the 2026 United States midterm election that elect voting members and determine representation in the upcoming 120th Congress are included. Where a Senate or House seat is decided by a runoff, the runoff result will determine attribution of that seat, even if it takes place after November 2026.

For seats contested in the specified election, seats are attributed to the party under which the member was elected. If a member-elect changes party affiliation, or vacates their seat, between election day and the formal organization of Congress, the seat is attributed to the party under which the member was elected. 

For seats not contested in the specified election, seats are attributed to the party that holds the seat as of the date of the election. If a current sitting member of the U.S. Senate who is not up for election changes party affiliation or vacates their seat after the date of the election, the seat is attributed to the party under which the member was affiliated at the time of the election.

Senate and House members elected as independents who formally caucus with, or, for newly elected members, who announce their intent to caucus with, a party are included in that party’s count. If the caucus decisions of members of the Senate or House elected as independents cannot be determined on the date of the election, this market may remain open until the earlier of (i) an announcement from the relevant members of their intents to caucus, or (ii) January 4th, 11:59 PM ET of the following calendar year. If no such announcement is made by January 4th, 11:59 PM ET of the following calendar year, the member will not count towards the seat count of any party.

The resolution sources for this market will be official information from relevant state electoral authorities, the United States Congress, and a consensus of credible reporting.

market.question: Will Aleksandar Vučić – United Serbia win the most seats in the 2026 Serbian parliamentary election?
market.rules:
Parliamentary elections to elect the 250 members of the National Assembly of Serbia are scheduled to take place on October 25, 2026.

This market will resolve to the electoral list that wins the greatest number of seats in the National Assembly of Serbia as a result of this election.

Electoral lists will be primarily ranked by the number of seats won in the specified election. If two or more lists are tied on seats, ties will be broken by the total number of valid votes received, with higher vote totals ranking higher. If lists remain tied, ties will be broken by alphabetical order of the listed names. This market will resolve to the list that occupies the highest finishing position after applying this ranking.

This market's resolution will be based solely on the number of seats won by the named electoral list, as it appears on the ballot and official proclamations, regardless of which parties make up the list or how its members later organize themselves in the National Assembly.

If the results of the specified election are not definitively known by March 31, 2027, 11:59 PM ET, this market will resolve to "Other".

This market will resolve based on the results of the elections, as indicated by a consensus of credible reporting. In the case of ambiguity, this market will resolve solely based on the results as reported by the Republic Electoral Commission of Serbia (https://www.rik.parlament.gov.rs/).

recent_facts.fact: In CRTA's poll, fielded 13–27 September 2026, 44% of citizens backed the Student List and 32% backed the Vučić-led bloc (United Serbia). These shares appear to be of the whole sample, not only of decided voters.

In Faktor Plus's September poll, the Student List rose 5.6 points from the previous poll and United Serbia rose 1.4 points. Faktor Plus's director said the opposition vote had consolidated because the People's Movement of Serbia, Ecological Uprising and New Face of Serbia had withdrawn from the race.
Faktor Plus's previous poll had SNS/United Serbia at 47.2% and the Student List at 31.5%.

An earlier CRTA/Stanford Democracy Action Lab face-to-face poll of 2,324 adults, fielded from 10 June, found 44.9% of decided voters (about 70% of the sample) for the Student List, 35.7% for SNS and 3.8% for SPS, with all others below the threshold. The article date is unconfirmed. Vučić publicly rejected CRTA's findings as propaganda.

The main lists on the ballot are: 1 'Aleksandar Vučić – United Serbia' (SNS-led); 2 'Ivica Dačić – Factor of Stability' (SPS, JS, SDPS, Zeleni); 3 'Student List – Students Are Winning' (ballot carrier Ilija Srdanović); 8 'Authentic Right – Dr. Miloš Jovanović' (NADA); 9 'European Serbia' (SSP and SRCE, led by Tepić and Ponoš). Wikipedia says polls are split, with some putting SNS first and others putting the Student List first.

DS, Green–Left Front, PSG (which left the Platform for European Serbia), New Face of Serbia and Ecological Uprising endorsed the Student List. SSP/SRCE (European Serbia) and NADA are running their own lists, so the opposition vote is split across several lists.
Vučić said he would resign as president on 27 September to campaign as the head of the United Serbia list. SNS nominated him as its candidate for prime minister.

All 250 seats are elected by closed-list proportional representation in one nationwide constituency, allocated by the D'Hondt method. There is a 3% threshold, which does not apply to ethnic-minority lists, and 126 seats is a majority. Because seats closely follow vote share among lists that pass the threshold, the list with the most votes would almost certainly also win the most seats.
16 lists are officially registered for the 25 October election: 17 were submitted, 1 was withdrawn and 1 was cancelled by the Republic Electoral Commission (RIK). Five of the 16 have minority status.

The early election was called on 9 September 2026 and will be held on 25 October 2026. The OSCE/ODIHR and CeSID will observe it, and TV debates are running on N1, RTS, Nova and Insajder through late September and October.

CRTA accused Vučić of trying to discredit it as an election observer and as a witness to possible fraud. The article date is unconfirmed. Separately, monitors report that Student List leader Ilija Srdanović has had no live appearances on national-coverage TV channels since 15 September.

Unverified, partly from memory: an SNS-led list won the most seats in each Serbian parliamentary election from 2012 to 2023 (2012, 2014, 2016, 2020, 2022, 2023, so 6 of 6). In December 2023 it won about 46.7% against about 23.6% for Serbia Against Violence.
