market.question: Israel accuses Iran/proxies of plane stabbing incident by Oct 31?
market.rules:
On September 30, 2026, FlyDubai flight FZ1073 from Dubai to Tel Aviv diverted to Saudi Arabia following an incident in the cockpit in which the co-pilot allegedly stabbed the captain. (see: https://www.reuters.com/world/middle-east/diverted-flydubai-flight-israel-was-not-hijacking-incident-israeli-prime-2026-09-30/).

This market will resolve to "Yes" if the Israeli national government, or an authorized representative of the Israeli national government, publicly announces that Iran or its affiliated groups deliberately caused this incident, by October 31, 2026, 11:59 PM ET. Otherwise, this market will resolve to "No".

A public announcement refers to an on-the-record statement issued by the Israeli national government or by its authorized representatives acting in an official capacity on behalf of the Israeli national government. A statement or press release issued by the Israeli national government or any of its agencies will qualify. A Prime Minister or Cabinet Minister’s public statements will always be considered to be issued on-the-record in a capacity representing the Israeli national government for purposes of this market. A statement from a lawmaker or other government official speaking in their own capacity or on behalf of a party not in government will not alone qualify.

For purposes of this market, an affiliated group of Iran is: any organization directly controlled by Iran, Hezbollah, Hamas, Palestinian Islamic Jihad, Houthis ("Ansar Allah"), Kata'ib Hezbollah, Asa'ib Ahl al-Haq, Badr Organization, and Harakat al-Nujaba. An unlisted group will only qualify if the Israeli claim itself, or accompanying statements or releases, specifies that the group is a proxy of or otherwise is controlled or directed by Iran. A general statement that it was conducted by an Iranian proxy will also qualify, even if no group is named.

Such a statement will be considered to claim that Iran or its affiliated groups deliberately caused the incident if it explicitly claims that Iran or an affiliated group ordered, carried out, planned, or otherwise directly aided or coordinated the incident. Statements that attribute only inspiration or ideological influence (e.g., "this would not have happened if Iran didn't radicalize terrorists," "the co-pilot was influenced by Hamas' ideas") will not qualify.

Once a qualifying announcement has been made, no subsequent walkback or retraction will be relevant for purposes of this market. 

The primary resolution source for this market will be official information from the Israeli national government; however, a consensus of credible reporting may also be used.

recent_facts.fact: An unnamed Israeli official familiar with the matter said 'there is no information that can rule out or confirm an Iranian connection to or involvement with the co-pilot.' The defense establishment's current assessment is that Omani co-pilot Hamam al-Hammami acted alone. The article names no Israeli minister who has claimed Iran was behind it.

market.question: Israeli airspace closed by October 31, 2026?
market.rules:
This market will resolve to “Yes” if Israeli Airspace (The Tel Aviv Flight Information Region (FIR)/LLLL) is closed between market creation and the specified date, 11:59 PM ET. Otherwise, this market will resolve to “No”.

A qualifying closure occurs when the aviation or governmental authority responsible for overseeing the specified airspace region issues a Notice to Airmen (NOTAM), or other official order under the regulations of the jurisdiction responsible for that airspace region, which generally cancels or suspends commercial aviation across the specified airspace region, and such closure is not excluded under the exclusions provision below. A qualifying closure must apply generally to commercial flights transiting, arriving in, and departing from the specified airspace region. A closure is not disqualified because the order permits limited exceptions, including humanitarian, medical, repatriation, or emergency flights, or select flights authorized by the responsible authority, provided that commercial flights are prohibited by default, rather than permitted subject to conditions or restrictions.

The following are not qualifying closures: (i) closures due to weather, including volcanic and seismic activity; (ii) closures for holidays or religious observances; (iii) closures planned or announced before Contract Issuance; (iv) closures occurring on a regular cadence whose occurrence was determined before Contract Issuance, even if not announced; (v) closures resulting from the failure or malfunction of air traffic control, navigation, communications, power, or other technical systems; (vi) restrictions applying to aircraft by nationality, state of registry, operator, or ownership rather than to commercial traffic generally; (vii) closures of a subset of the specified airspace region, including geographic sectors and altitude bands; (viii) ground stops, flow restrictions, capacity reductions, or other air traffic management measures that delay or restrict traffic without closing the specified airspace region to commercial aviation; and (ix) warnings, no-fly zones, flight suspensions, or other restrictions imposed by any party other than the aviation or governmental authorities responsible for overseeing the specified airspace region.

A qualifying closure is deemed to occur at the time the closure takes effect, regardless of when the closure is announced or the order is issued. Where no effective time is included in the order, the closure is deemed to take effect at the time the order is issued.

The resolution sources for this market will be official information from the Israeli government, including the Ministry of Transport, the Civil Aviation Authority, and the Israel Airports Authority, and a consensus of credible reporting.

recent_facts.fact: On 10 September 2026 the ECB raised the deposit facility rate by 25 bps, from 2.25% to 2.50%. This was its second hike since the US-Iran war began. From 16 September the key rates are: deposit facility 2.50%, main refinancing operations 2.65%, marginal lending 2.90%.

Governing Council member Joachim Nagel said there are 'no clear signs of second-round effects taking hold just yet', which suggests room to wait before tightening again. He also said inflation risks 'remain tilted to the upside' and the ECB should 'remain flexible and respond to incoming data'. The article describes this as a case for an October pause, with a December hike still possible.

President Lagarde said measured ECB hikes remain appropriate because this year's inflation has not yet produced dangerous second-round effects. She repeated that decisions are made meeting by meeting, with no pre-commitment to a rate path.

The September flash HICP for the euro area was 3.8%, up from 3.2% in August and the highest since September 2023. The rise was mainly energy-driven, and core and services pressures were described as 'broadly contained': German core was unchanged at 2.4% and Italian core rose from 1.4% to 1.6%.

MUFG wrote that the bar for an October ECB hike had risen after Lagarde's more measured tone and a pullback in gas prices. It said a renewed rise in energy markets over the coming weeks would be needed for the hawks to push for an October move.

Executive Board member Isabel Schnabel gave a clearly hawkish view of the inflation outlook. Econostream judged that the policy signal at the end of her speech points away from an October hike unless conditions worsen significantly in the coming weeks. In Berlin she called recent moves in energy prices 'quite concerning', citing diesel, reduced refining capacity, low European gas storage and competition with Asia for LNG. The exact date of the speech was not confirmed.
So far in this 2026 hiking cycle the ECB has alternated: +25 bps on 11 June, hold on 23 July, +25 bps on 10 September. That is 2 hikes and 1 hold in the last 3 meetings.

The Governing Council's monetary policy meeting is scheduled for 28-29 October 2026, with the decision announced on 29 October. The euro area flash HICP for October is normally published after that meeting, so the September 3.8% print is the last full inflation reading available before the decision.
The question resolves on the change in the deposit facility rate, currently 2.50%. The ECB has moved all three key rates in 25 bp steps in 2026, keeping the MRO 15 bps above the deposit rate.

This market will resolve to “Yes” if a diplomatic agreement between the United States and Iran over traffic in the strait of Hormuz is announced by the specified date, 11:59 PM ET.

A diplomatic agreement refers to an official agreement, treaty, deal, or substantially similar diplomatic instrument that establishes agreed actions, policies, obligations, or commitments between the United States and Iran.

A qualifying diplomatic agreement must establish Iranian policies, obligations, or commitments  aimed at permitting, restoring, or increasing vessel or shipping traffic through the Strait of Hormuz.

All listed countries must announce their acceptance of the same qualifying diplomatic agreement for the Payout Condition to be met. A joint announcement will qualify, as will separate announcements from each entity of its own acceptance of an agreement which, taken together, directly indicate that all the listed countries accepted the same agreement. Separate announcements of individual policies will not qualify if the policies are not announced as part of a diplomatic agreement.

Each announcement must be a declarative statement that clearly and unambiguously communicates acceptance of an agreement. Statements that reference ongoing negotiations or a prospective agreement, or that allude to or express support for an agreement without confirming acceptance of the agreement, do not qualify. A qualifying announcement need not reference the agreement by name or use specific terminology, provided it clearly communicates acceptance of an agreement.
 
Whether announcements from the listed countries represent a diplomatic agreement and whether such an agreement qualifies will be primarily determined through the announcements themselves. Where an announcement is made by all listed countries but, based on the announcements, it remains ambiguous whether the announcements represent a qualifying diplomatic agreement between the countries, this market will remain open until either i) definitive confirmation that the announcements represent a qualifying diplomatic agreement between the listed entities is achieved through further announcements from the listed countries or a consensus of credible reporting or ii) 14 calendar days (ET) have passed after the date that the last country made their first potentially qualifying announcement. If, at the end of the fourteenth calendar day, no definitive confirmation has been achieved, this market will resolve based on the totality of information available from the resolution sources at that time. No single statement, denial, or presentation of evidence will govern where it is contradicted by the totality of information.

The resolution sources for this market will be official information from the governments of the United States and Iran and a consensus of credible reporting.

market.question: Will Jynxzi, Ron and Los beat the Minecraft challenge by October 10?
market.rules:
Jynxzi, StableRonaldo, and Los Pollos are scheduled to begin a hardcore Minecraft marathon on October 5, 2026. Their goal, as of market creation, is to defeat the Ender Dragon in a hardcore Minecraft world without any of the three dying.

This market will resolve to "Yes" if Jynxzi, StableRonaldo, and Los Pollos defeat the Ender Dragon live on stream, as accepted by them as a successful completion of their challenge, between market creation and the specified date, 11:59 PM ET. Otherwise, this market will resolve to "No".

Only events occurring while at least one of the three players is broadcasting the challenge live will count. Footage of off-stream or previously recorded attempts will not qualify.

If the challenge is cancelled, abandoned before completion, or delayed to a point after the specified date, this market will resolve to "No".

The resolution source for this market will be footage from the official broadcasts of the challenge on Jynxzi's, StableRonaldo's, and Los Pollos's official broadcasts on YouTube and Twitch.

recent_facts.fact: Ron posted that 'tomorrow' (October 5) he would play hardcore Minecraft with Jynxzi and Los Pollos 'until we beat it,' which confirms the marathon start date.
The October rules Jynxzi gave: Los Pollos must do the main damage to the Ender Dragon, and enchantments and totems are not allowed.

Jynxzi announced the rules on about September 30 with an October 5 start: Los must kill the dragon, no crafting books, no sleeping in the Overworld, no armor for Ron, and no enchantments or totems. In hardcore, any death means a world reset. Los joked about it being 'a 10-day marathon.'
While discussing the October marathon, Jynxzi realized Los had not played Minecraft in nearly 7 years. (This post's date is approximate.)

In their previous marathon (started May 29, 2026), StableRonaldo and Jynxzi, without Los, beat the Ender Dragon in hardcore after 73 hours, with 77 total deaths. The winning run took 2 hours, on attempt 78. That run had fewer restrictions; Ron went armorless only until Day 4.
During the May run, Jynxzi died at the Ender Dragon fight by hitting an End Crystal at point-blank range, which wiped out more than 11 hours of progress. Reaching the dragon did not guarantee a kill.
For comparison, Kai Cenat and iShowSpeed finished their hardcore Minecraft marathon in 5 days, 1 hour and 2 minutes, with 42 deaths. That challenge had a different format, with four bosses.

recent_facts.fact: The 2026 Baycurrent Classic runs October 8-11, 2026 at Yokohama Country Club in Japan. The field is 72 players, the purse is $8 million, and it is the third of eight FedExCup Fall events. Schauffele is the defending champion, and Wyndham Clark is in the field.
The event has no cut for its 72 players. Under the market rules, a golfer who withdraws or does not tee off resolves No for Tournament Winner.
No player in the tournament's history (it was the Zozo Championship before the name change) has successfully defended the title. Schauffele is trying to be the first.
Schauffele is world No. 10 and has seven top-10 finishes in 2026. He won the event last year at 19-under, one shot ahead of Max Greyserman.

Schauffele has no win in 2026. He finished 14th in the FedExCup, with a 3rd at The Players Championship and a 2nd at the Rocket Classic. He shot 63 and 64 in rounds on the way to last year's Yokohama win.

Schauffele's recent form: T4 at the Tour Championship, with all four rounds in the 60s at East Lake. At the Presidents Cup he won the clinching point for the U.S. by beating Min Woo Lee in Sunday singles.
Wyndham Clark is world No. 5 and the highest-ranked player in the field. In 2026 he won the CJ Cup Byron Nelson, the U.S. Open and the BMW Championship.
Clark's three wins came in his last 11 starts. He went 1-4 at the 2026 Presidents Cup at Medinah, about two weeks before this event.
Clark's course history at Yokohama: T48 in 2025, and he did not break 70 until a closing 68.

Clark won the 2026 U.S. Open at Shinnecock Hills on June 21 by one shot over Sam Burns, going wire to wire after starting the final round six ahead. Earlier in 2026 his world ranking had fallen as low as 75th.

Other contenders in the field: past winner Collin Morikawa, Justin Thomas, Hideki Matsuyama, Jordan Spieth, Min Woo Lee, Adam Scott, Sungjae Im, Keegan Bradley, and Jacob Bridgeman, who has won twice in 2026, most recently at the Biltmore Championship Asheville.
13 players in the field played in the 2026 Presidents Cup, including Morikawa, Matsuyama and Thomas.
Tom Kim withdrew from the Baycurrent Classic after winning at the Asian Games. Search results showed no withdrawal by Schauffele or Clark.

Unverified, from memory: winners of the event from 2019 to 2025 were Woods, Cantlay, Matsuyama, Bradley, Morikawa, Echavarria and Schauffele. That is 7 different winners in 7 editions, and only 2020, played in California, was away from Japan.

market.question: Will Flávio Bolsonaro win the second round of the 2026 Brazilian presidential election by less than 4%?
market.rules:
The second round of the presidential election is scheduled to take place in Brazil on October 25, 2026.

This market will resolve according to the margin of victory between the top two candidates in the second round of the next Brazil Presidential Election.

For the purpose of this market, the “margin of victory” is defined as the absolute difference between the percentages of valid votes received by the first- and second-place candidates. Percentages of the valid votes received by each candidate will be determined by dividing the total number of valid votes each of the top two candidates receives by the sum of all valid votes cast in the election.

If the reported value falls exactly between two brackets, then this market will resolve to the higher range bracket.

If a candidate other than Flávio Bolsonaro or Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva receives the most valid votes in the second round, or if the top two candidates receive exactly the same number of valid votes, this market will resolve to "Other".

This market will resolve based on the official vote count once the vote count has been made official.

If a recount is initiated before the vote total has been made official, the market will remain open until the recount is completed and the vote is made official.

If the result of this election isn't known definitively by June 30, 2027, 11:59 PM ET, the market will resolve to "Other".

This market will resolve based on the result of the election, as indicated by a consensus of credible reporting. If there is ambiguity, this market will resolve based solely on the official results as reported by the Brazilian government, specifically the Superior Electoral Court (Tribunal Superior Eleitoral, TSE) (e.g., https://dadosabertos.tse.jus.br/).

recent_facts.fact: Final TSE first-round count: Flávio Bolsonaro (PL) got 47.03% of valid votes (56,104,503) and Lula (PT) got 45.16% (53,879,538), a gap of about 1.9 points. The runoff is on October 25, 2026.

market.question: Will CPI Core rise more than 0.3% in September? (Above 0.3%)
market.rules:
If the seasonally adjusted Consumer Price Index for All Urban Consumers: All Items less Food and Energy for September 2026, as published by the Bureau of Labor Statistics, increases by above 0.3%, then the market resolves to Yes.
Please note that the value of the Underlying is the single-decimal value reported by the BLS.

In the case of a delay in data caused by a federal government shutdown impacting the reliability of the Source Agency, the market’s latest Expiration Date will be extended to the sooner of the release of the Underlying or six months after the end of the government shutdown.

recent_facts.fact: BLS seasonally adjusted core CPI (all items less food and energy) rose 0.3% month over month in August 2026. The 12-month core rate was 2.4%, the lowest since March 2021.

Monthly core CPI changes in 2026: Jan 0.2%, Feb 0.2%, Mar 0.4%, Apr 0.2%, May 0.0%, Jun 0.2%, Jul 0.2%, Aug 0.3%. That is 7 of 8 months above 0.1% and 1 of 8 (May) at 0.1% or lower. This comes from one secondary source and was not checked against BLS directly.
The September 2026 CPI report is scheduled for release on October 14, 2026 at 8:30 a.m. ET, before the Fed's October 27–28 meeting.

Congress passed a continuing resolution (House vote 370–48) funding the federal government through December 11, 2026, and President Trump signed it on September 3. This averted an October 1 shutdown, so no shutdown delay to the BLS release is in place.

In August 2026, shelter rose 0.3% after two straight monthly gains of 0.1% (June and July). Used vehicles rose 0.4% month over month, transportation services rose 0.5%, and medical care services fell 0.2%.
August 2026 headline CPI rose 0.4% month over month (3.4% year over year). Gasoline rose 3.9% and accounted for over a third of the increase. Core's 0.3% came in above the 0.2% consensus.

The mid-September 2026 Manheim Used Vehicle Value Index fell 1.0% from August to 206.2 and was down 0.4% year over year, the first time in 2026 that wholesale used-vehicle prices fell below year-ago levels. Unadjusted wholesale prices fell 1.1% from August.

The question resolves on the one-decimal seasonally adjusted monthly percent change in CPI-U all items less food and energy as published by BLS. A reported 0.2% or higher resolves Yes; 0.1% or lower resolves No.

During the October 1–November 12, 2025 shutdown, BLS delayed the September 2025 CPI from October 15 to October 24 and canceled the October 2025 CPI. This is the only recent case of a shutdown disrupting a CPI release, and no shutdown is in effect for October 2026.

market.question: Will WTI Crude Oil (WTI) hit (HIGH) $95 in October?
market.rules:
This market will resolve to "Yes" if, at any point after market creation and during a trading session of October 2026, any Pyth 1-minute candle for the Active Month of ICE Futures Europe WTI Crude Futures (denoted by Pyth as "CLL") has a final "High" or "Low" price equal to or beyond (above for ↑ High Prices, below for ↓ Low Prices) the listed price. Otherwise, this market will resolve to "No".

Prices will be used exactly as published by Pyth, without rounding.

Only prices achieved during an applicable trading session of the specified timeframe's business days will be considered (See: "Trading Hours" at https://www.ice.com/products/213/WTI-Crude-Futures). The trading session for a given business day typically begins at 8:00 PM ET on the prior calendar date, except for the session dated Monday, which begins at 6:00 PM ET on the preceding Sunday, and where modified by holiday or other special hours (See: https://www.ice.com/holiday-hours).

The Active Month is the nearest listed contract, except during that contract's final three trading sessions. At the open of the third-to-last trading session, the next listed contract becomes the Active Month.

Each contract's last trading day will be determined by ICE Futures Europe per the WTI Crude Futures contract specification (generally the 4th US business day prior to the 25th calendar day of the month preceding the contract month, or five US business days prior if the 25th calendar day is not a US business day). The last trading day for each contract is posted at https://www.ice.com/products/213/WTI-Crude-Futures/expiry.

For example, if the last trading session for the nearest listed contract is the session for Monday the 20th, the next listed contract would become the Active Month at the start of the trading session for Thursday the 16th (8:00 PM ET on Wednesday), assuming a standard trading calendar.

If the relevant Pyth data is unavailable due to a system outage, data failure, or other disruption that prevents verification of the required 1-minute candle data, the official daily high/low price published for the Active Month WTI Crude Oil Futures contract by ICE Futures Europe may be used to determine whether the listed price was reached during the applicable trading session (See: https://www.ice.com/report/10 with "T-West Texas Intermediate Light Sweet Crude Future" selected).

In the event of a contract specification change, feed change, or similar structural modification affecting the underlying market during the listed time frame, this market will resolve based on adjusted prices as displayed on Pyth.

If the Active Month contract does not trade at all during the listed time frame, this market will resolve to "No".

The resolution source for this market is Pyth — specifically, the ICE Futures Europe WTI Crude Futures Active Month "High" and "Low" prices available at https://app.pyth.com/explore?search=CLL, with the chart settings configured for 1-minute candles. Historical 1-minute candles may be accessed by appending a Unix timestamp (seconds) to the Pyth chart URL using the "t=" parameter.

market.question: Will Jynxzi, Ron and Los beat the Minecraft challenge by October 10?
market.rules:
Jynxzi, StableRonaldo, and Los Pollos are scheduled to begin a hardcore Minecraft marathon on October 5, 2026. Their goal, as of market creation, is to defeat the Ender Dragon in a hardcore Minecraft world without any of the three dying.

This market will resolve to "Yes" if Jynxzi, StableRonaldo, and Los Pollos defeat the Ender Dragon live on stream, as accepted by them as a successful completion of their challenge, between market creation and the specified date, 11:59 PM ET. Otherwise, this market will resolve to "No".

Only events occurring while at least one of the three players is broadcasting the challenge live will count. Footage of off-stream or previously recorded attempts will not qualify.

If the challenge is cancelled, abandoned before completion, or delayed to a point after the specified date, this market will resolve to "No".

The resolution source for this market will be footage from the official broadcasts of the challenge on Jynxzi's, StableRonaldo's, and Los Pollos's official broadcasts on YouTube and Twitch.

recent_facts.fact: A YouTube compilation titled 'ALL of Los' Deaths on Day ONE of the Minecraft Marathon with Jynxzi' was posted about one day before the search. Clips describe Los dying within 10 seconds of a reset.

Jynxzi's announced marathon rules say Los Pollos must do the main damage to the Ender Dragon, with no enchantments and no totems. Market summaries list further limits: no crafting books, no sleeping in the Overworld, and no armor for Ron. Any death resets the world for all three.
Dexerto reported that the streamers said they would not sleep until they defeat the Ender Dragon, so the marathon is meant to run until they finish.
Ron posted: 'Tomorrow I will be playing HardCore Minecraft with @jynxzi and @LosPollosTV until we beat it.' The format is open-ended, with no fixed end date.
When Jynxzi went over the rules, Los Pollos pushed back, saying 'You wanna have a 10-day marathon.' He was suggesting the rules could stretch the run to about 10 days.
In the earlier Jynxzi and Ron duo hardcore marathon, they nearly finished after 32 hours, but Ron died to an Enderman in The End, with 36 deaths combined at that point.

About 57 hours into the duo marathon, Jynxzi and Ron lost their best run to the Ender Dragon, and Ron had spent up to $4K on cancelled flights home. A separate clip shows Jynxzi dying to an End Crystal at the dragon fight about 11 hours into a run.
In an earlier, separate challenge, Stable Ronaldo and FaZe Lacy beat hardcore Minecraft in under six hours with three deaths. That run had none of the current restrictions, and its date is uncertain.

recent_facts.fact: The strikes are $82,000 and $78,000. Either question resolves Yes if any Binance BTC/USDT 1-minute candle Low is at or below its strike between 00:00 ET Oct 5 and 23:59 ET Oct 11, 2026. About 3.5 days of the window remain as of Oct 8, including the weekend of Oct 10-11.

At 8:48 pm EDT on Oct 7, BTC was $83,342 and Binance BTC/USDT was 83,330. CoinDesk's daily low was 82,952.37, about $950 (1.2%) above the $82,000 strike and about $4,950 (6.0%) above $78,000. No report found shows Binance trading at or below $82,000 so far in the window.

BTC fell 4.2% from a high of $86,592 on the afternoon of Tuesday, Oct 6 to a low of $82,952 on Wednesday, Oct 7. On Thursday morning, Oct 8, it was $83,401, which is 1.7% above $82,000 and 6.9% above $78,000. It was down 2.4% over 24 hours and 0.25% over seven days.

Reports put BTC's intraday low on Bitstamp at $82,734 at about 9:45 a.m. ET on Oct 7, described as the weakest since Sept 28 and the lowest of October so far. That is $734 (0.9%) above $82,000. This is Bitstamp, not the resolution venue Binance.
On Oct 8, CoinGecko showed BTC at about $82,928, with a 24-hour range of $82,729 to $84,340. Coinbase showed about $83,309, down 3.58% on the day.
BTC was around $82,800 at 12:00 a.m. EDT on Oct 8, after a slide below $84,000 attributed to Iran tensions, rising oil and more than $400M in long liquidations.

On Oct 7, BTC broke $84,000 (7:09 a.m. EDT) and $83,000 (11:17 a.m.), then recovered about 1% to $83,500 by 12:27 p.m. Wintermute named $82,500 as the key downside level. The 10-year Treasury yield reached 5.37%, the 30-year hit a high of 5.715%, and Brent topped $100-101 after Iranian tanker attacks in the Strait of Hormuz.

The FOMC minutes released Oct 7 showed most officials expect one more rate hike this year; the policy rate is 3.75-4.00% after the September hike. At 3:18 p.m. EDT, The Atlantic reported that the White House had asked the Pentagon for Iran strike options.

Spot bitcoin ETFs took in $118.8M on Oct 6, then the non-BlackRock funds saw $277.2M of outflows on Oct 7. Over the 24 hours to Oct 8 morning, $713.2M of positions were liquidated, $651.2M of them longs ($173.9M BTC longs). Open interest fell 1.5% to $152B.

US September CPI comes out Oct 14 and the Fed decision is Oct 28, both after the window closes. Daily ETF flow reports are the only scheduled crypto catalyst found before Oct 11. No other scheduled macro release inside the window was found.

In late September, BTC dipped to an intraday low of $82,775.94. Analysts treated $81,500-$83,000 as support and $80,000 as a deeper level. No report found shows BTC trading at or below $82,000 in roughly the last 14 days (late Sept to Oct 8); this count is unverified on Binance candles.
BTC held about $83,500 on Oct 1 and $84,000 on Oct 4, so it traded between about $82.7K and $87K from late September to Oct 8. A level of $78,000 was last reported around early September.

On Binance spot, BTC fell below $84,000 early on Oct 7, trading at $83,976 at 5:01 a.m. ET. No timestamped Binance quote less than an hour old was available.

recent_facts.fact: The 2026 Baycurrent Classic runs October 8-11, 2026 at Yokohama Country Club in Japan. The field is 72 players, the purse is $8 million, and it is the third of eight FedExCup Fall events. Schauffele is the defending champion, and Wyndham Clark is in the field.

market.question: Will WTI Crude Oil (WTI) hit (LOW) $80 in October?
market.rules:
This market will resolve to "Yes" if, at any point after market creation and during a trading session of October 2026, any Pyth 1-minute candle for the Active Month of ICE Futures Europe WTI Crude Futures (denoted by Pyth as "CLL") has a final "High" or "Low" price equal to or beyond (above for ↑ High Prices, below for ↓ Low Prices) the listed price. Otherwise, this market will resolve to "No".

Prices will be used exactly as published by Pyth, without rounding.

Only prices achieved during an applicable trading session of the specified timeframe's business days will be considered (See: "Trading Hours" at https://www.ice.com/products/213/WTI-Crude-Futures). The trading session for a given business day typically begins at 8:00 PM ET on the prior calendar date, except for the session dated Monday, which begins at 6:00 PM ET on the preceding Sunday, and where modified by holiday or other special hours (See: https://www.ice.com/holiday-hours).

The Active Month is the nearest listed contract, except during that contract's final three trading sessions. At the open of the third-to-last trading session, the next listed contract becomes the Active Month.

Each contract's last trading day will be determined by ICE Futures Europe per the WTI Crude Futures contract specification (generally the 4th US business day prior to the 25th calendar day of the month preceding the contract month, or five US business days prior if the 25th calendar day is not a US business day). The last trading day for each contract is posted at https://www.ice.com/products/213/WTI-Crude-Futures/expiry.

For example, if the last trading session for the nearest listed contract is the session for Monday the 20th, the next listed contract would become the Active Month at the start of the trading session for Thursday the 16th (8:00 PM ET on Wednesday), assuming a standard trading calendar.

If the relevant Pyth data is unavailable due to a system outage, data failure, or other disruption that prevents verification of the required 1-minute candle data, the official daily high/low price published for the Active Month WTI Crude Oil Futures contract by ICE Futures Europe may be used to determine whether the listed price was reached during the applicable trading session (See: https://www.ice.com/report/10 with "T-West Texas Intermediate Light Sweet Crude Future" selected).

In the event of a contract specification change, feed change, or similar structural modification affecting the underlying market during the listed time frame, this market will resolve based on adjusted prices as displayed on Pyth.

If the Active Month contract does not trade at all during the listed time frame, this market will resolve to "No".

The resolution source for this market is Pyth — specifically, the ICE Futures Europe WTI Crude Futures Active Month "High" and "Low" prices available at https://app.pyth.com/explore?search=CLL, with the chart settings configured for 1-minute candles. Historical 1-minute candles may be accessed by appending a Unix timestamp (seconds) to the Pyth chart URL using the "t=" parameter.

market.question: Iran-Oman Hormuz Agreement by October 31?
market.rules:
This market will resolve to “Yes” if a diplomatic agreement between Oman and Iran over traffic in the strait of Hormuz is announced by the specified date, 11:59 PM ET.

A diplomatic agreement refers to an official agreement, treaty, deal, or substantially similar diplomatic instrument that establishes agreed actions, policies, obligations, or commitments between Oman and Iran.

A qualifying diplomatic agreement must establish Iranian or Omani policies, obligations, or commitments aimed at managing, permitting, restoring, or increasing vessel or shipping traffic through the Strait of Hormuz, including agreements defining vessel traffic corridors, fee collection policies, or other management policies.

All listed countries must announce their acceptance of the same qualifying diplomatic agreement for the Payout Condition to be met. A joint announcement will qualify, as will separate announcements from each entity of its own acceptance of an agreement which, taken together, directly indicate that all the listed countries accepted the same agreement. Separate announcements of individual policies will not qualify if the policies are not announced as part of a diplomatic agreement.

Each announcement must be a declarative statement that clearly and unambiguously communicates acceptance of an agreement. Statements that reference ongoing negotiations or a prospective agreement, or that allude to or express support for an agreement without confirming acceptance of the agreement, do not qualify. A qualifying announcement need not reference the agreement by name or use specific terminology, provided it clearly communicates acceptance of an agreement.
 
Whether announcements from the listed countries represent a diplomatic agreement and whether such an agreement qualifies will be primarily determined through the announcements themselves. Where an announcement is made by all listed countries but, based on the announcements, it remains ambiguous whether the announcements represent a qualifying diplomatic agreement between the countries, this market will remain open until either i) definitive confirmation that the announcements represent a qualifying diplomatic agreement between the listed entities is achieved through further announcements from the listed countries or a consensus of credible reporting or ii) 14 calendar days (ET) have passed after the date that the last country made their first potentially qualifying announcement. If, at the end of the fourteenth calendar day, no definitive confirmation has been achieved, this market will resolve based on the totality of information available from the resolution sources at that time. No single statement, denial, or presentation of evidence will govern where it is contradicted by the totality of information.

The resolution sources for this market will be official information from the governments of Oman and Iran and a consensus of credible reporting.

recent_facts.fact: The latest release covers August 2026. Seasonally adjusted CPI-U rose 0.4% in August after 0.1% in July. Core rose 0.3%, energy 2.1% and gasoline 3.9% seasonally adjusted (2.5% not seasonally adjusted). CPI was up 3.4% over 12 months.

Seasonally adjusted monthly headline CPI in 2026, with gasoline's seasonally adjusted change in brackets: Feb 0.3 (0.8), Mar 0.9 (21.2), Apr 0.6 (5.4), May 0.5 (7.0), Jun -0.4 (-9.7), Jul 0.1 (-2.9), Aug 0.4 (3.9). Only 1 of these 7 months (March) came in above 0.6%; April was exactly 0.6.

Core CPI ran 0.2, 0.2, 0.4, 0.2, 0.0, 0.2 and 0.3 from February to August 2026. In April, a 5.4% gasoline rise plus 0.4% core produced a 0.6% headline. In May, a 7.0% gasoline rise plus 0.2% core produced 0.5%.

AAA said the national average for regular gasoline was $4.33 for September 2026, a record for September, 50 cents above the previous record of $3.83 set in 2023. The October 1 average was $4.41, down nearly 7 cents from the week before.

AAA weekly national averages rose through September: $4.14 on Sep 3, $4.27 on Sep 10, $4.43 on Sep 17 and $4.48 on Sep 24, the highest ever for that time of year. AAA attributed the rise to volatility in the Strait of Hormuz and high crude prices.

market.question: Will the Democrats win the Vermont governor race in 2026?
market.rules:
This market will resolve according to the winner of the 2026 Vermont gubernatorial election.

A candidate shall be considered to represent a party in the event that he or she is the nominee of the party in question. Candidates other than the Democratic or Republican nominee (e.g., Greens, Libertarian, independent) may be added at a later date.

Candidates who run as independents will not be encompassed by the "Democrat" or "Republican" options regardless of any affiliation they may have with the party.

The candidates may be named in the contract for the convenience of traders. In the event that any named candidate is replaced as the nominee of their respective party prior to election day, the name in the contract will be updated and the market will resolve based on the replacement nominee of the party.

The resolution source for this market is the Associated Press, Fox News, and NBC. This market will resolve once all three sources call the race for the same candidate. If all three sources haven't called the race in this state for the same candidate, this market will resolve based on the official certification.

recent_facts.fact: The Vermont Public/Braun Research poll released Sept 28, 2026 has Republican Gov. Phil Scott at 42% and Democrat Amanda Janoo at 32%. Among likely voters it is Scott 44%, Janoo 34%, with 16% undecided or no opinion. Scott's job approval is 45%, down 15 points from Vermont Public's 2022 poll.

The UNH Green Mountain State Poll (835 likely voters, online, Sept 17–21, 2026, margin of error ±3.4) has Janoo at 49% and Scott at 43%, with 6% undecided and 2% for another candidate. The pollsters called it a statistical tie.

In UNH's July poll Scott led Janoo by 15 points, so its September poll is a 21-point swing toward Janoo. In UNH polling, Scott's approval fell from 61% (October 2025) to 52% (July 2026) to 47% (September 2026).
Scott was still rated the most popular governor in the country in Morning Consult's July 2026 data. His campaign says public polling has always undercounted his support.

Scott won the Republican primary with 98.5% (21,466 votes), facing only write-ins, and is the Republican nominee. Janoo won the Democratic primary with 49.1% (39,614 votes) to Aly Richards' 46.6% (37,570). Democratic primary turnout was about 80,700, compared with about 21,800 on the Republican side.

Three minor candidates are also on the general election ballot: June Goodband (Green Mountain Peace and Justice), Brian Judd (independent) and Dean Roy (Freedom and Unity). Bernie Sanders, the Vermont Democratic Party and 2022 nominee Brendan Brendan... [see correction]

Janoo outraised Scott in September, $291,000 to $223,000. Cycle totals are $706,000 raised for Janoo and $414,000 for Scott; cash on hand is $280,000 for Janoo and $296,000 for Scott. Scott spent about $137,000 on TV ads in September and Janoo about $60,000.
Scott said Democratic enthusiasm is the toughest reelection headwind he has faced since 2016. He defended unpopular decisions such as calling state employees back to the office.

In July 2026, after Scott's approval hit a four-year low in UNH polling, a UNH pollster said this could be the year Democrats unseat him. Coverage links part of his decline to his vetoes of progressive bills.
Two debates remain: Vermont Public on Oct 21, 2026 at 7 p.m. and WCAX on Oct 28, 2026 at 7 p.m. Scott has turned down earlier candidate forums. Election day is Nov 3, 2026.

Vermont elects its governor to a two-year term, and Scott is running for a sixth. If no candidate gets a majority of the vote, the Vermont General Assembly picks the governor from the top three, so a plurality win alone may not settle the race.

market.question: Will Jynxzi, Ron and Los beat the Minecraft challenge by October 10?
market.rules:
Jynxzi, StableRonaldo, and Los Pollos are scheduled to begin a hardcore Minecraft marathon on October 5, 2026. Their goal, as of market creation, is to defeat the Ender Dragon in a hardcore Minecraft world without any of the three dying.

This market will resolve to "Yes" if Jynxzi, StableRonaldo, and Los Pollos defeat the Ender Dragon live on stream, as accepted by them as a successful completion of their challenge, between market creation and the specified date, 11:59 PM ET. Otherwise, this market will resolve to "No".

Only events occurring while at least one of the three players is broadcasting the challenge live will count. Footage of off-stream or previously recorded attempts will not qualify.

If the challenge is cancelled, abandoned before completion, or delayed to a point after the specified date, this market will resolve to "No".

The resolution source for this market will be footage from the official broadcasts of the challenge on Jynxzi's, StableRonaldo's, and Los Pollos's official broadcasts on YouTube and Twitch.

recent_facts.fact: As of October 8, 2026, I found no report of Jynxzi, StableRonaldo and Los Pollos defeating the Ender Dragon. A Dexerto post from about two days earlier said the streamers 'aren't going to sleep until they defeat the Ender Dragon,' so the run appeared to still be going then.
Unverified fan clips show the group reaching the Nether about 24 hours into the marathon, and Ron dying on his first trip into the Nether. That death forced a reset.

Jynxzi's rules for the trio run: Los Pollos must do the main damage to the Ender Dragon, and enchantments and totems are banned. Other summaries add no crafting books, no sleeping in the overworld, and no armor for Ron.
While going over the rules before the start, Los Pollos joked to Jynxzi: 'You wanna have a 10-day marathon.'
In Jynxzi and Ron's earlier 24/7 duo hardcore marathon (late May 2026), they beat the Ender Dragon after about 73 hours. One summary said it took about 78 attempts and roughly 77 deaths (unverified).

In the May 2026 duo run, Jynxzi died in an Ender Dragon fight after hitting an End Crystal at point-blank range, losing more than 11 hours of progress in that world. Reaching the dragon did not guarantee a win.
In a comparable streamer marathon, Kai Cenat and IShowSpeed beat hardcore Minecraft after about 5 days, 1 hour (Aug 17–22, 2024), with 42 deaths/resets.
StableRonaldo and FaZe Lacy beat hardcore Minecraft in about 5–6 hours with 3 deaths in August 2024. Ron has finished a hardcore run before.

market.question: Will Mary Peltola win the Alaska Senate race in 2026?
market.rules:
This market will resolve according to the winner of the 2026 midterm Alaska U.S. Senate election, inclusive of any run-offs, currently scheduled for November 3, 2026.

If the results of the election are not confirmed by July 31, 2027, this market will resolve to "Other".

The resolution source for this market is the Associated Press, Fox News, and NBC. This market will resolve once all three sources call the race for the same candidate. If all three sources haven’t called the race in this state for the same candidate, this market will resolve based on official certification.

recent_facts.source: Wikipedia (2026 United States Senate election in Alaska)
recent_facts.fact: Polls since early September give mixed first-choice results. AARP (Fabrizio/Impact, Sep 8–11): Peltola 46, Sullivan 41. Alaska Survey Research (Sep 10–12): Peltola 48, Sullivan 44. Rasmussen (Sep 13–14): 39–39. co/efficient (R, Sep 14–17): Sullivan 48, Peltola 46. Trafalgar (R, Sep 22–24): Sullivan 47, Peltola 46. NYT/Siena (Sep 24–Oct 1, 504 LV, ±5.1): Peltola 50, Sullivan 43. Quantus (R, Sep 28–30): 46–46.

recent_facts.source: Wikipedia (2026 United States Senate election in Alaska)
recent_facts.fact: The polling average the page cites, as of 2026-10-03, is Peltola 48.7% and Sullivan 45.8%. In polls that ran the ranked-choice rounds, Peltola wins the final round 52–48 (ASR, Sep 10–12) and 53–47 (AARP, Sep 8–11).
In a new Alaska Survey Research poll of likely voters, Peltola leads Sullivan 51% to 49% after the third round of ranked-choice tabulation.
The RealClearPolitics average has Peltola at 48.5% and Sullivan at 47.3%, a Peltola lead of about 1.2 points.

In the Aug 18, 2026 top-four primary, Peltola (D) won 82,244 votes (49.5%) and incumbent Dan S. Sullivan (R) won 68,726 (41.4%). Daniel J. Sullivan Jr. took 2.5%, David Leslie (D) 1.1% and Gerald Heikes (R) 1.1%. Leslie withdrew under pressure from Democratic leadership, so the November ballot is Peltola, Dan S. Sullivan, Daniel J. Sullivan Jr. and Heikes. The two minor candidates are both registered Republicans.

A same-name candidate, Dan J. Sullivan of Petersburg, will appear on the November ballot with no party label. Republicans accuse him of being a Democratic plant meant to draw votes away from the incumbent. In polls he takes about 1–7% of first choices.

Since mid-July, outside groups backing Sullivan have spent about $15.5–20 million on ads and groups backing Peltola about $15.4 million. The Senate Leadership Fund has spent more than $8 million and Trump's super PAC about $3.6 million since early September.

Peltola's campaign raised $6.9 million in Q2 2026 to Sullivan's $2 million, and raised a record of about $8.9 million in Q1. Sullivan had more cash on hand: $8.3 million versus her $6.1 million. Q3 reports are due in mid-October.

recent_facts.source: Alaska's News Source / NYT-Siena (result from recall, unverified)
recent_facts.fact: In 2020, NYT/Siena's October poll had Sullivan leading Al Gross 45–37. Sullivan won by roughly 12–13 points (about 53.9–41.2, recalled and unverified), so the polls understated him.

In 2024 Peltola lost the at-large House seat to Begich: 46.4% to 48.4% on first choices and 48.7% to 51.3% after ranked-choice tabulation. ASR's final 2024 presidential poll had Trump at 55–45, and Trump won Alaska by about 13.
Democrats have not won a U.S. Senate election in Alaska since 2008, when Begich won. Sullivan won the seat in 2014 and 2020.

The general election is November 3, 2026, under ranked-choice voting with four candidates. If no one has a majority of first choices, Alaska runs the ranked-choice tabulation after absentee ballots arrive, typically about two weeks after election day. That means calls by AP, Fox and NBC may come after the question closes on Nov 4.
The question resolves when AP, Fox News and NBC have all called the race for the same candidate; otherwise it resolves on official certification. The results include the ranked-choice rounds.

market.question: Will the rate of core CPI inflation be above 2.4% for the year ending in September 2026? (Above 2.4%)
market.rules:
If the Consumer Price Index (CPI) for All Urban Consumers: All Items less Food and Energy increases by more than 2.4% in the twelve months ending September 2026 (as represented by the one-decimal place value reported by the Bureau of Labor Statistics), then the market resolves to Yes.
In the case of a delay in data caused by a federal government shutdown impacting the reliability of the Source Agency, the market’s latest Expiration Date will be extended to the sooner of the release of the Underlying or six months after the end of the government shutdown.

recent_facts.source: U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics (CPI Table 1)
recent_facts.fact: The unadjusted CPI-U index for all items less food and energy was 338.041 in August 2026, 337.133 in July 2026 and 329.970 in August 2025. BLS reported the 12-month change through August 2026 as 2.4%. From these index levels, the unrounded figure works out to about 2.446%.

recent_facts.source: U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics (CPI Table 1)
recent_facts.fact: Seasonally adjusted monthly changes in core CPI were 0.0% from May to June 2026, 0.2% from June to July 2026 and 0.3% from July to August 2026.

recent_facts.source: Ball State University CBER (from BLS data); BLS September 2025 CPI release
recent_facts.fact: The unadjusted core CPI index for September 2025 was about 330.54, up 3.03% from a year earlier (this level comes from a secondary source). The BLS release for September 2025 showed core up 0.2% seasonally adjusted that month and 3.0% over 12 months. 330.54 against 329.970 means the unadjusted increase from August to September 2025 was about 0.17%.

recent_facts.source: Derived from BLS index levels above
recent_facts.fact: For the published one-decimal figure to be 2.5% or higher, the September 2026 unadjusted core index needs to reach about 338.64 (330.54 × 1.0245). That is an unadjusted rise of about 0.18% or more from August's 338.041. In September 2025, the unadjusted change (about 0.17%) was roughly 0.05 percentage points below the seasonally adjusted change (0.227%).

Core CPI 12-month rates in 2026 were: Jan 2.5%, Feb 2.5%, Mar 2.6%, Apr 2.8%, May 2.9%, Jun 2.6%, Jul 2.5%, Aug 2.4%. The 2025 rates were Aug 3.1% and Sep 3.0%. October 2025 data was never published because of the 2025 lapse in appropriations.

recent_facts.source: Advisor Perspectives / news coverage of August CPI
recent_facts.fact: Headline CPI was up 3.4% year over year in August 2026, driven by energy: the energy index was up 16.3% year over year and gasoline was up 27.4%. Core at 2.4% was the lowest core rate since March 2021, and the 0.3% monthly core gain was one tenth above consensus.
One blog reported August core as +0.29% month over month unrounded and the 12-month rate easing from 2.48% to 2.45%. This is unverified; BLS index levels imply about 2.446%.
The September 2026 CPI release is scheduled for Wednesday, October 14, 2026 at 8:30 AM ET, the same day the question closes.

Jynxzi, StableRonaldo, and Los Pollos are scheduled to begin a hardcore Minecraft marathon on October 5, 2026. Their goal, as of market creation, is to defeat the Ender Dragon in a hardcore Minecraft world without any of the three dying.

This market will resolve to "Yes" if Jynxzi, StableRonaldo, and Los Pollos defeat the Ender Dragon live on stream, as accepted by them as a successful completion of their challenge, between market creation and the specified date, 11:59 PM ET. Otherwise, this market will resolve to "No".

Only events occurring while at least one of the three players is broadcasting the challenge live will count. Footage of off-stream or previously recorded attempts will not qualify.

If the challenge is cancelled, abandoned before completion, or delayed to a point after the specified date, this market will resolve to "No".

The resolution source for this market will be footage from the official broadcasts of the challenge on Jynxzi's, StableRonaldo's, and Los Pollos's official broadcasts on YouTube and Twitch.

recent_facts.fact: As of October 8, 2026, I found no report of Jynxzi, StableRonaldo and Los Pollos defeating the Ender Dragon. A Dexerto post from about two days earlier said the streamers 'aren't going to sleep until they defeat the Ender Dragon,' so the run appeared to still be going then.
Unverified fan clips show the group reaching the Nether about 24 hours into the marathon, and Ron dying on his first trip into the Nether. That death forced a reset.

Jynxzi's rules for the trio run: Los Pollos must do the main damage to the Ender Dragon, and enchantments and totems are banned. Other summaries add no crafting books, no sleeping in the overworld, and no armor for Ron.
While going over the rules before the start, Los Pollos joked to Jynxzi: 'You wanna have a 10-day marathon.'
In Jynxzi and Ron's earlier 24/7 duo hardcore marathon (late May 2026), they beat the Ender Dragon after about 73 hours. One summary said it took about 78 attempts and roughly 77 deaths (unverified).

In the May 2026 duo run, Jynxzi died in an Ender Dragon fight after hitting an End Crystal at point-blank range, losing more than 11 hours of progress in that world. Reaching the dragon did not guarantee a win.
In a comparable streamer marathon, Kai Cenat and IShowSpeed beat hardcore Minecraft after about 5 days, 1 hour (Aug 17–22, 2024), with 42 deaths/resets.
StableRonaldo and FaZe Lacy beat hardcore Minecraft in about 5–6 hours with 3 deaths in August 2024. Ron has finished a hardcore run before.

facts_dropped.fact: The trio's marathon started October 5, 2026. Day one logged 48 combined deaths, 34 of them by Los Pollos. One summary also said attempt 61 had gone past 23 hours with frequent resets. These are unverified tallies, and another source put day-one deaths at 42.
facts_dropped.reason: names a prediction market or sportsbook

facts_dropped.fact: This is hardcore mode, so any death by any of the three ends the world and forces a full reset. A market description also says Los Pollos has very little Minecraft experience, with one session about eight years ago.
facts_dropped.reason: names a prediction market or sportsbook

facts_dropped.fact: The deadlines are October 9 and October 10 at 11:59 PM ET. Those fall at the end of day 5 and day 6 counted from the October 5 start, and the dragon kill has to happen live on stream.

market.question: Bitcoin price on Oct 8, 2026? ($82,500 or above)
market.rules:
If the simple average of the sixty seconds of CF Benchmarks' Bitcoin Real-Time Index (BRTI) before 5 PM EDT is above 82499.99 at 5 PM EDT on Oct 8, 2026, then the market resolves to Yes.
Not all cryptocurrency price data is the same. While checking a source like Google or Coinbase may help guide your decision, the price used to determine this market is based on CF Benchmarks' corresponding Real Time Index (RTI). At the last minute before expiration, 60 RTI prices are collected. The official and final value is the average of these prices.

recent_facts.fact: At 1:19 AM EDT on Oct 8, BTC was about $82,810, down 1.84%. That is about 0.38% above $82,500 and about 0.07% above $82,750.

In Asian morning trading on Oct 8, BTC fell 1.6% to just under $82,800, breaking below $83,000, which FxPro called the recent low. FxPro said a break there could send BTC to $80,000 'fairly quickly.' Brent rose 2% to above $102 after a report that the White House asked the Pentagon for strike options against Iran, and the 10-year Treasury yield rose to 5.31%, close to its highest since 2002.
At 1:35 AM UTC Oct 8, BTC was about $83,364, down about 2% over 24h. The 24h range was $82,896 to $85,309, with support listed near $82,871 and resistance near $87,061.
CoinGecko listed BTC at about $82,928, down 1.30% over 24h and down 0.40% over 7 days.

BTC fell 4.2% from a high of $86,592 on the afternoon of Oct 6 to a low of $82,952 on Oct 7 (CoinGecko hourly data). It was $83,401 on the morning of Oct 8, down 2.4% over 24h but only 0.25% over 7 days. Support was cited near $82,950.

Spot bitcoin ETFs took in $118.8M on Oct 6. On Oct 7, funds other than BlackRock's IBIT reported $277.2M of outflows, with IBIT's figure still pending. Ether ETFs had net outflows on 7 straight trading days through Oct 7, totaling at least $452.7M.

CoinGlass showed $546.89M of crypto liquidations over 24h, about 88% of them longs ($479.73M), including $142.87M in BTC. BTC perpetual futures open interest was $69.29B. Spot BTC ETFs had a net outflow of $89.9M on Oct 5.

BTC had traded in a range of about $83,000 to $87,000 for about two weeks, and $87,000 had capped rallies since late September. So over most of the last 14 days BTC traded above both strikes, and the move below about $83,000 on Oct 7–8 was a new low for the range. I did not find a verified daily count of closes below $82,750.

The Fed minutes from the Sept 15–16 meeting were released Oct 7. That meeting raised rates 25bp to 3.75–4.00%, and the minutes say most participants thought a further increase by year-end would probably be appropriate.

Neither source lists a scheduled US macro release for Oct 8 before the 5 PM EDT settlement. Daily ETF flow data and oil/Iran headlines are the ongoing drivers. US September CPI is due Oct 14 and the next Fed decision Oct 27–28. Oct 8 is a Thursday, so there is no weekend effect.

BTC's all-time high is $126,080 (Oct 6, 2025), and BTC is about 33% below it. On Oct 7 the session range was $83,647.88 to $86,648.14, about 3.6%. That intraday range is about 8–25 times the current distance to each strike.

market.question: Will Bitcoin dip to $82,000 October 5-11?
market.rules:
This market will immediately resolve to "Yes" if any Binance 1 minute candle for Bitcoin (BTC/USDT) during the date range specified in the title (from 12:00 AM ET on the first date to 11:59 PM ET on the last) has a final "Low" price equal to or lower than the price specified in the title. Otherwise, this market will resolve to "No."

The resolution source for this market is Binance, specifically the BTC/USDT "Low" prices available at https://www.binance.com/en/trade/BTC_USDT, with the chart settings on "1m" candles selected on the top bar.

Please note that the outcome of this market depends solely on the price data from the Binance BTC/USDT trading pair. Prices from other exchanges, different trading pairs, or spot markets will not be considered for the resolution of this market.

recent_facts.fact: The strikes are $82,000 and $78,000. Either question resolves Yes if any Binance BTC/USDT 1-minute candle Low is at or below its strike between 00:00 ET Oct 5 and 23:59 ET Oct 11, 2026. About 3.5 days of the window remain as of Oct 8, including the weekend of Oct 10-11.

At 8:48 pm EDT on Oct 7, BTC was $83,342 and Binance BTC/USDT was 83,330. CoinDesk's daily low was 82,952.37, about $950 (1.2%) above the $82,000 strike and about $4,950 (6.0%) above $78,000. No report found shows Binance trading at or below $82,000 so far in the window.

BTC fell 4.2% from a high of $86,592 on the afternoon of Tuesday, Oct 6 to a low of $82,952 on Wednesday, Oct 7. On Thursday morning, Oct 8, it was $83,401, which is 1.7% above $82,000 and 6.9% above $78,000. It was down 2.4% over 24 hours and 0.25% over seven days.

Reports put BTC's intraday low on Bitstamp at $82,734 at about 9:45 a.m. ET on Oct 7, described as the weakest since Sept 28 and the lowest of October so far. That is $734 (0.9%) above $82,000. This is Bitstamp, not the resolution venue Binance.
On Oct 8, CoinGecko showed BTC at about $82,928, with a 24-hour range of $82,729 to $84,340. Coinbase showed about $83,309, down 3.58% on the day.
BTC was around $82,800 at 12:00 a.m. EDT on Oct 8, after a slide below $84,000 attributed to Iran tensions, rising oil and more than $400M in long liquidations.

On Oct 7, BTC broke $84,000 (7:09 a.m. EDT) and $83,000 (11:17 a.m.), then recovered about 1% to $83,500 by 12:27 p.m. Wintermute named $82,500 as the key downside level. The 10-year Treasury yield reached 5.37%, the 30-year hit a high of 5.715%, and Brent topped $100-101 after Iranian tanker attacks in the Strait of Hormuz.

The FOMC minutes released Oct 7 showed most officials expect one more rate hike this year; the policy rate is 3.75-4.00% after the September hike. At 3:18 p.m. EDT, The Atlantic reported that the White House had asked the Pentagon for Iran strike options.

Spot bitcoin ETFs took in $118.8M on Oct 6, then the non-BlackRock funds saw $277.2M of outflows on Oct 7. Over the 24 hours to Oct 8 morning, $713.2M of positions were liquidated, $651.2M of them longs ($173.9M BTC longs). Open interest fell 1.5% to $152B.

US September CPI comes out Oct 14 and the Fed decision is Oct 28, both after the window closes. Daily ETF flow reports are the only scheduled crypto catalyst found before Oct 11. No other scheduled macro release inside the window was found.
On Oct 3, BTC fell to $84,600 after being rejected near $87,000, with $433M in long liquidations.

In late September, BTC dipped to an intraday low of $82,775.94. Analysts treated $81,500-$83,000 as support and $80,000 as a deeper level. No report found shows BTC trading at or below $82,000 in roughly the last 14 days (late Sept to Oct 8); this count is unverified on Binance candles.
BTC held about $83,500 on Oct 1 and $84,000 on Oct 4, so it traded between about $82.7K and $87K from late September to Oct 8. A level of $78,000 was last reported around early September.
In early September 2026, BTC traded at about $78,686, after falling to $76,871 on Aug 31. Both are below the $78,000 strike, but more than a month before the current window.
On Binance spot, BTC fell below $84,000 early on Oct 7, trading at $83,976 at 5:01 a.m. ET. No timestamped Binance quote less than an hour old was available.

market.question: Baycurrent Classic: Max Homa wins
market.rules:
If Max Homa wins the Baycurrent Classic, then the market resolves to Yes.
If a golfer forfeits, withdraws, or does not participate prior to teeing off, their contracts will resolve as follows:
Tournament Winner and End of Round Leader markets will resolve to No
Finishing Position, Make the Cut, Head-to-Head, and 3-Ball markets will resolve to Fair Market Value

recent_facts.fact: The 2026 Baycurrent Classic runs October 8-11, 2026 at Yokohama Country Club in Japan. The field is 72 players, the purse is $8 million, and it is the third of eight FedExCup Fall events. Schauffele is the defending champion, and Wyndham Clark is in the field.
The event has no cut for its 72 players. Under the market rules, a golfer who withdraws or does not tee off resolves No for Tournament Winner.
No player in the tournament's history (it was the Zozo Championship before the name change) has successfully defended the title. Schauffele is trying to be the first.
Schauffele is world No. 10 and has seven top-10 finishes in 2026. He won the event last year at 19-under, one shot ahead of Max Greyserman.

Schauffele has no win in 2026. He finished 14th in the FedExCup, with a 3rd at The Players Championship and a 2nd at the Rocket Classic. He shot 63 and 64 in rounds on the way to last year's Yokohama win.

Schauffele's recent form: T4 at the Tour Championship, with all four rounds in the 60s at East Lake. At the Presidents Cup he won the clinching point for the U.S. by beating Min Woo Lee in Sunday singles.
Wyndham Clark is world No. 5 and the highest-ranked player in the field. In 2026 he won the CJ Cup Byron Nelson, the U.S. Open and the BMW Championship.
Clark's three wins came in his last 11 starts. He went 1-4 at the 2026 Presidents Cup at Medinah, about two weeks before this event.
Clark's course history at Yokohama: T48 in 2025, and he did not break 70 until a closing 68.

Clark won the 2026 U.S. Open at Shinnecock Hills on June 21 by one shot over Sam Burns, going wire to wire after starting the final round six ahead. Earlier in 2026 his world ranking had fallen as low as 75th.

Other contenders in the field: past winner Collin Morikawa, Justin Thomas, Hideki Matsuyama, Jordan Spieth, Min Woo Lee, Adam Scott, Sungjae Im, Keegan Bradley, and Jacob Bridgeman, who has won twice in 2026, most recently at the Biltmore Championship Asheville.
13 players in the field played in the 2026 Presidents Cup, including Morikawa, Matsuyama and Thomas.
Tom Kim withdrew from the Baycurrent Classic after winning at the Asian Games. Search results showed no withdrawal by Schauffele or Clark.

Unverified, from memory: winners of the event from 2019 to 2025 were Woods, Cantlay, Matsuyama, Bradley, Morikawa, Echavarria and Schauffele. That is 7 different winners in 7 editions, and only 2020, played in California, was away from Japan.

market.question: US announces end of Iranian blockade by October 15, 2026?
market.rules:
On July 13, 2026, Trump announced the United States would reinstate its naval blockade of Iran, targeting Iranian ships and customers.

This market will resolve to “Yes” if the United States government, or an authorized representative of the United States government, publicly and officially announces the end, termination, lifting, or suspension of the United States’ naval blockade on Iranian ships and ships of Iranian customers, between market creation and the specified date, 11:59 PM ET. Otherwise, this market will resolve to “No”.

An announcement qualifies if it communicates that the United States will generally cease blocking vessel traffic for Iranian ships and customers, including an announcement that the blockade will not take effect at all, even if some restrictions remain (for example, an imposition of fees). An announcement does not qualify if it reflects only a limited or partial change that stops short of a general end or suspension of the blockade, for example, an exemption for a specific vessel, cargo, or port.

A qualifying announcement must be a declarative statement of the United States government’s present termination or suspension of the blockade, previously-unannounced prior termination or suspension of the blockade, or definitive decision to terminate or suspend the blockade.

A qualifying announcement must clearly and unambiguously identify the end or suspension of the blockade. Statements that merely allude to, reference, or describe an end to the blockade, without clearly communicating it, do not qualify. The announcement need not use specific terminology or reference the end of a blockade by name; an announcement of a resumption of prior obligations, the maintenance of a status quo, or a return to a previously agreed baseline qualifies, provided the substantive policy of ending or suspending the blockade is clearly and unambiguously communicated.

A qualifying announcement must be made through official channels, by an individual acting in an official capacity. Statements made incidentally or informally in a context not intended for official communication do not qualify.

The following do not qualify:

Anonymous, unattributed, or leaked statements not confirmed as official;
Statements by persons not authorized to speak for the United States government;
Third-party speculation, analysis, or predictions that the United States government will announce or implement an end to the blockade;
Satirical, fabricated, hacked, or impersonated communications; and
Statements that describe a prospective, contingent, probable, or conditional end to the blockade rather than announcing a present and decided position.

Once a qualifying announcement is made, this market will resolve to “Yes” regardless of whether it is later reversed, or whether the blockade actually ends in practice.

Resolution will be based on official information from the United States government, including the President, the Department of Defense, the Department of State, and United States Central Command (CENTCOM), or the official representatives of the United States government.

recent_facts.fact: As of October 8, 2026, the US-led naval blockade of Iran was still in place and no agreement had been announced. Tanker data showed Iran had loaded no crude since late August.

Trump said Washington would soon decide whether to end the war 'the nice way or the not-so-nice way.' Vance said Iran must significantly cut its nuclear enrichment capacity to get a permanent ceasefire, and that backchannel talks with President Pezeshkian and FM Araghchi are underway.

The Pentagon reportedly told CENTCOM to prepare for a possible resumption of major combat operations against Iran. The White House reportedly asked for strike options before the November 3 midterms, though no final decision had been made.

CENTCOM said it had redirected 130 commercial vessels since the blockade restarted on July 14, the latest on October 5. It said it had also disabled 3 vessels and destroyed 13 over about 12 weeks. CENTCOM commander Brad Cooper said the mission remains a priority.
Trump rejected Iran's seven-day plan, which would have reopened Hormuz in exchange for the US lifting its blockade, releasing frozen assets and waiving oil sanctions, calling it not 'acceptable.'

Iran's top negotiator said the Strait of Hormuz will stay closed until the US accepts Tehran's seven-day plan. Iran insists the blockade be resolved first, while a US official said on September 28 there would be no deal unless Iran's nuclear program is addressed.

recent_facts.source: Gulf News / Iran Foreign Ministry (via search summary)
recent_facts.fact: Iran and Oman agreed on coordinates for safe transit routes through the Strait of Hormuz. Qatar said its US-Iran mediation continues and messages are still being exchanged, and Russia offered to mediate.
President Pezeshkian ruled out talks with the US, and a third tanker in two days was hit near Hormuz.
The tracker listed the Strait of Hormuz as effectively closed on Day 221, with 4 ships transiting on October 4 versus about 85 a day normally.

The only earlier official lifting came after a deal: on June 15 Trump said an agreement was reached and authorized the blockade's removal, and CENTCOM announced on June 18 that it had been lifted. That first phase ran April 13 to June 18, about 9 weeks.
On May 29, 2026, Trump posted on Truth Social that the blockade would be lifted, tied to a memorandum that had not been signed. The formal lifting came about 3 weeks later, on June 18.
Trump announced the renewed blockade along with Hormuz tolls on July 13 after the June ceasefire collapsed. The second phase began July 14 and had lasted about 12 weeks as of October 8.

No formal talks are scheduled. The upcoming dates noted in reporting are the US midterms on November 3 and the reported pre-midterm strike-option planning. The questions close October 15 and October 31 at 11:59 PM ET.

market.question: Will the Federal Reserve Hike rates by 0bps at their October 2026 meeting? (Fed maintains rate)
market.rules:
If the Federal Reserve does a Hike of 0bps on October 28, 2026, then the market resolves to Yes.
The outcomes are mutually exclusive: at most one can resolve to Yes. For example, a 50-basis-point hike resolves “Hike   25 bps” to Yes and “Hike 25 bps” to No.

If the scheduled FOMC meeting is canceled and does not occur on its scheduled date, “Fed maintains rate” resolves to Yes and all other outcomes resolve to No.

recent_facts.source: CNBC / Federal Reserve Bank of Atlanta (FOMC statement)
recent_facts.fact: At its September 15–16, 2026 meeting the FOMC voted 12-0 to raise the federal funds target range by 25 bps, from 3.50%–3.75% to 3.75%–4.00%. It was the first increase since 2023.

In the September dot plot, 16 of 18 participants projected at least one more hike in 2026. The median 2026 year-end rate was 4.1%, which equals one more 25 bp hike at either the October or December meeting. Some reports say four participants projected two more hikes.

The next FOMC meeting is October 27–28, 2026, less than a week before the US midterm elections. Minutes of the September meeting are due around October 7. Reuters describes the Fed as appearing set to hold in October and says analysts doubt another hike will come that close to the midterms.

The September jobs report showed payrolls up just 29,000, against an expected 88,000. August was revised to 133,000 and unemployment rose to 4.2% from 4.1%. Job creation has averaged about 45,000 a month over the past year. (Report date estimated as the first Friday of October.)
NY Fed President John Williams said the September hike had 'removed any urgency' and that one more increase 'may be appropriate before the end of 2026.'

Vice Chair Philip Jefferson said officials will 'need to come to our own judgment, which may take more time.' On the hawkish side, Boston Fed President Susan Collins said inflation has been 'too high for too long,' and KC Fed President Jeff Schmid said 'we just haven't fulfilled our promise on the inflation side.'
A White House economist said, citing the weak September jobs report, that Fed rate hikes may be over for 2026.
Fed Chair Kevin Warsh said 'inflation is too high' and described the September hike as removing a 'dose of accommodation.' He said the Fed wants a 'timelier' approach to curbing inflation.

In his Jackson Hole speech, Warsh cited 12-month PCE inflation of 3.7% and a six-month annualized rate of 4.1%. He said underlying inflation 'has not meaningfully improved.' Cleveland Fed President Beth Hammack said 'it is time for the Fed to act with rate hikes.' (Exact date unverified.)
September CPI is due October 14, 2026, which is the main inflation release left before the October 28 decision. The September PCE report is due October 29, one day after the decision.

The outcomes are mutually exclusive. If the FOMC leaves the 3.75%–4.00% range unchanged on October 28, or the meeting is canceled, 'Fed maintains rate' resolves Yes. A 25 bp increase to 4.00%–4.25% resolves 'Hike 25bps' Yes, and a 50 bp hike resolves both of these No.

facts_dropped.fact: August core PCE rose 0.2% m/m, below the 0.3% forecast. Year-over-year core PCE was 3.0% for August, and July was revised down to 3.0% from 3.3%. Headline PCE was 3.4% y/y.
facts_dropped.reason: makes a prediction

market.question: Will the Fed increase interest rates by 25 bps after the October 2026 meeting?
market.rules:
The FED interest rates are defined in this market by the upper bound of the target federal funds range. The decisions on the target federal funds range are made by the Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) meetings.

This market will resolve to the amount of basis points the upper bound of the target federal funds rate is changed by versus the level it was prior to the Federal Reserve's October 2026 meeting.

If the target federal funds rate is changed to a level not expressed in the displayed options, the change will be rounded up to the nearest 25 and will resolve to the relevant bracket. (e.g. if there's a cut/increase of 12.5 bps it will be considered to be 25 bps)

The resolution source for this market is the FOMC’s statement after its meeting scheduled for October 27-28, 2026 according to the official calendar: https://www.federalreserve.gov/monetarypolicy/fomccalendars.htm.

The level and change of the target federal funds rate is also published at the official website of the Federal Reserve at https://www.federalreserve.gov/monetarypolicy/openmarket.htm.

This market may resolve as soon as the FOMC’s statement for their October meeting with relevant data is issued. If no statement is released by the end date of the next scheduled meeting, this market will resolve to the "No change" bracket.

recent_facts.fact: At its September 15-16, 2026 meeting the FOMC voted 12-0 to raise the federal funds target range by 25 bps to 3.75%-4.00%, its first increase since 2023. This is the level the October change will be measured from (upper bound 4.00%).

The September minutes, released October 7, said 'most participants assessed that another increase in the target range for the federal funds rate would likely be appropriate by year end,' but gave no indication of timing. They added that decisions depend on incoming information. The remaining 2026 decisions are October 28 and December 9.

New York Fed President and FOMC Vice Chair John Williams said there is no urgency in deciding when to raise rates again, and Fed Vice Chair Philip Jefferson echoed that view. Reuters reported that investors who had expected hikes in both October and December changed their view after these comments, and that the Fed now seems set to hold in October.

Dallas Fed President Lorie Logan believes at least two more quarter-point hikes will be needed to control inflation. Chair Kevin Warsh has not spoken publicly since his September 16 press conference, in line with his pledge to give less policy guidance.

September payrolls rose by only 29,000, against a Dow Jones consensus of 84,000. Unemployment rose to 4.2% from 4.1%. Revisions cut July/August by a combined 60,000 (July is now -10,000), and average hourly earnings rose 0.1% m/m and 3% y/y.

Fed staff estimated PCE inflation at 3.8% y/y for August. Reuters noted that August inflation rose less than expected. The minutes said some participants saw the September hike as a risk-management 'insurance' move, while others saw it as necessary to curb inflation.
At the July 2026 meeting the Fed held rates, and three FOMC members dissented in favor of a quarter-point hike.
September 2026 CPI is scheduled for October 14, 2026 at 8:30 a.m. ET. This is the main inflation release before the October 27-28 FOMC meeting, and the Fed can also estimate September PCE from it.

The FOMC meets October 27-28, 2026, with the statement due at 2:00 p.m. ET on October 28, less than a week before the U.S. midterm congressional elections. The next meeting after that is December 8-9.
Coverage of the minutes reported that after the weak September jobs data, investors were positioned for the Fed to keep rates unchanged at the October 27-28 meeting.

Since the 1994 shock tightening, the Fed has generally prepared markets before acting rather than surprising them. Unverified: no cited count was found of FOMC decisions that went against market expectations on the eve of the meeting.
