market.question: Will Benjamin Netanyahu be the next Prime Minister of Israel?
market.rules:
Legislative elections are schedule to be held in Israel on October 27, 2026. 

This market will resolve to the next individual who is officially appointed and sworn in as Prime Minister of Israel following the 2026 parliamentary election. If an election is called early, this market will immediately resolve to the individual who is officially appointed and sworn in after that election.

To count for resolution, the individual must be formally sworn in. Any interim or caretaker Prime Minister will not count toward the resolution of this market.

If no such Prime Minister is sworn in by December 31, 2027, 11:59 PM ET, this market will resolve to “Other”.

The primary resolution source for this market will be official information from the Government of Israel; however, a consensus of credible reporting may also be used.

recent_facts.fact: The latest Channel 13 poll, published October 7, gives Netanyahu's bloc 55 of 120 seats, the Eisenkot-led Zionist opposition bloc 50 and the Arab parties about 15. Neither side reaches the 61 seats needed for a majority without the Arab parties.

The October 5 Channel 12 poll had Eisenkot's bloc at 54 seats, unchanged from the previous poll, and Netanyahu's bloc at 49. Ofer Winter's far-right People of Israel party again fell below the threshold, which is counted against Netanyahu's bloc. A poll-aggregator listing for October 5 shows Yashar 23 and Likud 21.

The Maariv/Lazar poll of October 2 projected Netanyahu's bloc at 51 seats, the opposition at 53 and the Arab parties at 12. It put Likud at 19, Otzma Yehudit at 9, Eisenkot's Yashar at 21 and Bennett's Together at 13.

The Jerusalem Post averaged five late-September polls (Channel 14, i24NEWS, Maariv, N12 and Channel 13). The averages were coalition bloc 54.6 seats, Zionist opposition 50.6 and Arab parties 12.4, with Likud at 23 and Yashar at 22.2. Individual polls varied widely: the coalition ranged from 49 seats (Maariv) to 63 for the right-wing bloc (Channel 14), and Likud ranged from 18 to 32.

A Times of Israel poll had Netanyahu's bloc at 51 seats and the opposition at a combined 55, after Winter's People of Israel party fell below the 3.25% threshold. Bloc totals in many polls depend on whether People of Israel and the Hendel–Zelekha Reservists/New Economic list cross the threshold.

Because the opposition refuses to rely on the Arab parties, a Channel 13 poll on September 30 put Netanyahu's bloc at 54 seats, two more than the opposition's Jewish parties. Yashar was the largest party at 21 seats and Likud had 19.

Eisenkot has said Yashar would work with junior partners such as RZP or Likud if Netanyahu is no longer prime minister. Benny Gantz has ruled out supporting a Netanyahu-led government and is pursuing a 'third bloc' that favors a unity government. Ra'am presents itself as a pragmatic partner seeking to replace the Netanyahu government, and five opposition leaders signed a pledge not to attack each other.

Eisenkot has said he would make no deals with the Arab parties. Netanyahu's campaign slogan is 'Eisenkot has no government without the Arab parties.' Gantz's Blue and White polled below the threshold, at 0.7% in one late-September Channel 12 poll.

Lists running include Together (Bennett 2026 plus Yesh Atid, headed by Bennett), the Joint List (Hadash, Ta'al and Balad), and Ra'am separately. Unity dropped out on September 4, and Hili Tropper joined Yashar. Surplus-vote pairings are Together with Yisrael Beiteinu, Yashar with the Democrats, the Joint List with Ra'am, and Likud with RZP–Zehut.

The election is on October 27, 2026, with diaspora voting on October 20. Surplus-vote agreements are due October 16, and official results are due to be confirmed on November 4. The 25th Knesset dissolved on July 17, 2026, after serving its full term.

The question resolves to the first person formally sworn in as prime minister after the 2026 election. A caretaker or interim prime minister does not count, so Netanyahu staying on as caretaker during a deadlock would not count. If nobody is sworn in by December 31, 2027, it resolves 'Other'. The forming government needs Knesset confidence, which in practice means 61 of 120 seats or abstentions.

In November 2022, final pre-election polls put Netanyahu's bloc at about 59–60 seats and exit polls at 61–62, but the official count gave it 64. Part of the gap came from about 290,000 votes for Meretz and Balad that were wasted when both fell below the threshold, and from higher turnout in right-leaning cities.

Unverified, from memory: of the 5 elections from April 2019 to November 2022, 2 (April and September 2019) produced no government and led to repeat elections. After March 2020 Netanyahu was sworn in on May 17, 2020; after March 2021 Bennett was sworn in on June 13, 2021; and after November 2022 Netanyahu was sworn in on December 29, 2022.

Republicans have not won a U.S. Senate race in Michigan since 1994. Democrats won every Michigan Senate race from 1996 through 2024.

recent_facts.fact: The latest BLS release, for August 2026, shows the seasonally adjusted index for all items less food and energy rose 0.3% in August. It was up 2.4% over 12 months (not seasonally adjusted), down from 2.5% in July. The 12-month figure is the lowest since March 2021.
Monthly seasonally adjusted core CPI changes in 2026 were: Feb 0.2%, Mar 0.2%, Apr 0.4%, May 0.2%, Jun 0.0%, Jul 0.2%, Aug 0.3%. Only 1 of these 7 months (June) was at or below 0.1%.

August 2026 core details: shelter rose 0.3% after two straight 0.1% gains and was up 3.0% year over year. Used cars rose 0.4% (a second straight gain), new vehicles 0.3%, airline fares 2.7% (after 2.2% in July) and transportation services 0.5%. Apparel was flat and medical care commodities fell 0.2%.

market.question: 2026 Balance of Power: R Senate, R House
market.rules:
This market will resolve according to the party that wins control of the United States Senate and the party that wins control of the United States House of Representatives in the 2026 United States midterm election.

A party wins control of the United States Senate if it wins a majority of the chamber’s voting seats. If no party wins a majority of voting seats, the party that wins control of the chamber is the party that wins half of the voting seats and holds the Vice Presidency. If the outcome remains ambiguous after applying the above criteria, the chamber will be deemed controlled by the party with which the first selected President Pro Tempore of the Congress that convenes after the specified election is affiliated.

A party wins control of the United States House of Representatives if it wins a majority of the chamber’s voting seats. If no party wins a majority of voting seats, the chamber will be deemed controlled by the party with which the first elected Speaker of the House of the Congress that convenes after the 2026 midterm election is affiliated.

The following rules govern the counting of seats for determining which party wins control of the chambers.

For determining Senate control, all regular and special Senate elections that determine representation in the upcoming 120th Congress and are scheduled to take place in November 2026 as of October 31, 2026 are included. Vacant Senate seats for which no election or special election to fill the seat is scheduled to take place in November 2026 as of October 31, 2026 will be treated as held by the party affiliation of the most recent member to hold that seat. For determining House control, all House elections in the 2026 United States midterm election that elect voting members and determine representation in the upcoming 120th Congress are included. Where a Senate or House seat is decided by a runoff, the runoff result will determine attribution of that seat, even if it takes place after November 2026.

For seats contested in the specified election, seats are attributed to the party under which the member was elected. If a member-elect changes party affiliation, or vacates their seat, between election day and the formal organization of Congress, the seat is attributed to the party under which the member was elected. 

For seats not contested in the specified election, seats are attributed to the party that holds the seat as of the date of the election. If a current sitting member of the U.S. Senate who is not up for election changes party affiliation or vacates their seat after the date of the election, the seat is attributed to the party under which the member was affiliated at the time of the election.

Senate and House members elected as independents who formally caucus with, or, for newly elected members, who announce their intent to caucus with, a party are included in that party’s count. If the caucus decisions of members of the Senate or House elected as independents cannot be determined on the date of the election, this market may remain open until the earlier of (i) an announcement from the relevant members of their intents to caucus, or (ii) January 4th, 11:59 PM ET of the following calendar year. If no such announcement is made by January 4th, 11:59 PM ET of the following calendar year, the member will not count towards the seat count of any party.

The resolution sources for this market will be official information from relevant state electoral authorities, the United States Congress, and a consensus of credible reporting.

recent_facts.fact: After Cook's September 2026 update, 17 Republican-held seats and 5 Democratic-held seats are rated Toss Up, 22 in all. Axios notes Republicans would need to win most of the Toss Ups to keep the House.
Cook's September 25, 2026 changes moved AZ-01 and NJ-07 from Toss Up to Lean D, and moved FL-22, NC-11 and TX-15 from Lean R to Toss Up. Its ratings page lists 22 Toss Up races.

FiftyPlusOne's weighted generic ballot average has Democrats at 51.2% and Republicans at 43.4%, about D+8. US Polling Data has D+7.4 (49.3% to 41.9%). An older Decision Desk HQ average had D+6 and said Democrats have led by 5 to 7 points since April.

The current House has 218 Republicans, 214 Democrats and 1 independent, Kevin Kiley (CA-3), who left the GOP but stays in the House Republican Conference. Two seats are vacant (TX-23 Gonzales R, FL Cherfilus-McCormick D). A majority is 218 of 435, so Democrats need a net gain of about 3 seats.

recent_facts.source: Sabato's Crystal Ball / redistricting trackers (Wikipedia, US News)
recent_facts.fact: After mid-decade redistricting in about 10 states, Sabato's Crystal Ball puts the expected net Republican gain from new maps at R+6, with a range of R+5 to R+9. Estimates by state: Texas about R+5 (upheld by SCOTUS 6-3 on April 27), California about D+5 (Prop 50 map, appeal denied), Florida about R+4, Ohio about R+1 to 2, Louisiana about R+1, Utah court map D+1. Virginia's map was struck down, so 0.

On September 25 the U.S. Supreme Court ruled that Missouri's 2022 map governs the 2026 election. The 2025 GOP map, which would have added about 1 Republican seat, goes to voters as Proposition A on November 3. Reports conflict on Missouri's status.

The president's party lost House seats in 18 of the 20 midterms from 1946 to 2022. The exceptions were 1998 (D +5) and 2002 (R +8). Losses ranged from 4 seats (1962) to 63 (2010), and losses above 40 seats happened 7 times.
On July 30, Crystal Ball moved 13 to 14 House races toward Democrats. Before that update it rated 213 seats Safe, Likely or Lean R, 207 Safe, Likely or Lean D, and 15 Toss Ups.

market.rules:
This market will resolve according to the winner of the 2026 midterm Texas U.S. Senate election, inclusive of any run-offs.

A candidate shall be considered to represent a party in the event that he or she is the nominee of the party in question. Candidates other than the Democratic or Republican nominee (e.g., Greens, Libertarian, independent) may be added at a later date.

Candidates who run as independents will not be encompassed by the “Democrat” or “Republican” options regardless of any affiliation they may have with the party.

The candidates may be named in the contract for the convenience of traders. In the event that any named candidate is replaced as the nominee of their respective party prior to election day, the name in the contract will be updated and the market will resolve based on the replacement nominee of the party.

The resolution source for this market is the Associated Press, Fox News, and NBC. This market will resolve once all three sources call the race for the same candidate. If all three sources haven’t called the race in this state for the same candidate, this market will resolve based on the official certification.

recent_facts.fact: In the Fox News poll (Beacon/Shaw, Sept. 24–28, 881 likely voters, MOE ±3), Democrat James Talarico had 51% and Republican Ken Paxton 49%. Talarico's favorability was 52/44 (net +8) and Paxton's 40/58 (net −18). 53% worry Talarico is too liberal, and 51% say Paxton is too close to Trump.
The Pollsmax average of 40 polls had Talarico at 48.4% and Paxton at 44.7%, a 3.7-point lead. Its latest entry was a YouGov poll of 3,625 likely voters with Talarico ahead 50–44.

recent_facts.source: The Hill / Fox News (via search summary)
recent_facts.fact: A NYT/Siena poll had Talarico leading 51–45, according to a search summary that gave no field date. The Decision Desk HQ polling average had Talarico ahead by 3 points.

Mason-Dixon (Sept. 8–10, 625 likely voters, ±4) had Talarico 46%, Paxton 43% and 8% undecided. In the same poll, Republican Gov. Abbott led Democrat Hinojosa 48–41. Among Latino likely voters, Talarico led 54–36.

recent_facts.source: The Hill / Texas Public Opinion Research
recent_facts.fact: Texas Public Opinion Research's late-September poll had Talarico at 49%, Paxton at 44% and 3% undecided. The group's previous monthly poll had Talarico ahead 48–42. Newsweek separately reported an Emerson poll with Paxton up 1.

The Senate Leadership Fund is raising its pro-Paxton ad buy to $100 million, after spending nearly $70 million. In September, its affiliate Texas PAC spent nearly $66 million against Talarico's roughly $22 million, and Republican groups' total for the month was about $103 million. The DSCC and Senate Majority PAC had committed no Texas ad money. Talarico had led in every public poll that month.

MAGA Inc. spent $10 million, $5 million on ads supporting Paxton and $5 million on ads attacking Talarico. The Cook Political Report moved the race from Lean Republican to Toss Up on Aug. 20, and that rating was still in place on Sept. 6.

Talarico left the campaign trail with the flu, and his campaign said he would return this weekend. Paxton ran attack ads about his absence and led a 'Where is Talarico?' chant at Trump's San Antonio rally. Axios separately obtained leaked audio of Paxton at a closed-door D.C. fundraiser.
Paxton beat Sen. John Cornyn in the GOP runoff, about 62% to 37%, after Trump endorsed him. AP called the race shortly after 8 p.m. Cornyn said he would support Paxton in the general election.
Talarico is set to appear at a CNN/Jubilee town hall in Texas on Oct. 14. Early voting starts Oct. 19, and Election Day is Nov. 3, 2026. Texas has no runoff in the general election; a plurality wins.

recent_facts.source: Wikipedia (2024 U.S. Senate election in Texas)
recent_facts.fact: In 2024, final polls showed Ted Cruz (R) ahead of Colin Allred (D) by about 3–5 points, for example Marist 51–46 and Emerson 48.3–46.8. Cruz won 53.05% to 44.56%, an 8.5-point margin, beating his polls by about 4 points.

In 2018, Cruz beat Beto O'Rourke 50.9% to 48.3%, a 2.6-point margin. The 270toWin average of Oct.–Nov. polls was Cruz 50.4%, O'Rourke 44.2% (Cruz +6.2), so O'Rourke beat his polling margin by about 3.6 points.

Unverified: Democrats have not won a U.S. Senate race in Texas since Lloyd Bentsen in 1988, and Republicans have won every Texas Senate race since. One search summary said the seat has been Republican since 1961, but that conflicts with Bentsen's tenure.

market.question: Will the Democratic Party control the Senate after the 2026 Midterm elections?
market.rules:
This market will resolve according to the party that wins control of the United States Senate in the 2026 United States midterm election.

A party wins control of the United States Senate if it wins a majority of the chamber’s voting seats. If no party wins a majority of voting seats, the party that wins control of the chamber is the party that wins half of the voting seats and holds the Vice Presidency. If the outcome remains ambiguous after applying the above criteria, the chamber will be deemed controlled by the party with which the first selected President Pro Tempore of the Congress that convenes after the specified election is affiliated.

The following rules govern the counting of seats for determining which party wins control of the chamber.

All regular and special Senate elections that determine representation in the upcoming 120th Congress and are scheduled to take place in November 2026 as of October 31, 2026 are included. Runoffs for qualifying elections will determine attribution of the relevant seat, even if they take place after November 2026. Vacant seats for which no election or special election to fill the seat is scheduled to take place in November 2026 as of October 31, 2026 will be treated as held by the party affiliation of the most recent member to hold that seat.

For seats contested in the specified election, seats are attributed to the party under which the member was elected. If a member-elect changes party affiliation, or vacates their seat, between election day and the formal organization of Congress, the seat is attributed to the party under which the member was elected.

For seats not contested in the specified election, seats are attributed to the party that holds the seat as of the date of the election. If a current sitting member of the U.S. Senate who is not up for election changes party affiliation or vacates their seat after the date of the election, the seat is attributed to the party under which the member was affiliated at the time of the election.

Senate members elected as independents who formally caucus with, or, for newly elected members, who announce their intent to caucus with, a party are included in that party’s count. If the caucus decisions of members of the Senate elected as independents cannot be determined on the date of the election, this market may remain open until the earlier of (i) an announcement from the relevant members of their intents to caucus, or (ii) January 4th, 11:59 PM ET of the following calendar year. If no such announcement is made by January 4th, 11:59 PM ET of the following calendar year, the member will not count towards the seat count of any party.

The resolution sources for this market will be official information from relevant state electoral authorities, the United States Congress, and a consensus of credible reporting.

recent_facts.fact: Cook's Senate ratings, updated Oct 6, 2026, list 7 Toss Up races. Six are Republican-held: Alaska (Sullivan), Iowa (open), Kansas (Marshall), Maine (Collins), Ohio (Husted) and Texas (open). One is Democratic-held: Michigan (open). Cook's estimate of possible Democratic pickups is 2 to 6 seats, and Democrats need a net gain of 4 for a majority.

The Senate currently stands at 53 R and 47 D, counting the 2 independents who caucus with Democrats. The Vice President is Republican JD Vance, so Republicans keep control at 50-50. Democrats therefore need 51 seats, which means a net gain of 4.

On Oct 6, Cook moved three races toward Democrats: Kansas from Lean R to Toss Up, New Hampshire from Toss Up to Lean D, and North Carolina from Lean D to Likely D. In late September, Cook had moved Georgia from Lean D to Likely D.

Recent Texas polls show Democrat Talarico ahead of Republican Paxton: NYT/Siena 51-45, YouGov 50-44 and Fox News 51-49. Ohio: NYT/Siena has Democrat Sherrod Brown at 49 and Republican Husted at 46, with a margin of error of about ±4.5.

Maine: a Marist poll has Democrat Troy Jackson at 51 and Collins at 47, while recent CNN/SSRS and NYT/Siena polls showed no clear leader. Iowa: NYT/Siena has Republican Hinson at 48 and Democrat Turek at 47, and an earlier Suffolk poll had Turek ahead 48-44.

Alaska: NYT/Siena has Democrat Mary Peltola at 50 and Republican Sullivan at 43 among likely voters, and Alaska Survey Research has her ahead 51-49. North Carolina: YouGov/Catawba has Democrat Cooper at 47 and Republican Whatley at 35.

In September polls of the Democratic-held open Michigan seat, Democrat El-Sayed led Republican Rogers in Trafalgar (47-45), NYT/Siena (49-44) and Suffolk (47-40). One co/efficient poll showed a tie. A Fox News poll from August had Rogers ahead 51-47.

Kansas: a Global Strategy Group poll (a Democratic firm) has Democrat Adam Hamilton at 47 and Sen. Roger Marshall at 43, with Libertarian Graham at 5%. An Emerson College poll, date not given, had Hamilton ahead by 2, within the margin of error.

Georgia, Democratic-held: a YouGov poll from Sept 15–18 of 3,447 registered voters (margin of error ±2.7) has Sen. Ossoff at 51 and Republican Mike Collins at 41, with 6% undecided. An InsiderAdvantage poll from Aug 16–17 had Ossoff ahead 50-43.

Nebraska: an internal GBAO poll (Sept 3–8, 800 likely voters) has independent Dan Osborn at 47 and Sen. Pete Ricketts at 46. No independent public poll from the fall was found. Under the rules, an independent counts toward a party only if he caucuses with it or announces he will, and no reporting was found on which party Osborn would caucus with.
Forbes's race tracker, updated Oct 6, reports Democrats leading in the Maine and New Hampshire Senate races, with historically Republican Kansas now a toss-up.

Election Day is Nov 3, 2026, and the question closes Nov 4, 04:59 UTC. Runoffs, such as Georgia's if no candidate passes 50%, decide those seats even if they happen after November. If an independent winner's caucus choice is unclear, the market may stay open until Jan 4.
Since WWII, the president's party has lost an average of about 4 Senate seats in midterms. Across 22 midterms from 1934 to 2018, it gained Senate seats only 6 times.

A 2006 editorial counted 3 midterms since WWII in which the president's party lost the Senate: 1946, 1954 and 1986. This count is unverified and looks incomplete, since 1994 is not listed and 2006 came after the editorial. Adding those makes about 5 of the 20 midterms from 1946 to 2022.

market.question: Will Iliana Iotova win the next Bulgarian presidential election?
market.rules:
Presidential elections in Bulgaria are expected to be held in the Fall of 2026.

This market will resolve according to the listed candidate who wins the next presidential election in Bulgaria. 

This market includes any potential second round. If the result of this election isn't known by December 31, 2027, 11:59 PM ET, the market will resolve to "Other".

This market will resolve based on the result of the election, as indicated by a consensus of credible reporting. If there is ambiguity, this market will resolve based solely on the official results as reported by the Bulgarian government, specifically the Central Election Commission (Centralna izbiratelna komisia, CEC) (www.cik.bg/).

recent_facts.fact: Trend poll (fieldwork 26 Sep–2 Oct, n=1,003): Iotova–Valchev 47.8%, Gyurov–Kandev 24.6%, Kostadinov–Volgin (Vazrazhdane) 9.7%, Vassilev–Manov (MECh) 4.6%, Mihaylov 2.4%, Hristanov 1.9%. 38% of adults say they will definitely vote and 20% are undecided. Trend calls a runoff certain and saw no significant change over the past month.

Alpha Research poll (24 Sep–1 Oct, n=1,000): Iotova 44.5%, Gyurov 26.1%, Kostadinov 10.5% among firm voters. Expected turnout is about 37%. The pollster says a runoff is certain and very likely between the top two, and that 30% of firm voters could still change their choice.

Other late-Sept/early-Oct polls (excluding undecided voters): Myara (26 Sep–4 Oct) Iotova 46.9 vs Gyurov 25.3; Market Links (26–29 Sep) 51.6 vs 27.5; Sova Harris (23–28 Sep) 50.2 vs 23.7. Iotova leads by 18–27 points in all five polls listed. None of these sources reported a head-to-head runoff poll.
Counting undecided voters, Market Links had Iotova at 41.4% and Gyurov at 21.9%.

Iotova, the incumbent running as an independent, is backed by Progressive Bulgaria, BSP–United Left, ISBG and VMRO-BND. Gyurov is backed by PP–DB. GERB endorsed no one and fielded no candidate after Borisov, Donchev and Fandakova declined to run. DPS registered but nominated no pair.

In the Alpha Research poll, almost half of GERB-UDF and DPS supporters say they will not vote. Of GERB-UDF supporters who will vote, 20–25% pick Gyurov, about 10% Iotova and 5% Kostadinov. Most DPS supporters who will vote back Iotova. Alpha flagged coordinated GERB/DPS voting as a possible surprise.
The first round is on 25 October 2026. If needed, a runoff between the top two pairs is on 1 November 2026. The question closes 2026-10-26 at 03:59Z, which is before any runoff.
To win in the first round, a candidate needs more than 50% of valid votes and turnout of at least 50%. Otherwise the top two go to a runoff. The market counts any second round.
The CEC registered 27 presidential/vice-presidential pairs (20 initiative committees, 7 parties). This is the most candidates in any Bulgarian direct presidential election.

No candidate has ever won a Bulgarian presidential election in the first round. Incumbents running again (unverified recall): Stoyanov lost in 2001, Parvanov won in 2006, Radev won in 2021, so 2 of 3 won.
Iotova became president on 23 January 2026 when Rumen Radev resigned. Radev's Progressive Bulgaria then won the 19 April parliamentary election with 44.6%, and Radev became prime minister.

The October 5 Channel 12 poll had Eisenkot's bloc at 54 seats, unchanged from the previous poll, and Netanyahu's bloc at 49. Ofer Winter's far-right People of Israel party again fell below the threshold, which is counted against Netanyahu's bloc. A poll-aggregator listing for October 5 shows Yashar 23 and Likud 21.

The Maariv/Lazar poll of October 2 projected Netanyahu's bloc at 51 seats, the opposition at 53 and the Arab parties at 12. It put Likud at 19, Otzma Yehudit at 9, Eisenkot's Yashar at 21 and Bennett's Together at 13.

The Jerusalem Post averaged five late-September polls (Channel 14, i24NEWS, Maariv, N12 and Channel 13). The averages were coalition bloc 54.6 seats, Zionist opposition 50.6 and Arab parties 12.4, with Likud at 23 and Yashar at 22.2. Individual polls varied widely: the coalition ranged from 49 seats (Maariv) to 63 for the right-wing bloc (Channel 14), and Likud ranged from 18 to 32.

A Times of Israel poll had Netanyahu's bloc at 51 seats and the opposition at a combined 55, after Winter's People of Israel party fell below the 3.25% threshold. Bloc totals in many polls depend on whether People of Israel and the Hendel–Zelekha Reservists/New Economic list cross the threshold.

Because the opposition refuses to rely on the Arab parties, a Channel 13 poll on September 30 put Netanyahu's bloc at 54 seats, two more than the opposition's Jewish parties. Yashar was the largest party at 21 seats and Likud had 19.

Eisenkot has said Yashar would work with junior partners such as RZP or Likud if Netanyahu is no longer prime minister. Benny Gantz has ruled out supporting a Netanyahu-led government and is pursuing a 'third bloc' that favors a unity government. Ra'am presents itself as a pragmatic partner seeking to replace the Netanyahu government, and five opposition leaders signed a pledge not to attack each other.

Eisenkot has said he would make no deals with the Arab parties. Netanyahu's campaign slogan is 'Eisenkot has no government without the Arab parties.' Gantz's Blue and White polled below the threshold, at 0.7% in one late-September Channel 12 poll.

Lists running include Together (Bennett 2026 plus Yesh Atid, headed by Bennett), the Joint List (Hadash, Ta'al and Balad), and Ra'am separately. Unity dropped out on September 4, and Hili Tropper joined Yashar. Surplus-vote pairings are Together with Yisrael Beiteinu, Yashar with the Democrats, the Joint List with Ra'am, and Likud with RZP–Zehut.

The election is on October 27, 2026, with diaspora voting on October 20. Surplus-vote agreements are due October 16, and official results are due to be confirmed on November 4. The 25th Knesset dissolved on July 17, 2026, after serving its full term.

The forming government needs Knesset confidence, which in practice means 61 of 120 seats or abstentions.

In November 2022, final pre-election polls put Netanyahu's bloc at about 59–60 seats and exit polls at 61–62, but the official count gave it 64. Part of the gap came from about 290,000 votes for Meretz and Balad that were wasted when both fell below the threshold, and from higher turnout in right-leaning cities.

recent_facts.fact: In the 12 months to August 2026, the CPI-U all-items index rose 3.4% (not seasonally adjusted), the same rate as for the 12 months to July. The NSA index was 334.980 in August 2026, up 0.3% from July before seasonal adjustment. On a seasonally adjusted basis it rose 0.4%.

The September 2025 CPI-U NSA index was 324.800, and August 2025 was 323.976, so September 2025 rose about 0.25% NSA month over month. My own calculation: a published 12-month rate above 3.6% (3.7% or higher after rounding, i.e. at least 3.65%) needs a September 2026 index of about 336.66 or more. That is roughly a +0.50% NSA rise from August's 334.980. A rise of about +0.40% NSA (index about 336.33) would round to 3.6%.
BLS will release September 2026 CPI on Wednesday, October 14, 2026, at 8:30 a.m. ET.

AAA put the September 2026 national average gasoline price at $4.33/gal, a record for September and 50 cents above the previous September record of $3.83 (2023). The national average peaked at $4.48 on September 24 and was $4.41 by October 1.

Through August 20, AAA's August 2026 national average gasoline price was $4.06/gal. Daily readings were about $4.07 on August 13 and $4.09 on August 27. If the full August average was around $4.06–4.09, September's $4.33 would be roughly a 6–7% month-over-month rise in retail gasoline.

EIA's weekly U.S. regular gasoline price was $4.319 on September 14, $4.478 on September 21 and $4.465 on September 28, 2026. The September 28 price was about $1.35 higher than a year earlier. The September 2, 2026 hold was the Bank of Canada's seventh straight decision with no change. The policy rate has been 2.25% since the October 29, 2025 cut.

In a September 21 speech, Governor Tiff Macklem said a hike is possible if inflation proves persistent but made no commitment. He said the Bank doesn't want to restrain growth unnecessarily if inflation pressures are contained, nor wait too long if they become persistent.

TD noted that the 2-year Government of Canada yield had risen more than 40 bp over the previous month as markets moved toward rate hikes. TD said the August CPI report did not support that degree of tightening.
Real GDP was essentially unchanged in July 2026. June growth was revised up to 0.4% from 0.3%. Second-quarter growth had come in stronger than expected.
Canada lost 41,700 jobs in August 2026 and the unemployment rate held at 6.4%. U.S. Section 338 tariffs took effect August 22.

Senior Deputy Governor Carolyn Rogers said the policy rate is too blunt a tool for housing affordability. According to The Hub, the Bank so far sees little sign that higher gasoline prices are spreading across the wider consumer basket. Economists expect any tightening to be capped at about 50 bp.

The September Labour Force Survey is due this week. It will be the first full month of jobs data since the U.S. Section 338 tariffs took effect.
September 2026 CPI is scheduled for release on October 19, 2026. That is the last inflation report before the decision.

Clark won the 2026 U.S. Open at Shinnecock Hills on June 21 by one shot over Sam Burns, going wire to wire after starting the final round six ahead. Earlier in 2026 his world ranking had fallen as low as 75th.

market.question: Next US-Iran senior diplomatic meeting by October 31, 2026? (copy)
market.rules:
On September 22, U.S. Special Envoy Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner met Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi on the sidelines of the UN General Assembly in New York, with President Trump saying another meeting is scheduled in the near future.(see: https://www.israelhayom.com/2026/09/22/witkoff-kushner-attended-us-iran-meeting-another-expected-soon). 

This market will resolve to “Yes” if there is a direct or indirect senior-level diplomatic meeting between the United States and Iran by the listed date, 11:59 PM ET. Otherwise, this market will resolve to “No”.

A diplomatic meeting occurs when representatives of both listed countries who are acting in an official capacity and are authorized to engage in diplomacy on behalf of their respective governments or governing authorities deliberately meet for the purpose of diplomacy or negotiation. A qualifying meeting need not result in any agreement, joint statement, or further engagement.

A diplomatic meeting is senior-level if each listed entity is represented by a head of state, a head of government, or a vice president; a foreign minister; a minister of cabinet rank; the secretary or head of a national security council; the presiding officer of a national legislature; a special envoy; or another individual designated by the head of state or head of government to conduct diplomatic negotiations on their behalf. Individuals authorized only for technical, implementation, monitoring, staff-level, preparatory, or working-group-level talks will not be considered designated to conduct diplomatic negotiations on behalf of the head of state or head of government. This definition includes, but is not limited to, all of the following individuals: for the United States, Donald Trump, JD Vance, Marco Rubio, Scott Bessent, Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner; and for Iran, Mojtaba Khamenei, Masoud Pezeshkian, Abbas Araghchi and Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf. In each case, a qualifying representative must participate in the meeting.

A direct meeting refers to a diplomatic meeting where the representatives of both countries directly interact with each other in person. Meetings conducted through translators qualify, provided direct, face-to-face communication occurs. An indirect meeting refers to a meeting conducted indirectly through designated mediators or facilitators. A qualifying indirect meeting must meet both of the following criteria (i) the designated intermediaries act with the knowledge and authorization of both entities; (ii) representatives of both entities are physically present in the same facility, venue, or city as part of a single organized round of talks convened for the purpose of diplomatic engagement, with the intermediary conveying communications between the representatives or delegations on the same day. “The same day” means the same calendar day local time at the meeting location.

Sessions, proceedings, or convenings of standing international organizations, treaty bodies, or recurring multilateral summits or conferences (e.g., the United Nations General Assembly, G7, and G20 summits) do not qualify, unless a qualifying and deliberate diplomatic meeting between representatives of the listed countries is separately held alongside such a convening.

The following do not qualify as either a direct or indirect diplomatic meeting: chance encounters; standalone exchanges limited to greetings, courtesies, or photo opportunities; meetings conducted remotely, by telephone, or by any other means where the relevant representatives are not physically present at the same facility, venue, or city on the same day; discussions involving persons not authorized to engage in diplomacy or negotiation on behalf of their respective governments.

The resolution sources for this market will be official information from the governments of the United States and Iran and a consensus of credible reporting.

Prices will be used exactly as published by Pyth, without rounding.

Only prices achieved during an applicable trading session of the specified timeframe's business days will be considered (See: "Trading Hours" at https://www.ice.com/products/213/WTI-Crude-Futures). The trading session for a given business day typically begins at 8:00 PM ET on the prior calendar date, except for the session dated Monday, which begins at 6:00 PM ET on the preceding Sunday, and where modified by holiday or other special hours (See: https://www.ice.com/holiday-hours).

The Active Month is the nearest listed contract, except during that contract's final three trading sessions. At the open of the third-to-last trading session, the next listed contract becomes the Active Month.

Each contract's last trading day will be determined by ICE Futures Europe per the WTI Crude Futures contract specification (generally the 4th US business day prior to the 25th calendar day of the month preceding the contract month, or five US business days prior if the 25th calendar day is not a US business day). The last trading day for each contract is posted at https://www.ice.com/products/213/WTI-Crude-Futures/expiry.

If the relevant Pyth data is unavailable due to a system outage, data failure, or other disruption that prevents verification of the required 1-minute candle data, the official daily high/low price published for the Active Month WTI Crude Oil Futures contract by ICE Futures Europe may be used to determine whether the listed price was reached during the applicable trading session (See: https://www.ice.com/report/10 with "T-West Texas Intermediate Light Sweet Crude Future" selected).

In the event of a contract specification change, feed change, or similar structural modification affecting the underlying market during the listed time frame, this market will resolve based on adjusted prices as displayed on Pyth.

If the Active Month contract does not trade at all during the listed time frame, this market will resolve to "No".

market.question: Baycurrent Classic: Michael Thorbjornsen wins
market.rules:
If Michael Thorbjornsen wins the Baycurrent Classic, then the market resolves to Yes.
If a golfer forfeits, withdraws, or does not participate prior to teeing off, their contracts will resolve as follows:
Tournament Winner and End of Round Leader markets will resolve to No
Finishing Position, Make the Cut, Head-to-Head, and 3-Ball markets will resolve to Fair Market Value

recent_facts.fact: The 2026 Baycurrent Classic runs October 8-11, 2026 at Yokohama Country Club in Japan. The field is 72 players, the purse is $8 million, and it is the third of eight FedExCup Fall events. Schauffele is the defending champion, and Wyndham Clark is in the field.
The event has no cut for its 72 players. Under the market rules, a golfer who withdraws or does not tee off resolves No for Tournament Winner.
No player in the tournament's history (it was the Zozo Championship before the name change) has successfully defended the title. Schauffele is trying to be the first.
Schauffele is world No. 10 and has seven top-10 finishes in 2026. He won the event last year at 19-under, one shot ahead of Max Greyserman.

Schauffele has no win in 2026. He finished 14th in the FedExCup, with a 3rd at The Players Championship and a 2nd at the Rocket Classic. He shot 63 and 64 in rounds on the way to last year's Yokohama win.

Schauffele's recent form: T4 at the Tour Championship, with all four rounds in the 60s at East Lake. At the Presidents Cup he won the clinching point for the U.S. by beating Min Woo Lee in Sunday singles.
Wyndham Clark is world No. 5 and the highest-ranked player in the field. In 2026 he won the CJ Cup Byron Nelson, the U.S. Open and the BMW Championship.
Clark's three wins came in his last 11 starts. He went 1-4 at the 2026 Presidents Cup at Medinah, about two weeks before this event.
Clark's course history at Yokohama: T48 in 2025, and he did not break 70 until a closing 68.

Clark won the 2026 U.S. Open at Shinnecock Hills on June 21 by one shot over Sam Burns, going wire to wire after starting the final round six ahead. Earlier in 2026 his world ranking had fallen as low as 75th.

Other contenders in the field: past winner Collin Morikawa, Justin Thomas, Hideki Matsuyama, Jordan Spieth, Min Woo Lee, Adam Scott, Sungjae Im, Keegan Bradley, and Jacob Bridgeman, who has won twice in 2026, most recently at the Biltmore Championship Asheville.
13 players in the field played in the 2026 Presidents Cup, including Morikawa, Matsuyama and Thomas.
Tom Kim withdrew from the Baycurrent Classic after winning at the Asian Games. Search results showed no withdrawal by Schauffele or Clark.

Unverified, from memory: winners of the event from 2019 to 2025 were Woods, Cantlay, Matsuyama, Bradley, Morikawa, Echavarria and Schauffele. That is 7 different winners in 7 editions, and only 2020, played in California, was away from Japan.

market.question: Will Flávio Bolsonaro win the second round of the 2026 Brazilian presidential election by 8–12%?
market.rules:
The second round of the presidential election is scheduled to take place in Brazil on October 25, 2026.

This market will resolve according to the margin of victory between the top two candidates in the second round of the next Brazil Presidential Election.

For the purpose of this market, the “margin of victory” is defined as the absolute difference between the percentages of valid votes received by the first- and second-place candidates. Percentages of the valid votes received by each candidate will be determined by dividing the total number of valid votes each of the top two candidates receives by the sum of all valid votes cast in the election.

If the reported value falls exactly between two brackets, then this market will resolve to the higher range bracket.

If a candidate other than Flávio Bolsonaro or Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva receives the most valid votes in the second round, or if the top two candidates receive exactly the same number of valid votes, this market will resolve to "Other".

This market will resolve based on the official vote count once the vote count has been made official.

If a recount is initiated before the vote total has been made official, the market will remain open until the recount is completed and the vote is made official.

If the result of this election isn't known definitively by June 30, 2027, 11:59 PM ET, the market will resolve to "Other".

This market will resolve based on the result of the election, as indicated by a consensus of credible reporting. If there is ambiguity, this market will resolve based solely on the official results as reported by the Brazilian government, specifically the Superior Electoral Court (Tribunal Superior Eleitoral, TSE) (e.g., https://dadosabertos.tse.jus.br/).

market.question: Will the Democrats win the Texas Senate race in 2026?
market.rules:
This market will resolve according to the winner of the 2026 midterm Texas U.S. Senate election, inclusive of any run-offs.

A candidate shall be considered to represent a party in the event that he or she is the nominee of the party in question. Candidates other than the Democratic or Republican nominee (e.g., Greens, Libertarian, independent) may be added at a later date.

Candidates who run as independents will not be encompassed by the “Democrat” or “Republican” options regardless of any affiliation they may have with the party.

The candidates may be named in the contract for the convenience of traders. In the event that any named candidate is replaced as the nominee of their respective party prior to election day, the name in the contract will be updated and the market will resolve based on the replacement nominee of the party.

The resolution source for this market is the Associated Press, Fox News, and NBC. This market will resolve once all three sources call the race for the same candidate. If all three sources haven’t called the race in this state for the same candidate, this market will resolve based on the official certification.

recent_facts.fact: In the Fox News poll (Beacon/Shaw, Sept. 24–28, 881 likely voters, MOE ±3), Democrat James Talarico had 51% and Republican Ken Paxton 49%. Talarico's favorability was 52/44 (net +8) and Paxton's 40/58 (net −18). 53% worry Talarico is too liberal, and 51% say Paxton is too close to Trump.
The Pollsmax average of 40 polls had Talarico at 48.4% and Paxton at 44.7%, a 3.7-point lead. Its latest entry was a YouGov poll of 3,625 likely voters with Talarico ahead 50–44.

recent_facts.source: The Hill / Fox News (via search summary)
recent_facts.fact: A NYT/Siena poll had Talarico leading 51–45, according to a search summary that gave no field date. The Decision Desk HQ polling average had Talarico ahead by 3 points.

Mason-Dixon (Sept. 8–10, 625 likely voters, ±4) had Talarico 46%, Paxton 43% and 8% undecided. In the same poll, Republican Gov. Abbott led Democrat Hinojosa 48–41. Among Latino likely voters, Talarico led 54–36.

recent_facts.source: The Hill / Texas Public Opinion Research
recent_facts.fact: Texas Public Opinion Research's late-September poll had Talarico at 49%, Paxton at 44% and 3% undecided. The group's previous monthly poll had Talarico ahead 48–42. Newsweek separately reported an Emerson poll with Paxton up 1.

The Senate Leadership Fund is raising its pro-Paxton ad buy to $100 million, after spending nearly $70 million. In September, its affiliate Texas PAC spent nearly $66 million against Talarico's roughly $22 million, and Republican groups' total for the month was about $103 million. The DSCC and Senate Majority PAC had committed no Texas ad money. Talarico had led in every public poll that month.

MAGA Inc. spent $10 million, $5 million on ads supporting Paxton and $5 million on ads attacking Talarico. The Cook Political Report moved the race from Lean Republican to Toss Up on Aug. 20, and that rating was still in place on Sept. 6.

Talarico left the campaign trail with the flu, and his campaign said he would return this weekend. Paxton ran attack ads about his absence and led a 'Where is Talarico?' chant at Trump's San Antonio rally. Axios separately obtained leaked audio of Paxton at a closed-door D.C. fundraiser.
Paxton beat Sen. John Cornyn in the GOP runoff, about 62% to 37%, after Trump endorsed him. AP called the race shortly after 8 p.m. Cornyn said he would support Paxton in the general election.
Talarico is set to appear at a CNN/Jubilee town hall in Texas on Oct. 14. Early voting starts Oct. 19, and Election Day is Nov. 3, 2026. Texas has no runoff in the general election; a plurality wins.

market.question: Will the Republicans win the Michigan Senate race in 2026?
market.rules:
This market will resolve according to the winner of the 2026 midterm Michigan U.S. Senate election, inclusive of any run-offs.

A candidate shall be considered to represent a party in the event that he or she is the nominee of the party in question. Candidates other than the Democratic or Republican nominee (e.g., Greens, Libertarian, independent) may be added at a later date.

Candidates who run as independents will not be encompassed by the “Democrat” or “Republican” options regardless of any affiliation they may have with the party.

The candidates may be named in the contract for the convenience of traders. In the event that any named candidate is replaced as the nominee of their respective party prior to election day, the name in the contract will be updated and the market will resolve based on the replacement nominee of the party.

The resolution source for this market is the Associated Press, Fox News, and NBC. This market will resolve once all three sources call the race for the same candidate. If all three sources haven’t called the race in this state for the same candidate, this market will resolve based on the official certification.

recent_facts.source: Wikipedia (2026 United States Senate election in Michigan)
recent_facts.fact: The nominees are Democrat Abdul El-Sayed and Republican Mike Rogers. Four minor-party nominees are also running: Lydia Christensen (Libertarian), Douglas P. Marsh (Green), Tim Long (U.S. Taxpayers) and Walter P. Kristy (Natural Law). No major independent is listed in the Senate race.
YouGov poll of 3,949 likely voters, Sept 22 to Oct 4, 2026: El-Sayed 49%, Rogers 48%, other 1%, undecided 2%.

Mitchell Research poll of 682 likely voters on Oct 1, 2026: El-Sayed 45.6%, Rogers 41.4%, each of the four minor-party candidates at 3% or less, undecided 6%, margin of error 3.8%. The pollster cautioned that in past Michigan Senate races Republicans gained support in the final weeks of the campaign.

recent_facts.source: Trafalgar Group, Beacon/Shaw and Marist via Wikipedia
recent_facts.fact: Trafalgar, Sept 28–30 (1,085 likely voters): El-Sayed 47%, Rogers 45%, undecided 5%. Beacon/Shaw, Sept 24–28: El-Sayed 50%, Rogers 49% among likely voters. Marist, Sept 24–27 (1,235 registered voters): El-Sayed 51%, Rogers 44%.

recent_facts.source: Cook Political Report / Sabato's Crystal Ball / Inside Elections via Wikipedia
recent_facts.fact: Race ratings as of October: Cook Political Report has it as a Tossup, Sabato's Crystal Ball as Lean D and Inside Elections as Tilt D.
The RealClearPolling average shows El-Sayed at 47.8% and Rogers at 43.8%, a gap of about 4 points.

Disclosed spending on the race is over $205 million. Since the start of 2025, Rogers and groups backing him have outspent El-Sayed and his allies by almost 2 to 1. For October, Republicans plan to spend more than $43 million, against about $25 million in Democratic reservations.
Rogers skipped a Tuesday-night debate, saying moderator Roop Raj favored El-Sayed. El-Sayed debated next to an empty podium and was questioned about Hasan Piker, Israel and socialist ties.
Rogers acknowledged that El-Sayed is 'doing a good job on campuses' and called this 'a little scary.' Republican ads describe El-Sayed as 'dangerous' and 'radical.'
A CNN headline from Oct 7 reads: 'Abdul El-Sayed is certain he'll win Michigan's Senate race. Some key Democrats quietly aren't so sure.' The article body could not be retrieved.

Mallory McMorrow, who left the primary in July, endorsed El-Sayed after the primary. Haley Stevens, the runner-up, said she would work to keep the seat Democratic. Gov. Whitmer had endorsed Stevens before the primary.

El-Sayed won the Aug 4 Democratic primary with 48.5%, narrowly beating Rep. Haley Stevens. Rogers was unopposed for the Republican nomination. As of July 15, El-Sayed had raised $14.5M and had $2.5M cash on hand; Rogers had raised $10.9M and had $4.5M on hand.
Rogers and El-Sayed are scheduled to meet in a televised debate on Oct 8, 2026. Election day is Nov 3, 2026.
In 2024, Slotkin (D) beat Rogers 48.6% to 48.3% (D+0.3). She had led by about 5 points for much of the race, and final polls on Nov 3–4 showed her ahead by 1 point (49–48).
Republicans have not won a U.S. Senate race in Michigan since 1994. Democrats won every Michigan Senate race from 1996 through 2024.

market.question: Will the Republican Party control the Senate after the 2026 Midterm elections?
market.rules:
This market will resolve according to the party that wins control of the United States Senate in the 2026 United States midterm election.

A party wins control of the United States Senate if it wins a majority of the chamber’s voting seats. If no party wins a majority of voting seats, the party that wins control of the chamber is the party that wins half of the voting seats and holds the Vice Presidency. If the outcome remains ambiguous after applying the above criteria, the chamber will be deemed controlled by the party with which the first selected President Pro Tempore of the Congress that convenes after the specified election is affiliated.

The following rules govern the counting of seats for determining which party wins control of the chamber.

All regular and special Senate elections that determine representation in the upcoming 120th Congress and are scheduled to take place in November 2026 as of October 31, 2026 are included. Runoffs for qualifying elections will determine attribution of the relevant seat, even if they take place after November 2026. Vacant seats for which no election or special election to fill the seat is scheduled to take place in November 2026 as of October 31, 2026 will be treated as held by the party affiliation of the most recent member to hold that seat.

For seats contested in the specified election, seats are attributed to the party under which the member was elected. If a member-elect changes party affiliation, or vacates their seat, between election day and the formal organization of Congress, the seat is attributed to the party under which the member was elected.

For seats not contested in the specified election, seats are attributed to the party that holds the seat as of the date of the election. If a current sitting member of the U.S. Senate who is not up for election changes party affiliation or vacates their seat after the date of the election, the seat is attributed to the party under which the member was affiliated at the time of the election.

Senate members elected as independents who formally caucus with, or, for newly elected members, who announce their intent to caucus with, a party are included in that party’s count. If the caucus decisions of members of the Senate elected as independents cannot be determined on the date of the election, this market may remain open until the earlier of (i) an announcement from the relevant members of their intents to caucus, or (ii) January 4th, 11:59 PM ET of the following calendar year. If no such announcement is made by January 4th, 11:59 PM ET of the following calendar year, the member will not count towards the seat count of any party.

The resolution sources for this market will be official information from relevant state electoral authorities, the United States Congress, and a consensus of credible reporting.

recent_facts.fact: Cook's Senate ratings, updated Oct 6, 2026, list 7 Toss Up races. Six are Republican-held: Alaska (Sullivan), Iowa (open), Kansas (Marshall), Maine (Collins), Ohio (Husted) and Texas (open). One is Democratic-held: Michigan (open). Cook's estimate of possible Democratic pickups is 2 to 6 seats, and Democrats need a net gain of 4 for a majority.

The Senate currently stands at 53 R and 47 D, counting the 2 independents who caucus with Democrats. The Vice President is Republican JD Vance, so Republicans keep control at 50-50. Democrats therefore need 51 seats, which means a net gain of 4.

On Oct 6, Cook moved three races toward Democrats: Kansas from Lean R to Toss Up, New Hampshire from Toss Up to Lean D, and North Carolina from Lean D to Likely D. In late September, Cook had moved Georgia from Lean D to Likely D.

Recent Texas polls show Democrat Talarico ahead of Republican Paxton: NYT/Siena 51-45, YouGov 50-44 and Fox News 51-49. Ohio: NYT/Siena has Democrat Sherrod Brown at 49 and Republican Husted at 46, with a margin of error of about ±4.5.

Maine: a Marist poll has Democrat Troy Jackson at 51 and Collins at 47, while recent CNN/SSRS and NYT/Siena polls showed no clear leader. Iowa: NYT/Siena has Republican Hinson at 48 and Democrat Turek at 47, and an earlier Suffolk poll had Turek ahead 48-44.

Alaska: NYT/Siena has Democrat Mary Peltola at 50 and Republican Sullivan at 43 among likely voters, and Alaska Survey Research has her ahead 51-49. North Carolina: YouGov/Catawba has Democrat Cooper at 47 and Republican Whatley at 35.

In September polls of the Democratic-held open Michigan seat, Democrat El-Sayed led Republican Rogers in Trafalgar (47-45), NYT/Siena (49-44) and Suffolk (47-40). One co/efficient poll showed a tie. A Fox News poll from August had Rogers ahead 51-47.

Kansas: a Global Strategy Group poll (a Democratic firm) has Democrat Adam Hamilton at 47 and Sen. Roger Marshall at 43, with Libertarian Graham at 5%. An Emerson College poll, date not given, had Hamilton ahead by 2, within the margin of error.

Georgia, Democratic-held: a YouGov poll from Sept 15–18 of 3,447 registered voters (margin of error ±2.7) has Sen. Ossoff at 51 and Republican Mike Collins at 41, with 6% undecided. An InsiderAdvantage poll from Aug 16–17 had Ossoff ahead 50-43.

Nebraska: an internal GBAO poll (Sept 3–8, 800 likely voters) has independent Dan Osborn at 47 and Sen. Pete Ricketts at 46. No independent public poll from the fall was found. Under the rules, an independent counts toward a party only if he caucuses with it or announces he will, and no reporting was found on which party Osborn would caucus with.
Forbes's race tracker, updated Oct 6, reports Democrats leading in the Maine and New Hampshire Senate races, with historically Republican Kansas now a toss-up.

Election Day is Nov 3, 2026, and the question closes Nov 4, 04:59 UTC. Runoffs, such as Georgia's if no candidate passes 50%, decide those seats even if they happen after November. If an independent winner's caucus choice is unclear, the market may stay open until Jan 4.
Since WWII, the president's party has lost an average of about 4 Senate seats in midterms. Across 22 midterms from 1934 to 2018, it gained Senate seats only 6 times.

A 2006 editorial counted 3 midterms since WWII in which the president's party lost the Senate: 1946, 1954 and 1986. This count is unverified and looks incomplete, since 1994 is not listed and 2006 came after the editorial. Adding those makes about 5 of the 20 midterms from 1946 to 2022.

This market will resolve to "Yes" if Jynxzi, StableRonaldo, and Los Pollos defeat the Ender Dragon live on stream, as accepted by them as a successful completion of their challenge, between market creation and the specified date, 11:59 PM ET. Otherwise, this market will resolve to "No".

Only events occurring while at least one of the three players is broadcasting the challenge live will count. Footage of off-stream or previously recorded attempts will not qualify.

If the challenge is cancelled, abandoned before completion, or delayed to a point after the specified date, this market will resolve to "No".

The resolution source for this market will be footage from the official broadcasts of the challenge on Jynxzi's, StableRonaldo's, and Los Pollos's official broadcasts on YouTube and Twitch.

recent_facts.source: Web search of news, social posts and Twitch (research desk)
recent_facts.fact: As of October 8, 2026, no news outlet, clip or social post found reports that Jynxzi, StableRonaldo and Los Pollos have defeated the Ender Dragon in this run. The Twitch page fetched today did not show a current stream title or day number.

recent_facts.source: Twitch (Jynxzi channel listing, via search snippet)
recent_facts.fact: A search snippet of Jynxzi's Twitch channel showed the stream titled "PLAYING HARDCORE MINECRAFT UNTIL WE BEAT IT W/ LOS & RON DAY 3" with about 3,695 viewers. This means the marathon was still going on day 3 (around October 7). The snippet's exact capture date is unverified.

Undated fan clips say the group "finally make it to the nether after 24 hours and Ron dies immediately", and that Los died 10 seconds into a run. These clips suggest frequent resets early in the marathon, but their exact dates are unverified.
StableRonaldo posted: "Tomorrow I will be playing HardCore Minecraft with @jynxzi and @LosPollosTV until we beat it." This confirms the October 5 start date.

In August, Jynxzi listed his marathon rules as no totems, no Iron Golems, no enchantments, no coach and no XP farms. That August plan with Ron was to beat four bosses in one run with no 10-day clause. The question itself only requires killing the Ender Dragon.
Los Pollos pushed back on the rules, saying: "You wanna have a 10-day marathon." This suggests a run of up to around 10 days was being discussed.
Jynxzi and Ron's earlier hardcore Minecraft marathon (May–June 2026, without Los) succeeded, but it took 78 attempts because they reset after every death.

In a comparable marathon, Kai Cenat and IShowSpeed finished hardcore Minecraft on day 5, after more than 105 hours (some reports say about 120) and 42 deaths. They also got speedrunner help on enchantments, which this trio's rules ban.
StableRonaldo and FaZe Lacy previously beat hardcore Minecraft by defeating the Ender Dragon in under six hours, so Ron has completed hardcore Minecraft at least twice.

market.question: 2026 Balance of Power: R Senate, D House
market.rules:
This market will resolve according to the party that wins control of the United States Senate and the party that wins control of the United States House of Representatives in the 2026 United States midterm election.

A party wins control of the United States Senate if it wins a majority of the chamber’s voting seats. If no party wins a majority of voting seats, the party that wins control of the chamber is the party that wins half of the voting seats and holds the Vice Presidency. If the outcome remains ambiguous after applying the above criteria, the chamber will be deemed controlled by the party with which the first selected President Pro Tempore of the Congress that convenes after the specified election is affiliated.

A party wins control of the United States House of Representatives if it wins a majority of the chamber’s voting seats. If no party wins a majority of voting seats, the chamber will be deemed controlled by the party with which the first elected Speaker of the House of the Congress that convenes after the 2026 midterm election is affiliated.

The following rules govern the counting of seats for determining which party wins control of the chambers.

For determining Senate control, all regular and special Senate elections that determine representation in the upcoming 120th Congress and are scheduled to take place in November 2026 as of October 31, 2026 are included. Vacant Senate seats for which no election or special election to fill the seat is scheduled to take place in November 2026 as of October 31, 2026 will be treated as held by the party affiliation of the most recent member to hold that seat. For determining House control, all House elections in the 2026 United States midterm election that elect voting members and determine representation in the upcoming 120th Congress are included. Where a Senate or House seat is decided by a runoff, the runoff result will determine attribution of that seat, even if it takes place after November 2026.

For seats contested in the specified election, seats are attributed to the party under which the member was elected. If a member-elect changes party affiliation, or vacates their seat, between election day and the formal organization of Congress, the seat is attributed to the party under which the member was elected. 

For seats not contested in the specified election, seats are attributed to the party that holds the seat as of the date of the election. If a current sitting member of the U.S. Senate who is not up for election changes party affiliation or vacates their seat after the date of the election, the seat is attributed to the party under which the member was affiliated at the time of the election.

Senate and House members elected as independents who formally caucus with, or, for newly elected members, who announce their intent to caucus with, a party are included in that party’s count. If the caucus decisions of members of the Senate or House elected as independents cannot be determined on the date of the election, this market may remain open until the earlier of (i) an announcement from the relevant members of their intents to caucus, or (ii) January 4th, 11:59 PM ET of the following calendar year. If no such announcement is made by January 4th, 11:59 PM ET of the following calendar year, the member will not count towards the seat count of any party.

The resolution sources for this market will be official information from relevant state electoral authorities, the United States Congress, and a consensus of credible reporting.

On September 30, 2026, FlyDubai flight FZ1073 from Dubai to Tel Aviv diverted to Saudi Arabia following an incident in the cockpit in which the co-pilot allegedly stabbed the captain. (see: https://www.reuters.com/world/middle-east/diverted-flydubai-flight-israel-was-not-hijacking-incident-israeli-prime-2026-09-30/).

This market will resolve to "Yes" if the Israeli national government, or an authorized representative of the Israeli national government, publicly announces that Iran or its affiliated groups deliberately caused this incident, by October 31, 2026, 11:59 PM ET. Otherwise, this market will resolve to "No".

A public announcement refers to an on-the-record statement issued by the Israeli national government or by its authorized representatives acting in an official capacity on behalf of the Israeli national government. A statement or press release issued by the Israeli national government or any of its agencies will qualify. A Prime Minister or Cabinet Minister’s public statements will always be considered to be issued on-the-record in a capacity representing the Israeli national government for purposes of this market. A statement from a lawmaker or other government official speaking in their own capacity or on behalf of a party not in government will not alone qualify.

For purposes of this market, an affiliated group of Iran is: any organization directly controlled by Iran, Hezbollah, Hamas, Palestinian Islamic Jihad, Houthis ("Ansar Allah"), Kata'ib Hezbollah, Asa'ib Ahl al-Haq, Badr Organization, and Harakat al-Nujaba. An unlisted group will only qualify if the Israeli claim itself, or accompanying statements or releases, specifies that the group is a proxy of or otherwise is controlled or directed by Iran. Such a statement will be considered to claim that Iran or its affiliated groups deliberately caused the incident if it explicitly claims that Iran or an affiliated group ordered, carried out, planned, or otherwise directly aided or coordinated the incident. Statements that attribute only inspiration or ideological influence (e.g., "this would not have happened if Iran didn't radicalize terrorists," "the co-pilot was influenced by Hamas' ideas") will not qualify.

The Mossad is in direct contact with its UAE and Saudi counterparts. Israel says it is still building a final profile of Hammami to decide whether he was a lone wolf, belonged to an organization, or was sent directly by Iran. Information passed to Israel so far has not settled this.

Asked about Iranian involvement, PM Netanyahu said it was 'too early to say' and added: 'We'll get to the root of this attacker, whether he had accomplices, whether Iran was behind it. I think we'll find out very soon.'

Netanyahu said the attacker 'underwent Islamist radicalization' and that investigators were 'examining whether he was sent, and whoever sent him will pay a very heavy price.' Two Israeli officials told Reuters that no evidence of Iranian involvement had been found so far and that the attacker appeared to have acted independently.

According to The Wall Street Journal, Omani authorities had earlier grounded the co-pilot over concerns that he had become radicalized. It is unclear whether Oman shared those concerns with other governments or airlines.

US President Trump said of possible Iranian involvement: 'I would say the answer, based on what I'm hearing, is yes, but we're working on it right now.' He later said 'I do. market.rules:
This market will resolve to "Yes" if, at any point after market creation and during a trading session of October 2026, any Pyth 1-minute candle for the Active Month of ICE Futures Europe WTI Crude Futures (denoted by Pyth as "CLL") has a final "High" or "Low" price equal to or beyond (above for ↑ High Prices, below for ↓ Low Prices) the listed price. Otherwise, this market will resolve to "No".

Prices will be used exactly as published by Pyth, without rounding.

Only prices achieved during an applicable trading session of the specified timeframe's business days will be considered (See: "Trading Hours" at https://www.ice.com/products/213/WTI-Crude-Futures). The trading session for a given business day typically begins at 8:00 PM ET on the prior calendar date, except for the session dated Monday, which begins at 6:00 PM ET on the preceding Sunday, and where modified by holiday or other special hours (See: https://www.ice.com/holiday-hours).

The Active Month is the nearest listed contract, except during that contract's final three trading sessions. At the open of the third-to-last trading session, the next listed contract becomes the Active Month.

Each contract's last trading day will be determined by ICE Futures Europe per the WTI Crude Futures contract specification (generally the 4th US business day prior to the 25th calendar day of the month preceding the contract month, or five US business days prior if the 25th calendar day is not a US business day). The last trading day for each contract is posted at https://www.ice.com/products/213/WTI-Crude-Futures/expiry.

For example, if the last trading session for the nearest listed contract is the session for Monday the 20th, the next listed contract would become the Active Month at the start of the trading session for Thursday the 16th (8:00 PM ET on Wednesday), assuming a standard trading calendar.

If the relevant Pyth data is unavailable due to a system outage, data failure, or other disruption that prevents verification of the required 1-minute candle data, the official daily high/low price published for the Active Month WTI Crude Oil Futures contract by ICE Futures Europe may be used to determine whether the listed price was reached during the applicable trading session (See: https://www.ice.com/report/10 with "T-West Texas Intermediate Light Sweet Crude Future" selected).

In the event of a contract specification change, feed change, or similar structural modification affecting the underlying market during the listed time frame, this market will resolve based on adjusted prices as displayed on Pyth.

If the Active Month contract does not trade at all during the listed time frame, this market will resolve to "No".

The resolution source for this market is Pyth — specifically, the ICE Futures Europe WTI Crude Futures Active Month "High" and "Low" prices available at https://app.pyth.com/explore?search=CLL, with the chart settings configured for 1-minute candles. market.rules:
Jynxzi, StableRonaldo, and Los Pollos are scheduled to begin a hardcore Minecraft marathon on October 5, 2026. Their goal, as of market creation, is to defeat the Ender Dragon in a hardcore Minecraft world without any of the three dying.

This market will resolve to "Yes" if Jynxzi, StableRonaldo, and Los Pollos defeat the Ender Dragon live on stream, as accepted by them as a successful completion of their challenge, between market creation and the specified date, 11:59 PM ET. Otherwise, this market will resolve to "No".

Only events occurring while at least one of the three players is broadcasting the challenge live will count. Footage of off-stream or previously recorded attempts will not qualify.

If the challenge is cancelled, abandoned before completion, or delayed to a point after the specified date, this market will resolve to "No".

The resolution source for this market will be footage from the official broadcasts of the challenge on Jynxzi's, StableRonaldo's, and Los Pollos's official broadcasts on YouTube and Twitch.

market.question: Bitcoin price on Oct 9, 2026? ($83,000 or above)
market.rules:
If the simple average of the sixty seconds of CF Benchmarks' Bitcoin Real-Time Index (BRTI) before 5 PM EDT is above 82999.99 at 5 PM EDT on Oct 9, 2026, then the market resolves to Yes.
Not all cryptocurrency price data is the same. While checking a source like Google or Coinbase may help guide your decision, the price used to determine this market is based on CF Benchmarks' corresponding Real Time Index (RTI). At the last minute before expiration, 60 RTI prices are collected. The official and final value is the average of these prices.

recent_facts.fact: Strikes are $82,500 (BRTI average must be above 82,499.99) and $84,000 (above 83,999.99). The test uses the simple average of the 60 one-second BRTI prices before 5 PM EDT on Fri Oct 9, 2026 (21:00 UTC). It is a single settlement value, not an any-touch test. Slovenia's Primož Dolenc said persistently high inflation and unresolved conflicts support 'moving policy rates towards a more restrictive territory', but that 'when and by how much we will determine on a meeting-by-meeting basis'.

In early October, financial-market stress led markets to scale back expected ECB rate hikes. ECB chief economist Lane has argued that 'demand destruction' from energy costs and higher long-term rates could limit how far rates need to rise.

Greek central bank governor Stournaras said an October move cannot be ruled out if energy costs or inflation surge, but warned against acting hastily. Schnabel has recently said higher bond yields could dampen price pressures.
Eurostat releases the full September 2026 HICP data on 16 October 2026, before the 28–29 October meeting. The October flash estimate comes after the meeting.

The UNH Green Mountain State Poll (835 likely voters, online, Sept 17–21, 2026, margin of error ±3.4) has Janoo at 49% and Scott at 43%, with 6% undecided and 2% for another candidate. The pollsters called it a statistical tie.

Former Conservative MP Chris Alexander suspended his campaign on Oct 6, the day advance voting opened, and said he will not endorse anyone. Bradford's endorsers include MPs Yvan Baker, Leslie Church, James Maloney, Judy Sgro, Scott Aitchison and others, plus Lisa Raitt, Brad Duguid, Geddy Lee, Ben Mulroney and ABC Toronto. Chow's include 8 councillors, MPs such as Gary Anandasangaree, MPPs, CUPE Local 79, LiUNA 183, the Toronto and York Region Labour Council and Progress Toronto. There are 57 registered candidates; John Tory, Ana Bailão, Josh Matlow and Anthony Furey declined to run.
Premier Doug Ford said his praise for Olivia Chow was not an endorsement.
Advance voting opened Oct 6, 2026. Election day is Oct 26, 2026, and the mayor is decided by first-past-the-post plurality.
A TMU, United Way and Toronto Star mayoral debate moderated by Edward Keenan took place Oct 6, 2026. Candidates needed at least 5% in polling averages to be invited.

In the 2023 by-election Chow won with 37.2% to Bailão's 32.5%. Mainstreet's final poll had Chow 36 and Bailão 30 after a late surge driven by endorsements, while earlier June polls (Ipsos, Viewpoints) had Bailão near 12%. Late movement was large, but the poll leader still won.

If the seasonally adjusted Consumer Price Index for All Urban Consumers: All Items less Food and Energy for September 2026, as published by the Bureau of Labor Statistics, increases by above 0.3%, then the market resolves to Yes.
Please note that the value of the Underlying is the single-decimal value reported by the BLS.

In the case of a delay in data caused by a federal government shutdown impacting the reliability of the Source Agency, the market’s latest Expiration Date will be extended to the sooner of the release of the Underlying or six months after the end of the government shutdown.

recent_facts.fact: The latest BLS release, for August 2026, shows the seasonally adjusted index for all items less food and energy rose 0.3% in August. It was up 2.4% over 12 months (not seasonally adjusted), down from 2.5% in July. The 12-month figure is the lowest since March 2021.
Monthly seasonally adjusted core CPI changes in 2026 were: Feb 0.2%, Mar 0.2%, Apr 0.4%, May 0.2%, Jun 0.0%, Jul 0.2%, Aug 0.3%. Only 1 of these 7 months (June) was at or below 0.1%.

August 2026 core details: shelter rose 0.3% after two straight 0.1% gains and was up 3.0% year over year. Used cars rose 0.4% (a second straight gain), new vehicles 0.3%, airline fares 2.7% (after 2.2% in July) and transportation services 0.5%. Apparel was flat and medical care commodities fell 0.2%.

recent_facts.source: BLS CPI home page / Nowflation release calendar
recent_facts.fact: BLS is scheduled to release the September 2026 CPI on Wednesday, October 14, 2026, at 8:30 a.m. ET. That is the same day the question closes (12:25 UTC).

On September 2, 2026, Congress enacted a continuing resolution that funds federal agencies at FY2026 levels through December 11, 2026. This averted an October 1 shutdown, so the BLS release schedule should not be disrupted by a lapse in funding.
Headline CPI rose 0.4% in August 2026 and 3.4% year over year. Gasoline rose 3.9% and accounted for more than one-third of the monthly gain. Energy does not count toward the core index.

recent_facts.source: Türkiye Ministry of Trade (citing BLS July 2026 CPI)
recent_facts.fact: In July 2026, core CPI rose 0.2% while headline CPI rose 0.1%. This followed a 0.4% fall in headline CPI in June.

recent_facts.source: Research desk recollection of BLS releases (unverified)
recent_facts.fact: Unverified recollection: in 2025, monthly core CPI was at or below 0.1% in roughly 2 of the 9 regularly published months (March and May at 0.1%). September 2025 core was about 0.2%. October 2025 was not published because of the shutdown.
The question resolves on the single-decimal seasonally adjusted monthly change in core CPI that BLS reports. A printed 0.1% or lower resolves No, and 0.2% or higher resolves Yes.

After 5 Premier League games, Man City are 1st on 15 points (W5 D0 L0, goal difference +8). Liverpool are 6th on 9 points (W2 D3 L0, goal difference +3) and are unbeaten in the league under Iraola.
